inspiration: A self-sustaining raiding column crosses deep empty country to wreck an enemy's grounded air power before it can scramble, then must recross that same emptiness ahead of the survivors it failed to kill.
skeleton: a combined-arms raid column must wreck a deep-rear airfield's grounded wing inside the scramble window and clear the open ground before dawn, knowing every fighter it fails to kill becomes its pursuer on the way home
title: OPERATION LONG GALLOP
situation: {WORLD}, deep in {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. {TARGET_FACTION} owns the air over the front line because it owns the airfield that fuels and arms its fighters. That base sits {RAID_DISTANCE_KM} kilometers behind the line, far out in flat, empty desert. {EMPLOYER} wants that air power destroyed. You cannot beat these fighters in the air, where they are strongest, so the plan is to catch them on the ground and wreck them before they can take off. {NPC:intel-source} reports {GROUNDED_FIGHTERS} fighters parked in earth-walled bays, a fuel depot of rubber tanks, and an ammunition dump dug in at the north edge of the field. That report is 11 days old, so treat the fighter count as a rough figure, not an exact one. The base is built to watch the sky, not the ground. A search radar on a tower spots any aircraft coming down within 40 kilometers, but the desert approaches are guarded by just one roving patrol. The enemy does not believe a ground force could cross this much open country and still carry enough fuel to get home. That belief is your opening. The desert is both your worst problem and your best cover. It is {RAID_DISTANCE_KM} kilometers of hardpan and dune with no cover and no water. At night you can cross it freely. By day, once the enemy knows where you are, it becomes open killing ground with nowhere to hide. Your column carries all its own fuel. After the round trip you have only {COLUMN_FUEL_HOURS} hours of fuel to spare, and every hour you spend fighting comes straight out of that margin. Here is the trade. Every fighter you destroy on the ground is one that can never chase you home. But every extra minute you stay pushes you closer to the moment the rest of them scramble. {NPC:opfor-commander} runs the field and has never been hit here. Once the alarm sounds, his ready flight can be airborne in {SCRAMBLE_MINUTES} minutes, and he can recall a patrol lance that is out on a sweep. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}. Wreck the parked fighters before they scramble. Miss that window and the wing you came to kill will catch you in the open on the way home, with your fuel nearly gone and dawn breaking.

objectives.primary: Destroy or ground at least 75 percent of the parked fighters before they can scramble. Then clear the open hardpan and break contact toward the extraction corridor.
objectives.secondary: Destroy the fuel farm and the ammunition dump. A field with airframes but no fuel or munitions is out of the war for weeks, no matter how many fighters survive.
objectives.bonus: Seize the field's records from the operations bunker before you withdraw: sortie logs, dispersal plans, and the enemy air units' order of battle.

complications.name: The Scramble Clock
complications.text: From the first alarm, the alert flight can be airborne in {SCRAMBLE_MINUTES} minutes. Any fighter still on the ground at that mark either dies in the next moments or lives to hunt you. The field commander has drilled this, and his ground crews sprint for the cockpits before they are fully awake.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track a scramble clock from the first alarm. At {SCRAMBLE_MINUTES} minutes, any surviving fighter not actively under fire lifts off. From the next turn it joins the fight as an aerospace unit on your withdrawal route.

complications.name: Fuel Margin
complications.text: The column hauled its own fuel across {RAID_DISTANCE_KM} kilometers and must drive itself back. The round trip leaves {COLUMN_FUEL_HOURS} hours of spare fuel, with no resupply. Time spent fighting, a long withdrawal, or a hard run in the heat all drain the same tank.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each extra 10 minutes on the field, and each forced high-speed leg, subtracts from the fuel margin. If the margin hits zero before the extraction corridor, vehicles strand. They must be abandoned or towed, which slows the whole column.

complications.name: Open Country, No Cover
complications.text: The open desert gives you nothing to hide behind. By night it is a clear road. But the moment a fighter is overhead in daylight, your own dust trail is visible from twenty kilometers away, and there is no tree line to reach.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During a daylight withdrawal with enemy fighters airborne, the column cannot break line of sight on open ground. Each turn, any aerospace unit gets a free strafing pass at your slowest element unless your own anti-air fire pins it.

complications.name: The Roving Section
complications.text: A guard section patrols the desert approaches on no fixed schedule. It is too light to stop you, but it carries a radio, and one contact report wakes the whole field before you reach the perimeter.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a 1-in-3 chance at mission setup, the column runs into the roving guard section during the approach. If the section radios in before you silence it, the scramble clock starts at that contact instead of at the perimeter.

decisionPoints.name: The Approach
decisionPoints.context: There is no safe way across {RAID_DISTANCE_KM} kilometers of open country — only three routes, each with a different risk. The route you choose determines which problem you face when you reach the field: too little fuel left, early detection by the radar, or running into the roving guard.

options.title: The Long Cold Run
advantages: Arrive completely unseen. The widest swing around the field keeps you clear of the roving patrol and the radar's detection range
The field stays quiet until you hit the perimeter, so the scramble clock starts as late as possible
disadvantages: The longest route burns the most fuel before the first shot
More hours in the open means more chances for the roving patrol to stumble onto your trail
options.consequence: You reach the field undetected, but with the least fuel left for the trip home. A long fighting withdrawal will run your tanks dry out in the open desert.

costs.resource: Fuel spent on the long approach. Your round-trip reserve drops to its minimum before the raid even begins.
costs.risk: With this little fuel left, a drawn-out withdrawal will strand vehicles in the open before they reach the extraction corridor.

options.title: Hug the Broken Ground
advantages: A hidden approach along a dry riverbed and cliff line, out of sight of both the radar and the open desert
The shortest fuel burn on the way in, so the column arrives with fuel to spare for the run home
disadvantages: This broken ground is exactly where the enemy sited a forward listening post, and slipping past it unseen is not guaranteed
If that post wakes the field, the scramble clock starts before you are even in gun range of the flightline
options.consequence: Fast and fuel-cheap, but the raid rides on getting past one manned outpost. Clear it silently and you arrive with time; alert it and you arrive into a scramble already running.

costs.resource: a scout element sent ahead to clear or bypass the listening post before the column passes
costs.risk: An alerted post starts the scramble clock early, so you hit the perimeter against a field already standing to arms

options.title: The Direct Dash
advantages: The fastest arrival, with the least time exposed in the open and the most fuel saved for the withdrawal
Hits the flightline at speed before the field can turn a confused radar blip into a real threat
disadvantages: The straight line crosses the search radar's range, and either the approach or the dust sets it off
{NPC:opfor-commander} gets his earliest possible warning, so the scramble clock starts at the radar contact, not the perimeter
options.consequence: You trade surprise for speed and fuel. The column arrives hard and fast with fuel to burn, but the alert flight is already climbing into cockpits when you cross the perimeter.

costs.resource: surprise spent. The radar contact hands the field its full {SCRAMBLE_MINUTES}-minute warning before you arrive
costs.risk: The scramble clock starts at the radar contact, so the alert flight may be airborne before the flightline is half-wrecked

decisionPoints.name: The Kill Method
decisionPoints.context: You have only minutes on the field and {GROUNDED_FIGHTERS} fighters to destroy. Thorough destruction takes time you may not have before the scramble; fast destruction leaves survivors that take off behind you. Choosing a method is a gamble on how much time you actually have.

options.title: Demolition Charges, Revetment by Revetment
advantages: Certain kills. A charge inside the airframe means a fighter that never flies again, not a damaged one that limps off
Quiet until it detonates, so the steady sweep can clear the line before the field even realizes it is under attack
disadvantages: The slowest method. A demolition party on foot works one parking bay at a time
Every minute on the line runs down both the scramble clock and the fuel margin
options.consequence: The highest kill count, if you have the minutes. But a slow, deliberate sweep is a race against the alarm that you may lose at the far end of the line.

costs.resource: a demolition party on foot on the flightline. These are the column's most exposed minutes, spent among the parked fighters
costs.risk: A sweep this slow may still be working the last parking bays when the scramble clock runs out

options.title: Torch the Fuel Farm First
advantages: The fastest way to cripple the whole field. A burning fuel farm takes the flightline with it and grounds anything not already fueled
Lets the column start its withdrawal early, saving fuel and beating the dawn
disadvantages: The earth-walled bays shield individual airframes from the fire, so fueled, ready fighters can still take off through the flames
The fire is a beacon. It draws the recallable patrol lance and any roving section straight to you
options.consequence: You cripple the field in minutes and leave early, but you leave fighters alive in the bays. And the fire on the horizon brings every enemy unit in the district running toward you.

costs.resource: incendiary stores spent on the fuel farm. The column commits to an early withdrawal under a burning sky
costs.risk: Survivors take off from the bays behind you, and the fire guides the patrol lance onto your withdrawal route

options.title: Gun-Run the Line
advantages: Fast, and no one leaves their vehicle. The column drives the flightline at speed, firing autocannon and missiles as it passes
Keeps the force together and mobile, ready to fight clear the instant the wing reacts
disadvantages: Loud from the first shot. The scramble clock starts immediately, with no quiet grace period at all
Firing on the move damages more than it destroys. Some fighters are only wounded and take off anyway
options.consequence: The shortest time on target, but the worst results. You move fast and get clear quickly, but you wake the whole field at once and leave the most survivors to chase you.

costs.resource: a heavy load of ammunition spent on the firing runs. The column may want that ammunition badly on the way home
costs.risk: Wounded fighters take off despite the runs, and the early noise gives the alert flight its full reaction time

entries.event: Contact at the perimeter — the alarm or the radar trips. The field alarm sounds. Ground crews run for the alert fighters, and {NPC:opfor-commander} heads for the operations bunker.
The anti-air section opens up and swings its guns onto the approaches to the flightline. The alert flight's first pilots reach their cockpits.
Scramble. The first ready fighters taxi and hold. From here, any surviving fighter can take off. This is the {SCRAMBLE_MINUTES}-minute mark come due.
The recalled patrol lance turns back toward the field, directed by the operations bunker onto your likely withdrawal route.
The first scrambled fighters return overhead armed, hunting the column in the open. The patrol lance closes the distance on the ground.
First light. The column's dust trail is now visible from the air across the flat desert. You have no cover for the rest of the run home.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Every parked fighter must be wrecked and the column rolling off the open flightline before the scramble at T+8:00. Anything left flyable takes off. And any unit still out on the bare hardpan when the fighters return at T+25:00 fights the rest of the withdrawal under an enemy sky, with its fuel already running low.

opforSketch.composition: Field garrison: 1 security company of light/medium 'Mechs (20-50 tons, Regular, facing outward against ground attack), an anti-air vehicle section of 3-5 mounts (the combined-arms element, sited against aircraft, not armor), ground crews, and a recallable patrol lance out on a sweep. The {GROUNDED_FIGHTERS} parked fighters are the objective, not fighters on the board — until the scramble puts them in the air, after which they are the deadliest thing here. No reinforcements closer than the front, {RAID_DISTANCE_KM} kilometers away.
opforSketch.behavior: A garrison that has never been attacked here: slow to believe a deep ground strike is real, but fast to react once it starts. The anti-air section is aimed outward at approaching aircraft and is nearly useless against a force already inside the perimeter. {NPC:opfor-commander}'s first priority is getting the fighters airborne. He will spend ground crews to scramble fighters, because once they are flying the advantage flips and your raiders become the hunted. The patrol lance pins you in place; the fighters do the killing.

forks.name: OPERATION FOLLOWING WIND
forks.trigger: The captured records (the bonus objective) name the enemy's next airfield and its resupply schedule.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} offers an immediate follow-on strike against that second field, while {TARGET_FACTION} still thinks the first loss was a one-off. It is a RECON_RAID to confirm the wing has relocated there before the front's air power comes back.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND APRON
forks.trigger: The fuel farm or ammunition dump is destroyed, but fewer than 75 percent of the fighters are killed, or the column withdrew during a partial scramble.
forks.consequence: The wing is grounded for lack of fuel and munitions, but its fighters survive in the bays. {EMPLOYER} pays for a return strike to finish the flightline before the field is resupplied — same ground, but a garrison now awake and dug in.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY RIVERBED
forks.trigger: The scramble beat the kill. The wing is airborne, the column is caught in the open, its fuel is spent, and the withdrawal corridor is cut.
forks.consequence: The column takes cover in the broken country short of the corridor and survives the only way it can: as a stranded raiding force living off the enemy rear it came to hit. It harasses supply and waits for a rescue that has to fight its way in. This is a GUERRILLA_WARFARE mission behind the line, at raised threat.

storyElementSeed: On the long drive in, a driver checks the fuel against the odometer at every stop and reads the number aloud without being asked. Everyone in the truck knows the number that really matters out here is not how many fighters they wreck, but whether they have enough fuel left to get home.

merc.objectives.primary: The contract pays on confirmed kills, counted by gun-camera footage or wreck count, whichever the auditor accepts. Full payment requires 75 percent of the parked fighters destroyed. Destroy fewer than that and the payout drops. Remember: the fuel you burn chasing the last few fighters comes out of your own reserve, not the employer's.

is-kurita.objectives.primary: A field commander who lets his wing be caught on the ground is already disgraced; your task is to make that disgrace complete. Destroy at least three of every four fighters while they are still parked. Any pilots who manage to take off too late will carry the shame of having failed to defend their own field.

RAID_DISTANCE_KM.unit: kilometers of open country from the front to the deep field

GROUNDED_FIGHTERS.unit: aerospace fighters parked on the field

SCRAMBLE_MINUTES.unit: minutes from first alarm to the alert flight airborne

COLUMN_FUEL_HOURS.unit: hours of round-trip fuel margin the column carries

resourceGates.lackingText: You have no DropShip to stage the fast approach from a nearby hiding spot. The direct dash must launch from the extraction corridor itself. That adds an hour each way, and both hours come straight out of the {COLUMN_FUEL_HOURS}-hour fuel margin.

inspiration: Two forces converge under fire on a fresh, valuable war-machine wreck that neither can both guard and haul, so victory turns on the one irreplaceable recovery rig and on whether the prize is worth more carried off than denied to all.
skeleton: a recovery force must rig and haul a fresh assault-machine wreck off contested high ground before a rival recovery force crests the saddle, when neither side can both fight for the prize and carry it and destroying it denies it to all
title: OPERATION FALLEN CROWN
situation: {WORLD}, a contested mining frontier in {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. Two days ago a front-line {TARGET_FACTION} assault machine fell on the high saddle above the mine workings when a lucky hit destroyed its gyro. It weighs {WRECK_TONNAGE} tons, and its power plant and weapons are worth more than the company that brought it down. It lies on the ridge intact and undamaged, and everyone with a salvage rig knows exactly where it is. It is the single most valuable thing on this front. {EMPLOYER} wants it recovered whole. An intact assault machine towed home is both a serious combat asset and a fortune in rare lostech parts. The same machine blown up where it lies is worth nothing to you; it only keeps the enemy from having it. The catch is that {TARGET_FACTION} wants it back just as badly, for the same reasons, and they too will take it whole or not at all. {NPC:intel-source} reports a {TARGET_FACTION} recovery force already climbing the far slope: {RIVAL_OMNIS} front-line OmniMechs escorting their own recovery rig. They consider this salvage theirs by right, as the spoils of the battlefield. That report is only 6 hours old, so treat it as solid. The terrain decides this fight. The wreck sits on a saddle between two rising slopes. Whoever reaches it first holds it, but holding it is not the same as getting it away. A dead {WRECK_TONNAGE}-ton machine cannot move itself; it must be cabled to a recovery rig and dragged. Your one rig crawls off the high ground at just {HAUL_SPEED_KPH} kph, and the only route down is a single switchback road. That road is also the only way either side can get the prize off the mountain. Lose your rig and you cannot move the prize. Lose the road and you cannot get it out. Your deadline is your DropShip: its next departure window opens in {LIFT_WINDOW_HOURS} hours and will not wait. So you face three questions at once. Can you reach the wreck first? Can you cable it up before the enemy's heavy machines reach the saddle? And if you cannot carry it off, is it worth more to you destroyed than it is worth to them recovered? Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}. Neither side wants to fire the shot that wrecks the prize. Both of you came to haul the same trophy off this mountain, and only one rig can take it down the road.

objectives.primary: Recover the downed {TARGET_FACTION} assault machine intact — cabled to the recovery rig and delivered down the haul road to the DropShip before the lift window closes.
objectives.secondary: If full recovery proves impossible, strip and extract the irreplaceable core — power plant, fire-control suite, and any lostech components — and deny the hull to the rival.
objectives.bonus: Recover or disable the rival's recovery rig; without it, their force cannot take the prize off the mountain even if they win the saddle.

complications.name: The One Rig
complications.text: A dead {WRECK_TONNAGE}-ton machine moves only as fast as the rig that drags it, and you have exactly one rig. It is unarmored, slow, and irreplaceable. It is also the only reason this trip is worth anything. Both sides know the rig, not the wreck, is the thing that actually has to survive.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The recovery rig is a non-combatant unit with minimal armor. If it is destroyed or disabled, full recovery (the primary objective) becomes impossible no matter who holds the wreck. The mission then falls back to the core-strip secondary at best.

complications.name: Can't Fight and Tow
complications.text: Cabling the wreck and crawling it down the switchback ties up the rig and the units guarding it. Those machines are not fighting while they haul. Every gun protecting the tow is a gun missing from the firing line, and the rival's recovery force faces the same problem in reverse.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any unit assigned to guard or rig the tow takes a movement and firing penalty: it slows to the rig's pace with a restricted facing. Whoever defends the haul road fights short-handed for as long as the tow is moving.

complications.name: Salvage by Right
complications.text: The rival force sees this salvage as theirs by the law of the battlefield, and they mean to take it whole. They will not fire the shot that wrecks the prize, and they may issue a formal challenge for the right to it, fighting clean, machine against machine, so long as you do the same. Break that code and the restraint keeping the wreck intact dies with it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Until the prize is secured or destroyed, the rival holds back on purpose: one target at a time, no area-effect fire near the wreck, no ganging up. If you fire area weapons near the wreck, take a dishonorable shot, or threaten to destroy the prize, the rival drops all restraint and fights to kill from the next turn.

complications.name: The Lift Window
complications.text: The DropShip's next lift window opens in {LIFT_WINDOW_HOURS} hours. It is set by orbital timing, not by how the fight is going. A prize still on the mountain when the window closes is one you cannot leave with, no matter how well you held the saddle.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track a lift clock. The rig carrying the prize must reach the base of the haul road before the window closes. If it does not, the recovery fails at extraction even if you won the saddle, and the prize is abandoned to whoever still holds the ground.

decisionPoints.name: The Race to the Saddle
decisionPoints.context: Two slopes climb to one saddle and one wreck, and the rival is already moving. Being first to the prize is not the same as being able to leave with it; the haul road off the mountain matters as much as the wreck on it. Choose what you are racing for.

options.title: Sprint the Direct Climb
advantages: First to the wreck by the shortest line. You reach the prize and start cabling before the rival's main force arrives
Holding the wreck early lets the rig start its work in relative quiet
disadvantages: A hard, fast climb leaves your force worn out, fighting the first clash from below, uphill, and already spent
Racing for the wreck lets the rival swing behind you, take the haul road, and cut your only way down
options.consequence: You reach the prize first and rig early, but if the rival takes the haul road while you cable, you hold a prize you cannot carry off the mountain.

costs.resource: the whole force arrives committed and worn out, with no reserve held back to contest the haul road
costs.risk: The rival flanks to the switchback and seals the way down while you are still cabling the wreck

options.title: Take the Haul Road First
advantages: Seize the single switchback and you own the only way the prize leaves the mountain, for either side
Forces the rival to come to you on ground you chose, with the wreck as bait between you
disadvantages: Giving up the wreck first means the rival's rig may cable it before you can contest the saddle
If they rig fast and you cannot retake the saddle, you hold an empty road while they work the prize above you
options.consequence: You control the exit and the pace, but you have handed the rival first claim on the wreck. The fight becomes whether you can take it back before their rig has it cabled.

costs.resource: the wreck given up for the first phase, so the rival reaches it ahead of you
costs.risk: A fast rival rig cables the prize before you retake the saddle, leaving you only the road they must be forced down

options.title: Split: Rig to the Wreck, Guns to the Road
advantages: Contest both the prize and the exit at once, giving the rival a free run at neither
Keeps the recovery option open whichever way the first clash breaks
disadvantages: Both groups fight below strength: the saddle force cannot mass and the road force cannot mass
The rig moves forward behind a thin screen toward a contested wreck, its most exposed position of all
options.consequence: You give up neither the prize nor the road, but you hold neither in strength. The battle becomes two understrength fights against the lift clock, with the rig forward in both.

costs.resource: the force split between saddle and road, giving up concentration to deny the rival a free objective
costs.risk: Two understrength fights at once, with the irreplaceable rig pushed forward behind a screen that may not hold

decisionPoints.name: Carried Off or Denied
decisionPoints.context: However the saddle fight breaks, the prize forces one last question before the lift window closes: what is it worth to you? A whole machine recovered, a core stripped and the hull destroyed, or a prize neither side gets to keep. The rival is asking themselves the same thing across the saddle.

options.title: Recover the Whole Machine
advantages: The biggest prize: a front-line assault machine towed home whole, all its combat value and all its lostech
Respects the rival's restraint, so the fight stays clean and the wreck stays whole while you cable it
disadvantages: The slowest option. Cabling and crawling {WRECK_TONNAGE} tons down the switchback at {HAUL_SPEED_KPH} kph eats the whole lift window
The rig and its escort are tied to the tow for the entire descent, fighting short-handed the whole way
options.consequence: If you can hold the saddle and the road long enough to crawl it down, the payoff is total. If the rival breaks through the tow anywhere on the switchback, you lose the prize, the rig, and the time.

costs.resource: the rig and a full escort tied to the tow for the entire descent, so the firing line fights short-handed
costs.risk: A single break-through on the switchback strands a half-towed prize and a stalled, irreplaceable rig

options.title: Strip the Core, Blow the Hull
advantages: Fast. The engineers pull the power plant, fire-control, and lostech in a fraction of the time a full tow takes
Keeps the hull from the rival for good. What you cannot carry, no one carries
disadvantages: A partial prize. The core is worth a fraction of the whole machine, and the edge of capturing it intact is gone
Blowing the hull near the rival is the dishonorable shot that ends their restraint, and the fight turns to a kill-everything brawl
options.consequence: You leave the mountain light and fast with the irreplaceable parts and a furious rival behind you. The prize is kept from them, but only half-won by you.

costs.resource: an engineering team forward on the wreck under fire, plus the demolition charges to drop the hull
costs.risk: Blowing the hull breaks the rival's restraint, so the withdrawal is fought against a force no longer fighting clean

options.title: Wire It and Bargain
advantages: Holds the prize hostage. Wired to blow, it becomes leverage over the whole saddle, and the rival wants it intact as much as you do
Buys time and may push the rival to back off rather than risk the wreck they came for
disadvantages: A bluff a Clan rival may call. They may decide a destroyed prize you cannot have is an acceptable outcome, and force the issue
Locks you into either blowing it or handing it over. Once the charges are set, there is no quiet third way out
options.consequence: You turn the wreck into a standoff. Either the rival gives up the saddle to save it, or they call the bluff and you must choose between blowing the one thing you both came for or walking away empty-handed.

costs.resource: demolition charges set on the wreck, plus a talk-team exposed to make the threat believable
costs.risk: A called bluff forces you to blow it or surrender it, and a Clan rival may accept a destroyed prize over a dishonored one

entries.event: Both forces break cover at the base of the slopes. The wreck lies on the saddle between them, cold and untouched. {NPC:opfor-commander} signals the rival's intent: recovery, by right, and intact.
Lead elements trade fire on the lower rocks. Both recovery rigs hold back below the crest, out of the first exchange.
The first force reaches the wreck and can start rigging. Cabling a full tow begins here; stripping the core is faster.
If cabling started at T+10:00, the tow is barely moving. The rig crawls across the saddle at {HAUL_SPEED_KPH} kph toward the switchback.
The rival's heavy element crests the far slope onto the saddle in strength. The fight is now general across the wreck.
Lift window check. The prize must be on the descent by now to reach the DropShip before the window closes. Anything still on the saddle is running out of time.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The prize must be rigged and the rig onto the descent before the rival's heavies crest at T+30:00. Miss that and you fight for it on the open saddle with the lift window closing at T+45:00. A prize still on the mountain when the window shuts is abandoned, no matter how well you held the saddle.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} recovery Star: {RIVAL_OMNIS} front-line OmniMechs (Veteran/Elite, a mixed-weight group with at least one assault chassis) escorting a single recovery rig of their own. No combat vehicles; this is a Clan force, 'Mechs and a rig. They consider the salvage theirs by right of the battlefield, and mean to take it whole or keep it from you. They will not fire the shot that wrecks the prize unless you do first.
opforSketch.behavior: Honor-bound and patient. The rival may open with a batchall, a formal Clan claim and challenge for the right to the salvage. They will fight cleanly, one target at a time, no ganging up, no area-effect fire near the wreck, as long as you do the same. Their recovery rig is their one critical weakness, exactly as yours is, and they protect it the same way. Dishonor them, with area fire near the prize, a threat to destroy it, or a treacherous shot, and the restraint ends. From that point they fight to destroy you completely, and the wreck both sides wanted whole may end the day as scrap neither can carry off.

forks.name: OPERATION HIGH ASSAY
forks.trigger: The machine is recovered intact, and its undamaged systems reveal the {TARGET_FACTION} forward salvage and supply cache that sent out the rival's rig.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} funds an immediate raid on that cache while the rival force is still recovering on the mountain. It is an OBJECTIVE_RAID to take or burn the supply base that would have rearmed the unit you just beat.

forks.name: OPERATION COLD ASSAY
forks.trigger: Only the core was stripped, or the prize was destroyed by both sides, or the rig came down the mountain damaged and followed.
forks.consequence: The rival, denied an intact prize, wants to know who you were and where the core went. They put a tracking element onto your trail. {EMPLOYER} sends you to confirm the rival's strength and line of advance before they find you first. It is a RECON_RAID with the enemy chasing you.

forks.name: OPERATION LEFT ON THE STONE
forks.trigger: The rig was destroyed, or the saddle was lost with your recovery crew still forward. Engineers and a stalled rig are stranded on the high ground as the rival takes the prize.
forks.consequence: Your people are on the mountain and the rival holds the ground between them and the road. Before anything else, you go back up for them. It is an EXTRACTION_RAID to pull a stranded recovery crew off contested high ground, against a force that now has every reason to kill them.

storyElementSeed: The recovery chief walks the cables out to the dead machine by hand while the lower slope is still trading fire. A tow rigged in a hurry snaps on the first switchback, and a snapped tow strands everything. She has decided the one thing she will not do today is lose the rig to save ninety seconds on the cabling.

is-kurita.objectives.primary: Recover the machine whole and it becomes a trophy the district will remember. Let it be destroyed on the saddle and the record will say you could not carry off what you had already won. Bring the prize down the mountain intact, on the rig, before the window closes. The Dragon counts what comes home, not what was merely held.

clan.objectives.primary: The salvage is isorla, the spoils owed to whoever proves the stronger over it. Take it whole and clean. A machine dragged home intact is honor doubled, the enemy's and your own. A machine wrecked just to deny it is a coward's prize that shames the rig meant to carry it. Win the right to it, then haul it home as a victor hauls his spoils.

WRECK_TONNAGE.unit: tons — the downed assault machine's recoverable mass

RIVAL_OMNIS.unit: front-line OmniMechs in the rival recovery force

HAUL_SPEED_KPH.unit: kph — the recovery rig's towing speed off the high ground

LIFT_WINDOW_HOURS.unit: hours until the DropShip's next lift window closes

resourceGates.lackingText: You have no established base or depot to receive and hold a {WRECK_TONNAGE}-ton recovery. A full intact tow is impossible, because there is nowhere to put it. The whole-machine option locks, so strip the core or destroy the prize instead.

inspiration: A precision strike breaches one structural keystone whose failure cascades down a whole industrial watershed — against defenses purpose-built for the only method that breaches it, knowing the cascade falls on the lifeline of the people it claims to free.
skeleton: a strike company must breach a dam's keystone by the one method its point-defense is laid against, inside the window a feint holds the reserve, choosing how much of the downstream lifeline the cascade is allowed to take
title: OPERATION BROKEN WEIR
situation: {WORLD}, the industrial heart of {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. {TARGET_FACTION} holds this valley because it holds the dam at the head of it. That one concrete dam drives the power turbines, fills the factory cooling lines, and floats the barge traffic that supplies every plant on the floodplain below. Destroy the dam and the entire war-industry region downstream loses power, coolant, river transport, and shell production for a season. {EMPLOYER} wants it destroyed. {NPC:intel-source} has detailed structural intelligence. The dam holds its water behind its spillway gates, and those gates can be breached by only one method: a precise hit on the seam of a gate, right at the waterline. Anything less just scars the concrete. That report is 8 days old but rated solid. {TARGET_FACTION} knows all this too, which is the core problem. They have placed {POINT_DEFENSE_GUNS} point-defense guns along that one approach path, the only line from which the seam can be hit. They also hold a mobile reserve back from the dam to crush anything that gets through the guns. The ground below the dam is what makes this mission hard to stomach. The floodplain is crowded farmland, cut with levees, where the same reservoir that feeds the factories also feeds the towns. A full-reservoir breach floods both. You can aim the breach to wreck the industry while sparing the floodplain, or aim it to take everything. The difference is counted in the lives of the people {EMPLOYER}'s own broadcasts claim to be freeing. To get a clear attack run at all, a diversion has to pull the reserve away, and a diversion only fools the enemy for so long. {NPC:opfor-commander} will send the reserve back toward the dam the moment he sees the diversion for what it is. You have {BREACH_RUNS} clean attempts at the seam before the guns learn your method and close the approach. You have until the reserve is released to make those attempts count. And once the seam is breached, the flood fully develops in {CASCADE_MINUTES} minutes, faster than any warning can run ahead of the water. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}. One seam, one method, one window. What happens to the valley below afterward is the one decision the briefing leaves to you.

objectives.primary: Breach the spillway-gate seam by your chosen method and shut down the dam's industrial output for the season. The turbines, coolant lines, and barge channel all depend on the reservoir being full.
objectives.secondary: Keep the company intact through the breach and the flood, and break contact through the valley before the mobile reserve closes the approach behind you.
objectives.bonus: Capture the dam's control house and its records before the breach: the water-release schedules, the downstream warning network, and the floodplain population data that decide who the flood reaches.

complications.name: One Method, Waiting Guns
complications.text: The seam can be hit from exactly one approach, and {TARGET_FACTION} has mounted {POINT_DEFENSE_GUNS} point-defense guns along that line. The surest way in is the one the defense was built to stop. Every run after the first flies into guns that now have your range and your timing.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each attack run on the seam after the first takes a growing defensive bonus as the guns learn your method. After {BREACH_RUNS} runs the approach is effectively closed: further attempts by that method draw crippling fire until the guns are suppressed or destroyed.

complications.name: How Long the Feint Holds
complications.text: Your whole window exists because a feint in another sector holds the mobile reserve away. {NPC:opfor-commander} is no fool. The diversion convinces him for a while, then it stops working, and the moment he sees it as a feint he sends the reserve straight at the dam.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track a feint clock. While it holds, the reserve is off the board. When it expires, or if the feint is mishandled, the reserve heads for the dam and arrives {RESERVE_DISTANCE_MIN} minutes later, fully committed.

complications.name: The Flood You Start
complications.text: Once the seam goes, the breach widens on its own. The reservoir does the rest of the work in {CASCADE_MINUTES} minutes, tearing the spillway open and sending the water down the valley faster than any warning can run ahead of it. The water does not tell the factories from the towns, and neither will the report afterward.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a successful breach, the flood builds over {CASCADE_MINUTES} minutes. Any unit, yours or theirs, still in the downstream channels must reach high ground before it fully develops or be swept away. The floodplain damage, and its civilian cost, depends on whether you chose a full breach or a smaller one.

complications.name: The Guns and the Reserve Are Separate
complications.text: The guns set on the seam cannot leave the seam. The reserve held back cannot react until it is released. The two halves of the defense are kept apart on purpose, and your chance exists in the gap between them, for exactly as long as the feint holds them apart.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The point-defense guns are fixed to the approach line and cannot chase you off it. The mobile reserve cannot engage until the feint clock expires. Your whole opportunity is the window while both of those are true at once.

decisionPoints.name: The Run
decisionPoints.context: The seam can be breached three ways, and the defense is built for the obvious one. Precision, mass, or a charge placed by hand: each pays for the breach differently in exposure, time, and certainty. Whichever you pick, the waiting guns are ready for it.

options.title: The Precision Run
advantages: The exact method the seam needs. One clean hit on the gate waterline breaches it outright
Fast. A single committed pass, with no time spent grinding away at the structure
disadvantages: This is exactly the run the {POINT_DEFENSE_GUNS} guns are set for, the most expected and most heavily defended line of all
It sends your attack element straight into the guns at their best range
options.consequence: If the run gets through, the seam breaches on the first try and you are clear before the reserve is released. If the guns kill the attack element, you have spent your best method against the defense built to stop it.

costs.resource: the attack element and its munitions committed to a single pass through the guns' best firing range
costs.risk: The one method the defense expects, flown straight at the guns built to break it. A lost attack element wastes the surest breach

options.title: Swamp the Gate With Mass
advantages: Overwhelms the point-defense by giving it more targets than {POINT_DEFENSE_GUNS} guns can handle at once
Spreads the risk across the company instead of betting the breach on one attack element
disadvantages: Massed fire is imprecise. It may only crack the seam instead of breaching it, wasting runs you do not have
It puts the whole company inside the guns' arc, trading one element's exposure for everyone's
options.consequence: The guns are swamped and the seam takes heavy, steady fire. But a crack that holds means another run against a fully alert defense, with the feint clock draining the whole time.

costs.resource: a heavy load of ammunition spent by the whole company in the saturation runs
costs.risk: Mass may crack but not breach the seam. A gate that holds after the salvo means another run with the reserve already stirring

options.title: Hand-Place the Charge
advantages: The surest breach of all. A charge set on the seam by an engineering team cannot miss the way a run can
Slips past the guns' best range. The guns are set for an approaching attack, not a team already on the dam
disadvantages: The slowest method by far. Getting a team onto the dam and setting the charge eats deep into the feint window
The team works the gate under fire, the most exposed position on the board and the hardest to pull back from
options.consequence: If the team reaches the seam and sets the charge, the breach is certain and you can time the flood exactly. But a team pinned on the dam when the reserve is released is a team you do not get back.

costs.resource: an engineering team forward on the dam crest under fire, plus the time to place and set the breaching charge
costs.risk: A team caught on the gate when the feint expires faces the full reserve with nowhere to fall back to

decisionPoints.name: How Far the Water Goes
decisionPoints.context: How you breach the dam matters as much as whether you breach it. The same seam, opened different ways, can destroy only the industry or flood the whole valley. {EMPLOYER}'s broadcasts call this valley's people liberated. The floodwater does not care about broadcasts, and what you decide here is what the record will say you did to them.

options.title: Full-Head Breach
advantages: Maximum destruction. The full reservoir tears the spillway wide open and ends the valley's war industry beyond any quick repair
Leaves nothing for {TARGET_FACTION} to restart. The dam and its water supply are gone together
disadvantages: The flood takes the farming floodplain along with the factories. The levee towns drown alongside the war works
The political and contract cost of drowning the people you claimed to free may outlast the military gain by years
options.consequence: The industry is destroyed, and so is the lifeline beneath it. You win the strategic goal, but you hand {TARGET_FACTION} a propaganda victory and the survivors a grudge with your employer's name on it.

costs.resource: the floodplain gambled away. The flood reaches the levee towns, not only the factories
costs.risk: Drowning a valley you came to free. The civilian cost becomes {EMPLOYER}'s war record and {TARGET_FACTION}'s recruiting poster

options.title: Breach the Turbine Feed, Spare the Plain
advantages: Kills the turbines and the coolant supply, so the industry goes dark, while the spillway gates keep the floodplain's water held back
Keeps the lifeline intact. The towns keep their levees, and you stay the side that freed them
disadvantages: Only partial destruction. The dam itself survives, and the industry can be rebuilt faster than after a full breach
A lower employer payout. The contract counted the whole watershed, and you delivered half of it on purpose
options.consequence: You shut down the war industry without drowning the valley. {EMPLOYER}'s auditors mark the smaller result, but the people keep a reason to call you the better side.

costs.resource: the precision to hit the turbine feed pipe specifically, not the gate seam. It is a harder, narrower target
costs.risk: A surviving dam means a faster {TARGET_FACTION} restart, and an employer weighing the spared valley against the unfinished job

options.title: Hold the Breach as Leverage
advantages: No destruction at all. Show that you can breach the gate, then demand {TARGET_FACTION} shut the industry down themselves
Keeps both the lifeline and the dam whole, if the threat is believed
disadvantages: Only works if {TARGET_FACTION} believes you will flood a valley full of people. A fanatic enemy may not
Locks you into either carrying out the threat or leaving with the industry still running
options.consequence: You turn the dam into an ultimatum. Either the enemy shuts down the factories to save the valley, or they call the bluff and you are back to choosing between a flood and leaving empty-handed.

costs.resource: the control house and its water-release network seized intact to make the threat believable
costs.risk: A called bluff against a fanatic leaves you breaching anyway or leaving with nothing, and the window does not reopen

entries.event: The diversion opens against the garrison's far flank. The point-defense crews move up onto the seam's approach line as the company runs in.
First attack run on the seam. The guns get your range. From here, each further run by the same method flies into a warned battery that has your timing.
The feint starts to wear off. {NPC:opfor-commander} calls the dam and begins to read the far-flank attack for what it is.
The feint expires. The mobile reserve heads for the dam, {RESERVE_DISTANCE_MIN} minutes out, fully committed.
The reserve closes on the dam approach. If the seam is breached, the flood is already tearing the spillway open and filling the downstream channels.
If breached near T+18:00, the flood is now fully developed. The water is down the valley, the approach is cut, and your only withdrawal route is whatever ground stayed above the flood.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The seam must be breached before the reserve is released at T+18:00. Miss that and you are flying attack runs into a fully ranged battery, with the reserve inbound and the feint spent, and the {BREACH_RUNS}-run window will close on the approach before the gate gives.

opforSketch.composition: Dam garrison: 1 defense company of Regular/Veteran 'Mechs (Jihad-era, medium/heavy bias), a dedicated point-defense battery of {POINT_DEFENSE_GUNS} mounts, and a mobile reserve held back from the dam, {RESERVE_DISTANCE_MIN} minutes away when released. The battery is flak and direct-fire vehicles (the combined-arms element) placed specifically across the seam's one approach line, tuned to that method by design. The point-defense and the reserve are two halves of one defense, kept apart on purpose.
opforSketch.behavior: The point-defense fights the approach and only the approach. It is fixed to its line and cannot chase you: deadly against the one method it was set for, ineffective against anything off its line. The reserve sits out the feint and arrives all at once when {NPC:opfor-commander} sees through the diversion. He defends the dam like a holy relic. He will spend the garrison freely to hold the gate, and he is counting on the floodplain behind him as a shield no honorable enemy will breach. The whole defense assumes you will refuse to drown the valley.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN SLUICE
forks.trigger: The gate is breached, and the captured records (the bonus objective) reveal the next point on the industrial lifeline: the power substation or barge lock the dark valley now depends on.
forks.consequence: With the industry already reeling, {EMPLOYER} mounts a follow-on diversionary strike to keep {TARGET_FACTION}'s reserve chasing a decoy while the wider offensive moves. It is a DIVERSIONARY_RAID that uses the lifeline loss to pin the enemy a sector away.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND SEAM
forks.trigger: The seam cracked but held, or only the turbine feed was breached and the dam still stands. The industry is hurt but repairable.
forks.consequence: The dam still stands and {TARGET_FACTION} is already repairing it. {EMPLOYER} pays for a return strike to finish the breach before repairs and a reinforced point-defense make it impossible. Same seam, but a defense now fully awake.

forks.name: OPERATION HIGH GROUND
forks.trigger: The breach failed and the reserve caught the company at the dam with the approach cut. The company is pinned in the valley with its withdrawal route lost.
forks.consequence: The company scatters into the flooded, levee-laced country and survives the only way it can: as a strike force in hiding, harassing the reserve's supply and the dam garrison until a rescue can fight its way to high ground. It is a GUERRILLA_WARFARE mission in hostile, half-drowned terrain, at raised threat.

storyElementSeed: The company's chaplain-engineer walks the breaching team through the control house's population records. How many towns sit below the dam. How high their levees stand. How long a flood warning takes to travel the valley. He does it not to change the order, but so that whoever sets the charge sets it knowing exactly what the water will reach.

merc.objectives.primary: The contract pays for the industry stopped, not the valley drowned. Read the rider in Section 7 before you choose the breach. A full-reservoir flood voids the conduct clause, and the war-crimes protection with it. A clean industrial kill pays in full and keeps your bond. The auditor measures the factories dark and the levees still standing, in that order.

comstar.objectives.primary: The dam is the single point on which the whole valley's industry depends — destroy it and the enemy's war production collapses with it. Breach the industrial side of the dam and record exactly how far the resulting flood reaches. Blake's enemies lose their factories, and the Order would rather have a precise measurement of the flood than have to answer for it later.

BREACH_RUNS.unit: clean attack runs the axis allows before the point-defense closes it

CASCADE_MINUTES.unit: minutes from breach to a fully developed downstream cascade

RESERVE_DISTANCE_MIN.unit: minutes for the mobile reserve to reach the dam once released

POINT_DEFENSE_GUNS.unit: point-defense mounts laid on the seam's approach axis

resourceGates.lackingText: You have no depot stock of the special breaching munition the precision run needs. It must be bought forward at a premium and in limited quantity, fewer than {BREACH_RUNS} rounds on hand. So a missed first run may leave no second attempt by this method.

skeleton: an air-landed company must keep the single clearing it came down on both defended and landable - its only conduit for relief and casualty lift, and the enemy's fixation - so every contraction that buys survival narrows the door its rescue must land through, while the attacker's honor convention is the only thing keeping the full weight off it.
inspiration: the air-assault defence of Landing Zone X-Ray in the Ia Drang, 1965 - a heli-landed force holds its own LZ, its only resupply and medevac conduit, against a far larger encircling force until relieved.
title: OPERATION GREEN LANTERN
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. Your command was dropped in to hold a single clearing in deep forest: {LZ_WIDTH_M} meters of open ground ringed by thick jungle, with a ridge to the east that rises three hundred meters above the treetops. {EMPLOYER} landed your company here ahead of the main line because the relief column behind you needs a place to land, and this is the only flat ground a DropShip can safely set down on within two hundred kilometers. The order is simple. The odds are not. Hold the landing zone open until the relief arrives. The main column is {RELIEF_HOURS} hours away and cannot reach you any sooner. The {TARGET_FACTION} advance guard ahead of it can reach you within the hour. {NPC:intel-source} estimates that guard at {ATTACKER_RATIO} times your combat weight: a Clan vanguard that bid its way to the front and means to take this ground before the column behind you can use it. You have one advantage, and it is an odd one. The Clans fight by their honor code, one challenger at a time, and they hold mass attacks in contempt. That is the only reason a company this outnumbered can survive at all, and it lasts only as long as you give them no reason to drop it. The clearing is both your lifeline and your weak spot. It is the only ground your own casualty flights and reinforcements can land on, and it is exactly the ground the enemy most wants under their guns. Every meter of perimeter you give up to survive narrows the opening your relief has to land through. {CASUALTY_LIFT} of your crews are already wounded and waiting on the evacuation line at the clearing's north edge. Smoke from the first wrecks is thickening over the trees. And the lead relief flight, a single heavy lander bringing your first reinforcements and there to lift out your worst casualties, is already inbound on a schedule that will not wait. It will land only if the clearing is clear of fire when it arrives. If the enemy holds the ridge or breaks your southern line, it diverts, and your company is cut off, with its wounded and no way out. The watch you stand tonight is not really about holding ground. It is about keeping one patch of open grass landable until first light.

objectives.primary: Keep the landing zone landable until the lead relief flight arrives at the end of the assault. That means holding the south arc and keeping the clearing's center clear of direct fire, so the flight can set down and lift the casualty line.
objectives.secondary: Keep the {TARGET_FACTION} guard off the east ridge that overlooks the pad, or retake it before the flight makes its approach.
objectives.bonus: Take a prisoner or an intact wreck from a fallen challenger for {NPC:intel-source}. The guard's markings will name which Cluster bid for this ground.

complications.name: The Honor Code at the Tree Line
complications.text: The Clan guard fights by its honor-duel code, engaging in ones and twos instead of swarming, and this alone keeps their numbers off you. But any act they see as dishonorable can free the whole guard to come on at once: massing fire on a single challenger, firing on a machine they think is disabled, or faking a surrender.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The attacker commits units a few at a time (one to two engaged per defender) until the defender breaks the honor code. From that point the attacker may mass fire freely on any target for the rest of the fight.

complications.name: The Ridge Battery
complications.text: A Clan Star is climbing the east ridge above the clearing. From the crest its weapons reach the pad directly, and while it holds the ridge the eastern third of the clearing is a death-trap for anything that tries to land there.
complications.mechanicalEffect: While the enemy holds the ridge, the main pad is unsafe to land on: any relief or casualty-lift landing takes a direct-fire damage roll on approach, and the lead flight will divert rather than land under fire unless the ridge is suppressed.

complications.name: Canopy Smoke
complications.text: Burning wrecks and the close jungle canopy lay smoke across the clearing in drifting banks. It blinds the guard's gunnery as readily as your own, but it also narrows the relief flight's approach window to the minutes the pad is visible from the air.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During smoke turns all detection and visual ID ranges are halved for both sides; the relief flight's landing window only opens on turns the pad is smoke-clear, randomized after deployment.

complications.name: Casualty Drag
complications.text: Every crippled friendly 'Mech puts its crew on the lift line, and that line keeps growing at the clearing's north edge. The wounded cannot be left behind, and the ground they wait on must stay clear no matter how the line bends elsewhere.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each crippled defender adds to a casualty count. Once it passes a set number, one perimeter position at the lift line must be held for the lift instead of maneuvered, pinning a unit in place.

decisionPoints.name: The Perimeter and the Door
decisionPoints.context: Your company cannot hold a perimeter wide enough to keep the whole clearing clear of fire and also strong enough to survive a rush. The line you draw is the door your relief lands through. Draw it wide and it is thin; draw it tight and the pad falls under the guard's guns.

options.title: Hold Wide - Keep the Pad Clear
advantages: The clearing's center stays out of direct fire, so the relief can land safely
The casualty lift can work the whole north edge without taking fire
disadvantages: The perimeter is thin everywhere, and a concentrated attack can break through
No real reserve. A breakthrough is met with whatever unit is nearest
options.consequence: The pad is clear and the flight lands clean, unless the guard concentrates on one arc. If it does, the line opens there and the fight comes to the lift line.

costs.resource: no reserve held back. Every 'Mech is on the line
costs.risk: A thin line gives way where it is hit, and if it breaks, it breaks at the pad

options.title: Contract Tight - Survive First
advantages: A small, strong perimeter you can actually hold against the weight coming at you
A real reserve, free to plug a breach or answer a challenge
disadvantages: The clearing's center falls inside the guard's direct-fire range
The relief must land under fire at the pad's edge, or divert to the worse backup site
options.consequence: Your company survives the night intact, but the pad is unsafe. The lead flight lands under fire or diverts, and the casualty lift is paid for in the open.

costs.resource: the pad's clear airspace, given up to the guard's guns
costs.risk: The relief flight lands under fire and may be hit on the pad, or diverts and leaves you with no reinforcement this window

options.title: Sally the Guns
advantages: A spoiling attack at the ridge approach pushes the guard's direct-fire weapons back off the clearing
Buys clean airspace over the pad for the landing window without giving up the perimeter
disadvantages: The attacking element fights outside the perimeter, where the guard can mass on it without breaking their honor code
The rest of the line is weaker for every 'Mech you send out
options.consequence: If the attack reaches the ridge approach, the pad clears and the flight lands clean. If it is cut off, you have spent a third of your company outside the perimeter for nothing.

costs.resource: a third of the company committed outside the perimeter
costs.risk: Outside the perimeter, a single challenge turns into a mass envelopment the moment the guard rules your attack dishonorable

decisionPoints.name: The Lead Flight on Final
decisionPoints.context: The relief lander calls inbound, carrying your first reinforcement and the only lift your casualty line will get this window. The pad is not clean. Whether it comes in, holds off, or diverts is your call, and what limits that call is the flight's fuel, not what you would prefer.

options.title: Wave It In Hot
advantages: The casualty line clears now, and your first reinforcement is on the ground this minute
Closes the window before the guard fully ranges the pad
disadvantages: The lander takes fire on final approach and may be hit on the pad, blocking it for every flight after
Locks you into defending the pad's airspace at the worst moment of the assault
options.consequence: Reinforcement and lift happen now, at the price of a ship exposed. A lander hit on the pad turns your lifeline into a wreck the next flight cannot land past.

costs.resource: the lander exposed on final approach
costs.risk: A lander killed on the pad blocks the clearing. No flight can land past its wreck until it is dragged clear

options.title: Hold It Off Until the Pad Is Clean
advantages: The ship is not risked until the ridge is suppressed and the south arc holds
The landing, when it comes, is clean, and the reinforcement arrives organized
disadvantages: The casualty line waits, and some of the wounded do not have the time
No reinforcement lands this window. Your thin line fights the next push as it is
options.consequence: You trade the ship's safety for your wounded's time and your line's strength. The flight lands later, or not at all if the pad never clears.

costs.resource: the casualty line's time, plus one window of reinforcement that never lands
costs.risk: If the pad never clears, the flight burns its fuel and leaves with your wounded still on the line

options.title: Divert to the Secondary Pad
advantages: The ship is saved, and the reinforcement lands away from the guard's guns
The casualty line can be walked to the backup site under cover of the tree line
disadvantages: The backup site is a worse, unguarded spot a twenty-minute fight off the perimeter
The reinforcement arrives in small groups, on foot through contested forest, late to the line
options.consequence: The flight lands safely but is useless to the immediate fight. Your reinforcement walks in a few at a time and your casualties move overland while the assault peaks behind them.

costs.resource: the reinforcement's speed. It arrives in small groups, twenty minutes late
costs.risk: A casualty column moving overland through the enemy ring is a soft target the guard may cut off from the perimeter

entries.event: Alarm. The advance guard's first challengers step out of the south tree line. The lead relief flight reports inbound, ETA the zone T+28:00, and will land or divert based on the pad's state when it arrives.
First indirect fire lands across the clearing. The south picket falls back to the inner tree line. The casualty lift point is set at the pad's north edge.
A Clan Star begins climbing the east ridge. If it reaches the crest, the eastern third of the pad comes under direct fire and turns unsafe.
The south arc must be re-secured by now, or the clearing's center enters direct-fire range. The ridge element is minutes from the crest.
Last clean window. The ridge must be suppressed or retaken and the south arc held for the pad to be clear for the inbound flight.
The lead flight is on final approach. It lands, with medevac and reinforcement, only if the pad is clear. Otherwise it diverts to the backup site and the company holds on cut off.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The pad must be clear, with the south arc held and the ridge off the clearing's center, by T+22:00. Miss that and the lead flight on final approach at T+28:00 diverts: the medevac is scrubbed, no reinforcement lands, and the hold becomes a cut-off fight with the wounded still inside the perimeter.

opforSketch.composition: A Clan advance guard the weight of a reinforced Trinary (10-15 OmniMechs), medium-heavy bias (45-75 tons), Veteran-to-Elite, fighting MECH_ONLY per Clan invasion doctrine: no vehicles, no aerospace beyond an occasional strafing pass. A forward Star presses the south arc, a second Star maneuvers for the east ridge, and the rest is the reserve the bidding left them.
opforSketch.behavior: The guard fights by its honor code in the open: challengers engage in ones and twos and scorn ganging up, which is the only reason a company survives the first hour. It treats massing fire on a single challenger, or firing on a machine it thinks is disabled, as dishonorable. Such an act frees the whole guard to attack as one. It pushes for the ridge and the pad, not the kill: it takes ground, not prisoners, and it breaks off individual duels once honor is satisfied, not at a set damage level.

forks.name: OPERATION ANVIL HELD
forks.trigger: Pad clear at T+28:00, ridge cleared, lead flight landed, and the casualty line lifted.
forks.consequence: The relief column lands clean behind you and the corridor opens. Your company is pushed forward to harass the guard's drop site before it can regroup. It is an OBJECTIVE_RAID into the ground the guard just held.

forks.name: OPERATION SHORT FINAL
forks.trigger: The pad stayed landable, but the ridge stayed contested or the casualty lift only partly cleared.
forks.consequence: The lead flight landed under fire and lifted what it could. The company holds the zone another night against the guard's second push while the ridge stays a constant threat on the flank. It is GARRISON_DUTY continued, at raised threat.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN PAD
forks.trigger: The landing zone went unsafe, with the south arc collapsed or the ridge holding the clearing's center, and the lead flight diverted.
forks.consequence: Cut off with the wounded and no lift, the company must break contact and fight its way out through the tightening enemy ring to the relief's backup site. It is a fighting linkup with the enemy chasing, RELIEF_DUTY in reverse.

storyElementSeed: A medic marks the lift line with a strip of orange panel weighted by a rock, then moves it ten meters north when the first round lands where it was; the wounded are carried to the new mark without being told why, and that scrap of panel becomes the most-watched thing in the clearing.

merc.objectives.primary: The contract priced the LZ, not the night. Keep the pad landable until the lead flight lands - the bond pays on a flyable zone and a lifted casualty line, and the auditors will read the landing log, not your bruises.

comstar.objectives.primary: The zone is the conduit and the conduit must stay open. Hold the pad green until the lead flight is down; a landing made is a sacrament kept, a diversion is a prayer unanswered, and both go into the log in clear.

ATTACKER_RATIO.unit: times the defender's weight - the advance guard's strength

RELIEF_HOURS.unit: hours until the main relief column reaches the zone

CASUALTY_LIFT.unit: wounded crew waiting on the lift line

resourceGates.lackingText: You have no DropShip to work the backup site. The diverted reinforcement comes in on {EMPLOYER}'s contracted lift, on its schedule, not yours. And the casualty column walks the full overland route to meet it, so twenty minutes becomes forty.

phases.name: POSTURE - THE CLEARING
phases.lead: You came down on this grass an hour ago and the line is still being set. The first job is reading the ground you will defend before the south tree line sets the schedule for you: where the jungle gives the guard a hidden approach, where the ridge overlooks the pad, and where the casualty line can wait out of the worst of it.

dataBlock.Landing clearing: {LZ_WIDTH_M}m across, canopy on three sides, the east ridge 300m above the treetops
dataBlock.Casualty line: north edge, {CASUALTY_LIFT} crew waiting, the one arc that must stay clear for the lift
dataBlock.Relief windows: lead flight ETA T+28:00; main column {RELIEF_HOURS}h out
dataBlock.Pad state: green = landable; red the moment the ridge is held or the south arc breaks

phases.protocol: Pad-state calls run on the company net in one word. GREEN means the clearing's center is clear of direct fire and the lift can work. RED means the ridge has the pad or the south arc has opened. The inbound flight flies on that word and nothing else. Challenge discipline is the other half: no 'Mech opens on a single Clan challenger with more than its own guns. Massing fire is the act that ends their honor code, so the company holds to one-on-one duels until the guard breaks that code first.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Why a Clan guard that outnumbers you {ATTACKER_RATIO} to one comes on one machine at a time, and the exact list of things you can do that would make it stop.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT - THE DOOR UNDER FIRE
phases.lead: The assault comes for the ridge and the pad, not for you, and the clock is the lead flight on final approach at T+28:00. The hard deadline is a clear pad at T+22:00. Everything in this fight is arranged around keeping the door open long enough for the relief to come through it.

dataBlock.Ridge crest: east side; from the crest the pad's eastern third is under direct fire and unsafe
dataBlock.South arc: must be re-secured by T+15:00 or the clearing's center enters weapons range
dataBlock.Clean window: T+22:00 - last point to suppress the ridge and hold the arc for a clear pad
dataBlock.Flight final: T+28:00 - lands if the pad is clear, diverts if it is not

routes.name: GRASS
routes.desc: Straight across the open clearing to the ridge approach, the short way.
routes.tradeoff: Fastest to the ridge, but every meter is in the open under the guard's guns, and a 'Mech crossing the pad is a 'Mech off the perimeter.

routes.name: ROOTLINE
routes.desc: Along the inner tree line at the clearing's east edge, under cover to the foot of the ridge.
routes.tradeoff: Hidden by the jungle and out of the guard's line of fire until the final climb, but slower, and the smoke that hides you also hides what waits at the ridge foot.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Holding a door open while it is the most-shot-at ground on the planet: why the reserve is spent on the ridge and not the line, and what a clear pad is worth against what it costs to keep.

phases.name: RESOLUTION - WHAT LANDED
phases.lead: This fight is judged by what could land, not by who is still standing. The flight lands or it diverts. The casualty line clears or it walks out. The ridge is yours or it is a threat hanging over the next night. What the guard left behind on the grass is collected before the column's heavy flights need the clearing.

dataBlock.Pad audit: landings made versus diverted; a hot landing that corked the pad counts against the lift
dataBlock.Casualty lift: {CASUALTY_LIFT} crew off the line, or the count that walked to the secondary
dataBlock.Wreck recovery: fallen challengers' markings name the bidding Cluster - taken before the relief's flights need the pad clear

sidebarKernel.kernel: The lift line as a position: why the wounded's ground is defended like the ridge, and what a scrubbed medevac costs the company that has to hold another night.

skeleton: an under-manned frontier post with no relief and no retreat survives an overwhelming night assault by rehearsedly trading its outer wall for time - contracting wave by wave into pre-built inner redoubts - so it still exists at the attacker's dawn withdrawal hour, spending ground as the currency that buys the survival of the column sheltering in its lee.
inspiration: the night defence of the mission station at Rorke's Drift, 1879 - a tiny garrison outlasts an overwhelming night assault by abandoning an over-long wall for a barricaded inner redoubt.
title: OPERATION LAST WATERLINE
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The post is a walled compound on a dry riverbed at the edge of the hardpan — a water-cracking and communications-relay station, with blast-berms and earthwork defenses where a river once ran, the last permanent structure for ninety kilometers in any direction. {EMPLOYER} hired your detachment to hold it, and for three weeks that meant logging dust storms and rationing coolant. Tonight it means survival. {COLUMN_SOULS} displaced civilians — a column that outran a Blakist sweep two districts away — reached the station at dusk and now shelter behind it, and the {TARGET_FACTION} assault force that drove them here is forming up on the dust plain to the south. {NPC:intel-source} estimates the attacker at {ATTACKER_WEIGHT} times the post's combat weight — fanatics who do not fight the way a professional force does. They attack in successive waves, climbing over their own dead, and they do not stop just because they are losing. The relay went dead at last light, jammed or cut, it makes no difference. No message is getting out, and no relief is coming until the sector network comes back up or the dawn patrol rides out. Neither will happen before morning. You have {DAWN_HOURS} hours of darkness to survive. You cannot hold the entire wall, because the outer compound is too long a perimeter for the troops you have. What you can do is what the post was quietly built for: give up the outer wall on purpose, on your own terms, and fall back through {REDOUBT_LINES} prepared inner positions, trading ground for time, until the attacker's own deadline forces it to retreat off the open plain before daylight catches it there. Survival here is not measured in ground held. It is measured by one thing: whether the post still stands at first light. The civilians sheltering behind it live or die on that single fact, and the order in which you give up each wall is what decides it. The defenses are dug, the inner positions are laid out, the night-vision batteries are charged. What is not yet decided is which wall you give up first, and when, and whether the people behind the last one are still alive when the plain empties at dawn.

objectives.primary: The post must still stand at the attacker's dawn withdrawal hour: at least one prepared inner redoubt held, with the civilians sheltering behind it unharmed.
objectives.secondary: Keep the rear arc completely clear. No fire, friendly or enemy, reaches the civilians sheltering behind the post.
objectives.bonus: Recover an attacker's marker or prisoner that pins down the assault's staging point for {NPC:intel-source}.

complications.name: No Word Out
complications.text: The relay went down at last light and stays down. No call for help reaches the sector net, no one outside the wire knows the post is even engaged, and nothing - no flight, no patrol, no reinforcement - is coming before the dawn patrol's scheduled ride. The post fights the whole night on exactly what is inside its walls.
complications.mechanicalEffect: No reinforcement of any kind arrives before the dawn hard deadline; the defender fights the entire engagement with its starting force and stores, with no off-map support possible.

complications.name: The Column Behind the Wall
complications.text: {COLUMN_SOULS} displaced civilians shelter behind the post, packed against the rear wall with nowhere else to go. Any fire into the rear arc, any blaze that spreads from a sally, any redoubt overrun from behind, falls on them. The rear of the post must stay a no-fire zone, and there is no way around that.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The rear quarter of the post is a no-fire zone. Any area-effect, building-collapse, or incendiary damage there triggers an immediate employer-standing penalty and ends bonus-objective eligibility.

complications.name: An Enemy That Spends Itself
complications.text: The attacker takes casualties no professional force would, coming on in waves over its own dead, ignoring losses that would break a mercenary command twice over. It does not falter, it does not pause to regroup, and it does not negotiate. It simply comes again.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The attacker does not test morale until it is very heavily reduced. Waves arrive on a fixed schedule tied to the dark hours regardless of losses, each aimed at the weakest point in your line, not the strongest.

complications.name: Powder and Light
complications.text: Ammunition and night-optic batteries both limit the fight. Firing at every shadow on the plain drains both long before dawn, and the last waves are the heaviest. Spend your ammunition and power too early and you fight the worst of the night half-blind and short of rounds.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track a shared endurance pool. Sustained fire above a set rate drains it, and once it is spent the final waves are fought at reduced effective range and with night-optic-blind penalties.

decisionPoints.name: The First Breach
decisionPoints.context: The first wave reaches the outer wall's south face, and that wall will not hold all night. The compound is too long a line to keep, and what you do at this first breach shapes every fallback after it: hold the wall, give it up on your terms, or hit the wave before it lands.

options.title: Hold the Outer Wall
advantages: Maximum distance from the enemy. The killing ground in front of the wall is at its widest
The civilians behind the post are farthest from the fighting while the wall holds
disadvantages: The outer line is too long to hold against this weight. A rush that carries it catches your reserve in the open
If the wall is taken before you choose to give it up, the fallback turns into a rout
options.consequence: You keep the widest buffer for as long as the wall holds. But a wall taken by storm, rather than given up on your terms, scatters your people across open ground with the redoubt not yet manned.

costs.resource: the reserve committed forward to a line that cannot be held
costs.risk: A wall stormed instead of given up on your terms turns an orderly fallback into a rout in the dark

options.title: Give the Outer, Fight the Inner
advantages: A timed, covered withdrawal into the first redoubt while the line is still intact
Shorter firing lines you can actually hold, with the reserve free behind them
disadvantages: You give up the outer stores, the outer wounded, and the buffer distance
Firing lines collapse to close range, where the attacker's numbers count for most
options.consequence: You survive deeper into the night on a line you can hold, but at the cost of everything left in the outer compound and a fight fought at the range that favors the wave.

costs.resource: the outer compound given up: stores, wounded, and buffer distance
costs.risk: At close range, {ATTACKER_WEIGHT}-to-one stops being a number on paper and becomes a press you cannot shoot your way out of

options.title: Sally and Burn
advantages: A quick strike burns the attacker's staging area and their siege rams before the wave fully forms
Breaks the wave rhythm and buys a wave's worth of time to fall back
disadvantages: The strike element is outside the wall, where the wave can surround it
Your tiny mobile reserve is the only thing that can make the strike, and also the only thing that can plug a breach
options.consequence: If the strike burns the staging area, the next wave comes in disordered and late. If it is cut off outside the wall, the post fights the night with no reserve at all.

costs.resource: the mobile reserve risked outside the wall
costs.risk: A reserve cut off in the open is a reserve you do not have when the redoubt's gate is rushed

decisionPoints.name: The Inner Door
