decisionPoints.context: The second fallback is on you. The first redoubt is no longer holding, and the inner line is the next wall back. How you close on the redoubt decides whether it becomes a fort or a trap: sealed tight, held open, or covered by fire behind you.

options.title: Seal the Redoubt
advantages: Maximum protection. The redoubt is shut and fought from inside its earthworks
The civilians behind the post are fully behind the sealed line
disadvantages: You give up the last of the outer wounded and any stores not already inside
Firing lines drop to point-blank, and there is no recovering anyone left outside the door
options.consequence: The redoubt becomes a hard shell that holds, but anyone and anything not inside when it seals is gone, and the fight is now at the range where numbers decide.

costs.resource: the last outer wounded and stores, sealed out
costs.risk: A sealed redoubt that is breached has nowhere further to fall back to. It is the last wall, by choice

options.title: Hold the Gate Open for Counterattacks
advantages: The reserve can strike back and recover wounded through an open gate
The post can still break up a forming wave, not just absorb it
disadvantages: The open gate is the weak point every determined rush aims for
Holding it open ties the reserve down to guard it
options.consequence: You keep the ability to recover people and break up waves, but you have built your weakest point into your last wall, and the attacker can spot an open gate.

costs.resource: the reserve tied to guarding the open gate
costs.risk: An open gate rushed at the wrong moment puts the wave inside the last redoubt with the civilians

options.title: Fire the Outer Compound Behind You
advantages: Denies the attacker the cover and staging room of the abandoned compound
The line of fire buys a wave's delay while it burns across
disadvantages: The smoke and heat blind your own night optics as badly as theirs
A fire in the dry-riverbed compound can spread to the civilians' shelter if the wind turns
options.consequence: The attacker loses its covered approach for a crucial stretch, but you fight the next wave half-blind, and a shift in the wind puts the civilians' shelter at risk from the fire you set.

costs.resource: your own night-optic visibility, traded for the attacker's cover
costs.risk: A fire that spreads into the rear arc does to the civilians exactly what the no-fire rule was meant to prevent

entries.event: Alarm. The first wave crosses the dust plain against the outer wall's south face; the relay goes silent in the same minute - no word out, none coming.
The outer wall's south face is breached or no longer holdable. The choice to hold it or give it up on your terms must be made now.
The second wave commits against the breach. The reserve is the only thing that can re-seal it or cover a fallback into the first redoubt.
The inner redoubt must be fully manned by now, or the next wave carries the gap into the compound's center and the rear arc.
Heaviest wave. The attacker throws everything at the redoubt. The civilians behind the post are one collapse away from the fighting.
The attacker's withdrawal deadline. It must clear the open plain before first light. If the redoubt holds, the wave breaks off. If it has been carried, the post and the civilians are lost.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The inner redoubt must still be held at T+40:00, the hour the attacker must break off to clear the open plain before the dawn patrol. Miss that and it is carried in the dark, and the {COLUMN_SOULS} civilians sheltering behind the post are lost with it. Survival is measured by still existing at that minute, not by ground held.

opforSketch.composition: A Blakist assault wave the weight of a reinforced battalion, COMBINED_ARMS: a screen of light-medium 'Mechs (20-50 tons), Regular-to-Veteran and fanatical, fronted and flanked by light combat vehicles (hover and wheeled, roughly 0.3 of the weight) pinning the wall, plus a mass of fanatic infantry that fills out every wave but is not the killing edge. No aerospace; the night and the blackout are their cover.
opforSketch.behavior: It spends itself freely: it comes on in wave after wave over its own dead, ignoring losses, on a fixed schedule tied to the dark hours. It does not test morale until very heavily reduced. It aims each wave at a weak point (a breach, a gate, the rear arc) rather than the strongest face. It breaks off only at its withdrawal deadline, never at a set damage level. Until first light forces it off the plain, it does not stop coming.

forks.name: OPERATION FIRST LIGHT
forks.trigger: Redoubt held, the outer compound retaken or never lost, the civilians intact, and a prisoner or marker taken.
forks.consequence: The dawn patrol arrives to find the post still standing. The civilians move on, and the intelligence on where the assault came from sends your command to find the staging point before the next nightfall. It is a RECON_RAID onto the plain the wave came off.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND NIGHT
forks.trigger: The redoubt held, but the outer compound and its stores were lost, or the post took heavy losses.
forks.consequence: The attacker withdrew at dawn and will be back the next night, now that it knows the post's true strength. Your command holds a battered post another night, with resupply uncertain and the civilians still sheltering behind it. It is GARRISON_DUTY continued, at raised threat.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN WALL
forks.trigger: The redoubt was carried, or the fighting reached the civilians.
forks.consequence: The survivors must break out of the overrun post and guide what is left of the civilian column across open ground to the dawn patrol's line. It is a fighting withdrawal with civilians in tow, escorting them with the enemy in pursuit.

storyElementSeed: Between waves a trooper refills the night-optic batteries from a hand-cranked charger and counts the turns aloud, because the count is the only clock anyone trusts; when the cranking stops, the whole redoubt notices before the next wave does.

is-marik.objectives.primary: The post stands at dawn or the parliament asks why a Free Worlds station was left this thin. At least one inner redoubt held, the column in its lee whole - that is the report, and the provincial levy at the wall will be remembered by name either way.

comstar.objectives.primary: The post endures to first light: one redoubt held, the flock in its lee unbroken. The relay is silent but the watch is not; the dawn that finds the post standing is the answer logged in clear to a prayer no one outside heard sent.

REDOUBT_LINES.unit: pre-built inner positions to fall back through

COLUMN_SOULS.unit: displaced civilians sheltering behind the post

resourceGates.lackingText: Without a prepared base, the sally goes out cold: no incendiary staged in advance and no rehearsed exit gate. So the strike costs an extra wave's worth of exposure to form up, and the reserve is outside the wall longer.

phases.name: POSTURE - THE DRY WATERCOURSE
phases.lead: Three weeks of dust and coolant logs end the evening the civilian column arrives ahead of the sweep that drove it. The work now is the fallback nobody wanted to rehearse, settled before the plain to the south starts moving: which wall is given up first, where each inner line is manned from, and how the civilians behind the post are kept out of every line of fire.

dataBlock.The post: walled compound on a dry riverbed, blast-berms and {REDOUBT_LINES} prepared inner redoubts, last fixed structure for 90km
dataBlock.The civilians: {COLUMN_SOULS} displaced people sheltering behind the post - the no-fire zone
dataBlock.The night: {DAWN_HOURS} hours of darkness; no relief before the dawn patrol
dataBlock.The wall: outer compound too long to hold; survival means falling back, not standing off

phases.protocol: The fallback is run by codeword, not by sight, because no one will see the whole wall once it starts. EBB sends the outer line back into the first redoubt on a timed withdrawal. SLACK WATER seals the inner door. The rear arc is a no-fire zone on every fire-control set: any station that aims into it is corrected by name on the net before it fires. Ammunition and battery power are reported as one endurance figure every half hour, so no wall is given up for lack of light no one knew was gone.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Why a post is built to be given up in pieces: how the inner redoubts are sited so each shorter line is harder than the last, and which wall is designed to be lost first.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT - WAVE OVER WAVE
phases.lead: The assault is less a battle than a tide that will not go out until its own deadline makes it. The hard hour is T+40:00, when the attacker must clear the open plain before the dawn patrol. The post's whole task is to still be a post at that minute, giving up walls inward to get there.

dataBlock.Outer wall: south face breached by T+6:00; the hold-or-give-up choice is forced there
dataBlock.Inner redoubt: must be fully manned by T+20:00 or the gap reaches the compound's center
dataBlock.Heaviest wave: T+30:00, aimed at the weak point nearest the rear arc
dataBlock.Withdrawal deadline: T+40:00 - the attacker breaks off to clear the plain, or the redoubt is carried in the dark

sidebarKernel.kernel: Spending ground to buy time in the right order: why giving up a wall too early wastes your buffer and giving it up too late loses the reserve, and how the rhythm of the waves tells you which.

phases.name: RESOLUTION - WHAT STOOD AT DAWN
phases.lead: First light empties the plain and grades the night by one question: is the post still here. The redoubt held or it did not. The civilians behind the post are whole or they are not. What the attacker left on the approach, in its rush to clear the open ground, is collected before the dust and the heat take it.

dataBlock.The count: redoubts still held; the survivors against the {COLUMN_SOULS} civilians who sheltered
dataBlock.The compound: outer stores and wounded recovered or written off in the abandoned ring
dataBlock.Recovery window: markers and fallen left on the approach name the staging point - taken at first light, before the heat ruins the evidence

sidebarKernel.kernel: Treating a night fought at knife-range between waves: triage with no evacuation, and why the aid point moves inward with every contraction instead of staying put.

skeleton: a road-bound relief column must fight up a single mountain road through the layered ambush belts of a closing encirclement to reach a cut-off garrison whose own perimeter clock runs out faster than the column can safely advance - spending speed against security at each belt while the ring closes behind it on the only road home.
inspiration: the fighting relief and breakout along the Chosin Reservoir road, 1950 - a column forces successive blocking positions on a single mountain road to reach a cut-off force on a hard weather-and-attrition clock.
title: OPERATION COLD SWITCHBACK
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The road is the whole problem. {ROAD_KM} kilometers of single switchback track climb from the valley floor to the pass town where {EMPLOYER}'s garrison has been cut off for two days — one lane of frozen scree with a cliff on one side and a drop on the other, the only all-weather route to the head of the pass and the only way a relief force can reach the garrison before it is overrun. The {TARGET_FACTION} raiding force that cut the road did not just block it; it built prepared ambush positions on the switchbacks, sited and pre-ranged, and it is tightening a ring around the garrison's hill on a timetable everyone can see. {NPC:intel-source} counts {AMBUSH_BELTS} ambush belts between your column and the garrison, each designed to bleed you rather than stop you outright — cheap armor dug in to pin the column in place while the raiders' 'Mechs fire down into the killing ground from the high ground above. The garrison reports it can hold {GARRISON_HOURS} hours at the current rate of losses, no longer; {GARRISON_HOLDOUTS} effectives are left on the hill, low on ammunition and even lower on cover. The math tonight is cruel and simple: your column cannot move fast and stay safe at the same time. Force your way through an ambush belt and you save time, but you pay in wrecks and wounded you cannot recover on a road with no shoulder. Clear a belt carefully and your column survives, but the careful hours are hours the garrison does not have. On top of that, the pass head is far colder than 'Mechs and vehicles can sit idle in safely. Stay stopped too long while clearing an ambush and your joints stiffen and your fuel thickens, so even standing still costs you. And the ring is closing behind you as you climb, which means the road you came up may not be the road you leave by. You are not racing the enemy's strength. You are racing the garrison's clock — and every cautious choice that keeps your column alive spends time the people you came to save do not have. Your start line is the valley floor. The garrison is at the top. Between them is a road built for ore trucks that is about to decide the fate of a sector.

objectives.primary: Reach fighting contact with the garrison's hill before its perimeter folds, and break the inner ring enough to join the garrison to the column.
objectives.secondary: Keep the road home open - at least one viable route back down the pass not closed by the ring.
objectives.bonus: Recover the garrison's wounded and its intelligence cache intact on the way out.

complications.name: The Garrison's Clock
complications.text: The cut-off garrison can hold {GARRISON_HOURS} hours at the current rate, and not one more. Every hour the column spends deploying to clear a belt rather than driving through it is an hour off that figure, and the garrison does not get a vote on how the column spends its time.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A running garrison-clock advances each turn; methodical choices (clear, flank) advance it faster than bulling through. At zero the garrison's outer perimeter folds and the mission shifts toward breakout.

complications.name: Cold Soak
complications.text: The pass head is far colder than any 'Mech or vehicle is rated to sit idle in. Standing still to clear an ambush bleeds heat out of the joints and thickens the fuel. A unit that stands too long stiffens up, and a cold vehicle may not restart on the first try.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A unit stationary for more than a set number of turns takes a movement and startup penalty on its next activation. Combat vehicles roll a cold-start check after a long halt, and on a failure they lose their next move.

complications.name: The Belt Behind the Belt
complications.text: The ambush belts are layered. Reduce the one you can see and the raiders' depth position - sited after they watched where a relief force would naturally bypass - opens on the very route you chose to flank by. The obvious way around is the way they planned for.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each flank choice carries a chance the flanking route is covered by a depth ambush placed by the gamemaster after deployment; a flank that walks into it loses the detached element's surprise and a march-turn.

complications.name: Wrecks on the Single Road
complications.text: The road is one lane of frozen scree with a cliff above and a drop below and no shoulder anywhere. A knocked-out 'Mech or vehicle on a switchback corks the column behind it, and nothing passes until the wreck is shoved clear - which on this grade is its own slow, exposed job.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A destroyed unit on a road hex blocks it; the column's tail cannot pass until the wreck is pushed clear, which takes a recovery unit a set number of turns under whatever fire still reaches the road.

decisionPoints.name: The First Belt
decisionPoints.context: The lead element rounds a switchback into the first ambush belt - dug-in armor across the road, the raiders' 'Mechs above on the high ground, the killing ground pre-ranged. The garrison's clock is running. What you do here you will do again at the next belt, and the next, but the first one sets the column's habit.

options.title: Bull Through
advantages: Keeps the garrison's clock - the column drives through and does not stop
Denies the belt the time it was built to take from you
disadvantages: You take the hits the belt is designed to deal, full in the killing ground
Wrecks and wounded are left on a road with no shoulder and no recovery
options.consequence: You reach the next belt with the clock intact but the column bled, and whatever you lost in the killing ground stays there - including a wreck that may cork the road for your own tail.

costs.resource: the column's strength - casualties taken in the killing ground, unrecovered
costs.risk: A unit killed mid-belt on the single road corks the column at the worst possible point

options.title: Clear It
advantages: The belt is reduced and the column passes intact, recovering its own
The road behind is clean for the tail and for any route home
disadvantages: The methodical hours come straight off the garrison's clock
A halted column at the pass head soaks cold into every machine that stops
options.consequence: You pass whole and unbled, but the garrison's margin shrinks by every hour the reduction takes, and the cold settles into the column while it works.

costs.resource: garrison-clock hours, spent on a careful reduction
costs.risk: A column stationary in the cold-soak stiffens; the garrison that runs out of hours while you clear is on you

options.title: Flank It
advantages: A detached element works around the belt and avoids the killing ground entirely
If it gets behind the belt, the dug-in armor is taken from a side it cannot face
disadvantages: The column is split on a road where the ring is already closing
The obvious bypass may be exactly where the raiders sited their depth position
options.consequence: The belt is unhinged if the flank lands clean; if the bypass is covered, you have a detached element in trouble off the road and a column waiting on a clock for it to rejoin.

costs.resource: the column split - a detachment off the road, the main body halted to await it
costs.risk: A flank into a depth ambush loses the detachment's surprise and may lose the detachment, on a closing ring

decisionPoints.name: The Ring Behind You
decisionPoints.context: Partway up the pass the ring closes across the road behind the column, cutting the route home. The garrison is still above you and still on its clock. What you do about the threat at your back changes how much force you can throw at the ring ahead.

options.title: Push On Regardless
advantages: The full weight of the column goes into reaching the garrison before its clock runs out
No strength taken off the force that has to break the inner ring
disadvantages: The route home closes behind you - the column may be trapped inside the ring with the garrison
A relief force that becomes a second cut-off force has saved no one
options.consequence: You maximize the chance of reaching the garrison in time, and accept that if you do, you may both have to break out together down a road the ring now owns.

costs.resource: the route home, left to close behind you
costs.risk: Two forces inside the ring instead of one, and a breakout to fight on the way down

options.title: Detach a Rearguard
advantages: The back door is held open - a viable route home is kept against the ring
The garrison, once reached, has somewhere to be extracted to
disadvantages: The rearguard is weight off the force that must break the inner ring
The detached element fights its own battle out of supporting range of the main body
options.consequence: You keep an exit at the cost of the strength you reach the garrison with. The inner ring is broken with a lighter force, or not broken at all.

costs.resource: a detachment held back to keep the road home open
costs.risk: A force too light to break the inner ring leaves the garrison unrelieved with the clock at zero

options.title: Call the Garrison Out to Meet You
advantages: Halves the distance and the clock - the garrison fights toward you instead of waiting
Two forces converging can crack a belt from both sides
disadvantages: A cut-off garrison breaking cover into the open is fragile and low on everything
If the timing slips, the garrison is caught in the open between you and the ring
options.consequence: The linkup comes faster if both halves time it, but a garrison that leaves its perimeter early is exposed in the open with nothing to fall back to if the column is late.

costs.resource: the garrison's perimeter, abandoned to make the meeting
costs.risk: A mistimed sortie leaves the garrison caught between the column and the ring with no cover left

entries.event: Step-off. The column crosses the line of departure onto the single road; the cut-off garrison reports it can hold {GARRISON_HOURS} hours at the current rate, no longer.
The first ambush belt opens from the switchback above; the lead element is in the killing ground and the speed-or-security choice is forced now.
The ring closes across the road behind the column's tail; the route home is now contested.
The next belt - or a depth position - engages on the approach to the garrison's hill; the garrison clock is past half.
The garrison's outer perimeter folds to the inner ring; if the column is not in fighting contact with the hill by now, the linkup becomes a breakout.
Garrison clock zero: the inner ring is carried unless the column has broken through to it.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The column must be in fighting contact with the garrison's hill by T+42:00 - when the outer perimeter folds - or there is no garrison left to relieve and the mission inverts to breaking two bled forces back out through a ring that has closed behind them.

opforSketch.composition: A raiding force the weight of a reinforced company-plus holding the road, COMBINED_ARMS: light-medium 'Mechs (25-55 tons) sited as the ambush belts' killing element at Regular quality, fronted by cheap light combat vehicles and dug-in armor (roughly 0.3 of the weight) whose job is to fix and bleed the column, not to win it. A separate fast element closes the ring behind the column. No aerospace; the weather and the pass walls are the ambush's cover.
opforSketch.behavior: The raiders fight to bleed and delay, not to stop the column dead: the belts are built to cost you time and tonnage, trading cheap armor for the relief clock. Each belt fights from prepared, pre-ranged positions and withdraws up the next switchback rather than be pinned down. The ring element presses the road behind to force the column to choose between its garrison and its exit. A belt breaks off when it has bought its time, not when it is beaten.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN ROAD
forks.trigger: Linkup made before the clock, the belts broken, the road home held, and the garrison and its wounded extracted.
forks.consequence: The pass is open. The column turns on the now-exposed ring element to break it before it can relocate and cut the road again - an OBJECTIVE_RAID with a short window before the raiders go to ground.

forks.name: OPERATION HARD LINKUP
forks.trigger: The garrison was reached, but the road home closed behind, or the column arrived too bled to break the inner ring cleanly.
forks.consequence: Both forces are now inside the ring and must break out together up a contested road - the relief becomes a fighting withdrawal, the garrison's survivors and the column's wounded all to bring down the pass.

forks.name: OPERATION GRAVEYARD WATCH
forks.trigger: The column arrived to a garrison already overrun, or could not break through before the clock ran out.
forks.consequence: Recover what can still be recovered - survivors, wounded, the garrison's dead and its intelligence cache - and withdraw down a road the ring now owns: an EXTRACTION_RAID under pursuit, the clock now running on getting out instead of in.

storyElementSeed: At a halt the column commander walks the line and finds the lead driver chipping ice off a viewport with a ration spoon; neither says anything about the garrison's clock, but the spoon stops and the engine note comes up a quarter-turn before the order to move is given.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Reach the garrison and join it to the column - and account for every machine you spend doing it, because the recovery bill and the fuel burned on this grade are the part of the after-action the House actually reads. A wreck left to cork the road is a wreck charged twice.

merc.objectives.primary: The bond pays on a relieved garrison, not a heroic try - reach the hill before the clock and break enough of the inner ring to link up. Read the contract's recovery clause before you leave a single chassis on that road; the salvage you abandon is salvage you bought.

AMBUSH_BELTS.unit: prepared ambush belts on the road

GARRISON_HOURS.unit: hours the cut-off garrison can hold

ROAD_KM.unit: kilometers of single road to the garrison

GARRISON_HOLDOUTS.unit: effectives still holding the garrison hill

resourceGates.lackingText: Without forward depot access the column carries its own recovery and spare ammunition up the grade: a methodical reduction runs slower and the cold-soak penalty bites harder, because the recovery gear that should be staged forward is back in the valley.

phases.name: POSTURE - THE LINE OF DEPARTURE
phases.lead: The column forms on the valley floor in the dark and the cold, and the briefing is short because the road allows nothing else. What is settled here is the column's habit at a belt - the order of march, who clears and who recovers, and the one figure that governs everything: the garrison's hours against the road's kilometers.

dataBlock.The road: {ROAD_KM}km single switchback, frozen scree, cliff above and drop below, no shoulder
dataBlock.The belts: {AMBUSH_BELTS} prepared ambush belts, armor below and 'Mechs above, pre-ranged
dataBlock.The clock: garrison holds {GARRISON_HOURS} hours; {GARRISON_HOLDOUTS} effectives left on the hill
dataBlock.The cold: pass head below cold-soak baseline; every long halt stiffens the column

phases.protocol: The column runs on two words because the road will not allow a conference. PUSH commits the lead through a belt at speed and the tail follows close to keep the cork from forming; ANVIL halts the column and deploys to reduce, recovery forward. The garrison clock is read on the net at every switchback, plain numbers, so no one spends an hour clearing without hearing what it cost. A cold-start failure is called by vehicle, not waited on - the column does not stop in the killing ground for one machine that would not turn over.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The grade and the cold as a logistics problem: what a long halt costs in cold-soak and fuel, and why the recovery vehicle's position in the order of march decides whether a wreck corks the road.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT - BELT BY BELT
phases.lead: The climb is a sequence of the same decision under a clock that does not stop - bull, clear, or flank, at each belt, while the ring closes behind. The hard line is fighting contact with the garrison's hill by T+42:00, before its perimeter folds; everything the column spends on the way up is measured against that minute.

dataBlock.First belt: opens T+8:00 from the switchback above; lead element in the killing ground
dataBlock.Ring closure: T+18:00 - the road home contested behind the column's tail
dataBlock.Approach belt: T+30:00 on the run-in to the garrison's hill; clock past half
dataBlock.Perimeter fold: T+42:00 - outer perimeter to the inner ring; after this, linkup becomes breakout

routes.name: GRADE
routes.desc: Straight up the ore road through each belt, switchback by switchback.
routes.tradeoff: The only route the whole column can take together, and every belt is built to be met on it - speed here is paid in the killing ground.

routes.name: SCREE
routes.desc: A detached element off the road across the frozen scree to turn a belt's flank.
routes.tradeoff: Avoids the prepared killing ground, but the scree is slow, it splits the column on a closing ring, and the obvious bypass is where the depth ambush waits.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Reading a bleed-and-delay belt: how to tell armor meant to stop you from armor meant only to cost you time, and why the second kind wants you to clear it carefully.

phases.name: RESOLUTION - THE WAY DOWN
phases.lead: Whether the column reached the garrison or not, the pass has a second half - the road down, which the ring has been closing the whole climb. The fight that began as a relief is graded on what comes back off the mountain, and the garrison's clock has handed off to the column's.

dataBlock.Linkup state: in contact with the hill by T+42:00, or the garrison's perimeter already folded
dataBlock.The road home: at least one route down not closed by the ring - or a breakout to fight for one
dataBlock.Recovery: garrison wounded and intelligence cache extracted, or written off to the hill

sidebarKernel.kernel: Clearing the road under fire: what it takes to shove a wreck off a switchback with a drop on one side, and why the recovery crew is the most important element on the mountain on the way down.

skeleton: an encircled hub's relief has exactly one viable break-in lane that runs through the player company's perimeter slice, so the sector must stay holdable from both sides at once - bleeding inward against the ring while keeping the outward lane open for a relief whose arrival hour the holder cannot control
inspiration: an encircled road-hub is held in a ring while an armoured column fights to break in, and the one sector that decides everything is the shoulder the relief must come through - held inward and outward at once.
title: OPERATION OPEN SHOULDER
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. Seven paved roads meet in one upland town, and in deep winter they are the only roads in the sector that can bear heavy weight — every other track is buried in snow to the axles. Whoever holds the junction can move freely; whoever loses it is reduced to walking pace. A {TARGET_FACTION} attack drove past the town in the first week and closed a ring around it from behind. The friendly battalion garrisoning the place is now surrounded, dug into a perimeter it cannot extend, living off whatever was in its supply depots when the ring closed — {AMMO_DAYS} days of ammunition at the current rate of fire, and that rate is not dropping. Relief is coming, but it is distant: an armored column is fighting its way up the one southern highway against the same snow and the same ring, and {NPC:intel-source} estimates it cannot arrive for {RELIEF_WINDOW_DAYS} days. {EMPLOYER} assigns your command — {FORCE_SIZE} — to the southwest sector: {SHOULDER_KM} kilometers of perimeter straddling the southern highway. This is the section of the line the relief column must break in through, and it is the one sector that has to defend in two directions at once. Facing inward, you hold against an enemy ring that probes your line on {RING_AXES} approaches. It treats the southwest as the weak point exactly because it is the relief's way in. Facing outward, you must keep that opening wide enough, and the highway approach firm enough, that an armored column arriving cold and badly mauled can force the last few kilometers into your line instead of breaking against a closed gate. The besieger's pre-ranged tracked guns can drop artillery onto the cleared roads at will. Off the roads, the snow swallows all movement. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands the ring and is in no hurry. The town will run out of ammunition long before it runs out of will, and the relief can be beaten on the very day it arrives if the southwest sector is sealed shut for even one hour at the right moment. The town does not fall when the perimeter is breached somewhere. It falls when the southwest sector is sealed shut on the day the relief arrives. Hold the opening. Count your rounds. The column is coming on a schedule no one inside the ring controls, including you.

objectives.primary: Keep the southwest break-in lane open. A blocking position must hold the mouth of the lane, with the highway approach firm, when the relief column arrives, so the column can break in instead of breaking against a closed gate.
objectives.secondary: Hold the sector's share of the perimeter. Let no enemy breakthrough reach the mouth of the lane, and do not let the garrison's shared ammunition drop below what the relief window requires.
objectives.bonus: Locate and pin down the besieger's pre-ranged guns on the cleared roads by tracking their fire, so the relief does not run its break-in blind into those kill zones.

complications.name: The Timed Push
complications.text: The besieger does not assault on a schedule of his own - he assaults on the relief's. His net traffic spikes whenever the column is reported close, and his heaviest direct-assault echelon shifts onto the shoulder precisely in the window the relief is expected. The day the relief is nearest is the day the shoulder is hit hardest.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On the turn the relief enters the map, the attacker gains an additional assault wave against the shoulder and a +1 to-hit reduction from pre-registered fire on the lane mouth; the defender that has not pre-positioned a blocking force eats both.

complications.name: Counting the Rounds
complications.text: The garrison shares one depot, and the fight for your sector burns the most ammunition of any part of the perimeter. Every turn of sustained fire to hold the seam draws from a reserve the whole town lives on, and that reserve does not refill until the ring is broken.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Sustained fire draws down a shared ammunition track. Once it crosses a threshold, all units roll each turn for running out of ammo, and a unit that runs out fights with melee and its remaining energy weapons only until the lane is reopened.

complications.name: The Snow Clock
complications.text: Deep snow slows the relief and funnels everything onto the cleared roads - which are exactly where the besieger has ranged his guns. The column cannot detour off the hardtop without bogging, and neither can you. The terrain that strands the enemy strands the rescue.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Off-road movement is halved and risks bogging down in the drifts. On-road movement is fast but runs inside the attacker's pre-ranged kill zones: any unit that uses the cleared roads at speed draws artillery on entry.

complications.name: Two Ways At Once
complications.text: The sector must face the ring inward and keep the lane open outward in the same hour. Concentrating to break an inward push leaves the lane mouth thin; holding the lane mouth firm leaves the inward seam to the militia. There is no posture that is strong in both directions.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any turn the company masses toward an inward penetration, the lane mouth is reduced to militia cover and a relief arriving that turn must fight in unsupported; the reverse holds if the company faces outward during an inward assault.

decisionPoints.name: Where the Shoulder Bends
decisionPoints.context: Your company cannot hold {SHOULDER_KM} kilometers of perimeter in strength, keep a wide break-in lane open, and keep a reserve, all at once. You can do two of the three. The militia will take its confidence from which you choose, and the relief will arrive into whatever shape you have set.

options.title: Hold Forward
advantages: The outer junction is held well forward and the lane stays at full width, so the relief breaks in clean and supported
The besieger is fought far enough out that the town center never comes under direct fire
disadvantages: A thin forward line with no depth. One heavy breakthrough reaches the mouth of the lane before a reserve can form
Nothing held back to exploit a stumble by the enemy
options.consequence: The relief gets a wide, clean door if the line holds. If the line is broken anywhere, the break is at the mouth of the lane, with nothing behind it.

costs.resource: militia labor: 4 days of prepared positions dug forward of the line
costs.risk: a thin line with no depth: one heavy breakthrough reaches the mouth of the lane before a reserve can form

options.title: Layered Depth
advantages: A line with depth that can survive. You give up the outer ground, but the inner line cannot be rushed
A real reserve held back to seal a breakthrough
disadvantages: The lane narrows to a single road width, so the relief fights the last two kilometers into the pocket itself
Set the inner line too deep and the relief breaks against it instead of through it
options.consequence: The sector survives almost anything, but the relief earns the last stretch the hard way, and a column already mauled may not have that last stretch left in it.

costs.resource: the lane narrowed to one road width, so the relief fights the last 2 km itself
costs.risk: an inner line set too deep, so the relief breaks against it rather than through it

options.title: Mobile Reserve
advantages: No fixed line to be broken. A roving reserve plugs whichever breakthrough develops
The company answers the threat that actually comes, not the one it guessed at
disadvantages: Nothing is held firm anywhere. The militia have no anchor, and their watch slips
A relief arriving while the reserve is off on the far flank finds the door shut
options.consequence: Flexibility against an unpredictable ring, at the price of an unpredictable door. The relief must arrive when the reserve happens to be back in place.

costs.resource: watch duty doubled: no machine across the sector's width ever fully rests
costs.risk: a relief arriving while the reserve is off on the far flank finds the lane shut

decisionPoints.name: Counting the Rounds
decisionPoints.context: The shared depot holds {AMMO_DAYS} days of fire and the relief is {RELIEF_WINDOW_DAYS} days out, and those two numbers do not leave margin. How the sector spends its ammunition decides whether the town can still fight on the day the door is forced.

options.title: Fire to Hold
advantages: The line never thins - every push answered at range, the seam never reached
Militia confidence holds because the guns never go quiet
disadvantages: The shared depot drains fastest of any sector - the town's reserve goes with the shoulder's
If the relief slips its window the town fights its last day dry
options.consequence: The shoulder is the firmest in the perimeter and the depot is the emptiest; a relief on time wins, a relief late finds empty racks.

costs.resource: shared depot ammunition drawn at full rate - {AMMO_DAYS} days becomes fewer
costs.risk: if the relief slips its window the town fights its final day with empty racks

options.title: Ration the Reserve
advantages: The rounds last past the relief window with margin to spare
A disciplined line cannot be baited into spending itself on probes
disadvantages: Enemy pushes get close before they are broken, and the seam can be infiltrated under the artillery
Higher losses as fights reach close quarters
options.consequence: The ammunition outlasts the wait, but the sector is held closer and bloodier, and the seam is harder to keep sealed.

costs.resource: close-quarters casualties: pushes reach grips before they break
costs.risk: a rationed line lets the seam be infiltrated under the besieger's artillery

options.title: Spend on the Window
advantages: Maximum violence delivered exactly when the besieger throws his timed blow on the relief's day
The reserve is intact for the one engagement that decides the lane
disadvantages: The holding days before the window are run on almost nothing
A push on the wrong day catches the company holding fire it dares not spend early
options.consequence: The decisive day is fought at full weight. Every day before it is held by nerve and by rationing, and a besieger who moves his blow up early catches you saving rounds.

costs.resource: the holding days before the window run on a bare-minimum reserve
costs.risk: a timed blow delivered on the wrong day catches the company deliberately holding fire

entries.event: Picket on the southwest seam reports the ring's tracked guns registering - indirect fire walking onto the cleared roads. The relief lead is reported {RELIEF_WINDOW_DAYS} days out; besieger net traffic spikes.
Probing assault on the shoulder - a reinforced lance tests the seam for depth and reserve. The push reads the line; it does not yet commit.
The relief column is reported within a day's fighting march; the ring's heaviest direct-assault echelon shifts onto the southwest sector.
The timed blow - the besieger throws his main assault at the shoulder to shut the lane before the relief can reach it.
Relief lead elements reach the highway approach to the lane mouth. If the shoulder still holds a blocking position, the column punches in; if not, it breaks against a closed gate.
Last chance for a break-in. Beyond this the relief runs out of steam short of the line and pulls back to regroup, and the town's ammunition will not survive a second wait.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: A blocking position must hold the mouth of the lane open when the relief column reaches the highway approach at T+26:00, and no later than T+34:00. Miss that and the relief breaks against a closed sector and the garrison's ammunition runs to zero before a second attempt. The primary objective fails from running dry, not from assault.

opforSketch.composition: A besieging force tightening the ring on the southwest seam: a reinforced company-plus of medium-to-heavy 'Mechs (45-75 tons) at Regular-to-Veteran quality, a battery of tracked assault guns and missile carriers pre-ranged on the cleared roads (the combined-arms weight, roughly 30 percent of the force), and a mechanized infantry contingent for the perimeter-reduction work. No aerospace in the winter overcast beyond occasional spotting. The assaulting echelon breaks off a given push at about 35 percent damage and reconstitutes for the next.
opforSketch.behavior: He reduces the town on the relief's schedule, not his own. He probes the seam, pins the defender with missile-carrier fire, and throws his heaviest assault at the sector in the window the relief is expected, willing to spend a whole wave to shut the lane on the day it matters. He does not pursue if the relief breaks in; instead he withdraws to fight for control of the open road network.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN ROAD
forks.trigger: The lane held open, the relief broke in on time, and the besieger's gun line was fixed and counter-battered.
forks.consequence: The combined force turns outward off the relieved town to break the ring's grip on the road net before the besieger reconstitutes - a PLANETARY_ASSAULT breakout up the cleared highways while the snow still favors whoever holds the roads.

forks.name: OPERATION CLOSED POCKET
forks.trigger: The shoulder was shut on the relief's day, or the shared ammunition ran out before the column reached the lane.
forks.consequence: The relief broke against a closed gate and withdrew; the town is now a pocket with empty racks. Your company fights out of the closing ring before it is reduced - an EXTRACTION_RAID breakout across the snow, leaving what cannot move under power.

forks.name: OPERATION NARROW LANE
forks.trigger: The relief broke in but mauled, through a lane narrowed to a single road, with the sector held at heavy cost.
forks.consequence: The corridor is open but a thread - one cleared road under fire, carrying every ton in and every casualty out. Your command escorts the lifeline traffic up the same shoulder while the besieger works to pinch it shut again - RELIEF_DUTY on a corridor that exists by the hour.

storyElementSeed: A crew chief chalks the day's round count on the back of a road sign at the lane mouth, rubbing out yesterday's number first, and the new one is smaller; a relief that is two days out and a number that is one day smaller do not add up, and everyone reading the sign does the arithmetic without saying it.

merc.objectives.primary: Contract performance is measured at the lane: the break-in clause pays on the column reaching your line through an open door. A shoulder shut when the relief arrives is a failed deliverable regardless of how well the rest of the perimeter held - read which number the auditor counts before you spend the last rounds anywhere else.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: The town is the investment and the relief is the dividend - hold the shoulder so the column can realize it. Keep the door open and the highway shoulder firm; everything spent inside the ring is recovered only when the relief breaks in, and not one round before.

RELIEF_WINDOW_DAYS.unit: days until the armoured relief can break the ring

AMMO_DAYS.unit: days of garrison ammunition at present rate of fire

RING_AXES.unit: axes the besieger can press the southwest seam

SHOULDER_KM.unit: km of perimeter your company holds

resourceGates.lackingText: No district depot access for fortification stores: the inner line is dug with hand tools and salvage - 4 additional days and a weaker position, or 14,000 C-bills for commercial materiel freighted up the contested highway under fire.

phases.name: POSTURE - THE RING SETTLES
phases.lead: The ring shut in the first week and now it tightens by the day. The work before the blow is all numbers. Weigh the round count against the relief clock. Weigh the sector's two-way problem against the militia's nerve. Weigh the cleared roads against the besieger's guns. Do it until the company knows which day will be the day, before anyone fires a shot.

dataBlock.Ammunition: {AMMO_DAYS} days of shared garrison reserve at present rate of fire - the shoulder is the thirstiest sector in the perimeter
dataBlock.Relief window: {RELIEF_WINDOW_DAYS} days out, no sooner, fighting up the one cleared southern highway
dataBlock.Sector: {SHOULDER_KM} km of perimeter astride the highway - the relief's only break-in lane, pressed on {RING_AXES} axes
dataBlock.Roads: Seven hardtop roads bear weight; everything off them is snow to the axles and pre-ranged where it is cleared

phases.protocol: Lane status is passed by landline, not radio, in two words: GATE OPEN means the lane mouth is held to full width and a relief can break in supported; GATE THIN means it is down to militia cover and the column must fight in unsupported. The besieger listens to the net; the wire does not carry. Round-count is reported to the depot officer hourly so the shared reserve is one number the whole town can see.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The two numbers that kill a siege: rounds-on-hand against days-to-relief, and why the sector that holds the door spends the town's reserve fastest - what to ration first when the curves cross before the relief does.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT - THE TIMED BLOW
phases.lead: The besieger assaults on the relief's clock, not his own. When the column is closest the shoulder is hit hardest, and the engagement is arranged around one fact: a blocking position must hold the lane mouth when the relief reaches the approach, or the rescue breaks on a shut gate.

dataBlock.Blocking position: The lane mouth at the highway approach - held to full width, the column breaks in; reduced to militia cover, it breaks against the gate
dataBlock.The window: Heaviest direct assault shifts onto the shoulder from T+14:00; the timed blow lands T+20:00; relief reaches the approach T+26:00
dataBlock.Last break-in: T+34:00 - beyond it the relief runs out of steam short of the line and the town's racks will not survive a second wait
dataBlock.Two-way cost: Massing inward thins the lane mouth that same turn, and the reverse - there is no posture strong in both directions at once

sidebarKernel.kernel: Holding a sector that faces two ways: why the reserve must be committed to the door and not the breach when the relief is on the map, and how to tell the besieger's timed blow from his probe before you spend the round count answering the wrong one.

phases.name: RESOLUTION - THE BREAK-IN
phases.lead: The relief breaks in, or it does not, and the racks are counted either way. What the sector kept - the lane, the gun-line fix, the reserve - decides whether the next mission is a breakout up the open road or a fight out of a closing pocket.

dataBlock.Corridor audit: Lane width at break-in determines whether the relief arrives whole or fights the last 2 km into the pocket alone
dataBlock.Round-count audit: Shared reserve measured at the moment the relief reaches the depot - the secondary objective rides on it not having hit zero
dataBlock.Gun-line fix: Counter-battery plots on the besieger's pre-ranged road guns - the bonus, and the break-in's safe-conduct through the beaten zones

sidebarKernel.kernel: Reading a besieger who times to the relief: what his net-traffic spike and gun-registration pattern reveal about the hour of the blow, and why fixing his gun line is worth more to the break-in than one more day of held line.

skeleton: an outnumbered company trades the whole numerical fight for one defile where width not strength decides - holding the gate frontally is winnable indefinitely, but a single concealed high traverse around the shoulder, if found and turned, makes every hour spent holding the gate the trap that destroys the holders
inspiration: an outnumbered force plugs the one defile an advance must funnel through, where width and not strength decides - until a concealed path around the shoulder, if found and turned, makes every hour at the gate the trap that destroys the holders.
title: OPERATION NARROW GATE
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. A range of rugged mountains cuts across the line of advance, and through it there is exactly one route a 'Mech force can move along at speed: a narrow pass that pinches down to {GATE_WIDTH_M} meters of passable rock at its narrowest point, with walls too steep and broken for a formation to spread out off the road. Every other route means a week of climbing for machines built to fight, not climb. A {TARGET_FACTION} breakthrough force needs this pass, and needs it quickly — behind the mountains a friendly battalion is falling back to fortify a defensive line, and it is not ready yet. {EMPLOYER} orders your command — {FORCE_SIZE} — into the pass as a plug: hold the narrow point for {HOLD_DAYS} days while that line forms, against a force that outnumbers you by more than {ENEMY_OVERMATCH} to one. In the narrows that numerical advantage disappears — only three or four machines can fight side by side, so an outnumbered company can hold a head-on fight there for as long as its armor and ammunition last, because the enemy can only bring a fraction of his strength to bear at any one time. That is the whole tactical logic of the position, and it has exactly one weakness. Somewhere on the high ground above the pass runs a hidden route around it: a herders' track, an old mining road, a ridge a light 'Mech could walk. The enemy's planners have not mapped it yet, but they are actively hunting for it. {NPC:intel-source} reports the enemy has sent out a fast, light element to find it, and a local who knows the high country could sell its location in an afternoon. If they find that route and use it, a flanking force comes down behind your position and the whole situation flips. Your company is trapped in a pass too narrow to turn and fight the other way, cut off, while the line behind you is still forming. {NPC:opfor-commander} knows the head-on fight is a loser and is not really trying to win it — he is using it to pin you in the pass while his climbers search for the way around. The narrows are the most defensible ground on the planet and the high route is the most dangerous, and they are two ends of the same hill. Hold the pass. Watch your own back.

objectives.primary: Hold the defile throat against the breakthrough column for {HOLD_DAYS} days, denying the lane long enough for the interior line behind the range to form.
objectives.secondary: Keep the high traverse screened or denied so the gate is never turned - and extract the company intact into the interior line rather than leaving it cut off in the defile.
objectives.bonus: Identify and map the concealed traverse before the enemy does, so it can be denied permanently rather than merely watched.

complications.name: The Trickle at the Throat
complications.text: Only three or four machines fit abreast in the throat, so the enemy's {ENEMY_OVERMATCH}-to-one weight arrives a handful at a time. The frontal grind is winnable for as long as your armor holds - which is the trap, because the longer the gate holds the more time the climbers have on the traverse.
complications.mechanicalEffect: No more than four attacker 'Mechs may engage across the throat per turn regardless of force size; the rest queue behind. The defender's frontal position is durable, but every turn it holds is a turn added to the flanking element's traverse clock.

complications.name: The Path Someone Sells
complications.text: The traverse is not on the enemy's maps yet. It is in the heads of people who graze and mine the high country, and one of them will trade it for cash, grievance, or fear. The enemy's light element is paying to learn what a local already knows.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll for the traverse's discovery on a rising track each in-game day; a defender who has mapped and screened the path first removes the roll, while a defender who has neglected the high country lets the enemy buy the route and shortens the {TRAVERSE_HOURS}-hour flank clock by a third.

complications.name: Nowhere to Fight Rearward
complications.text: The narrow pass that makes the gate impossible to break from the front makes it a death-trap from behind. There is no room in the throat to turn a wall of 'Mechs around, and a flanking force that reaches the rear can pour fire down the length of a corridor the holders cannot maneuver in.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If an attacker element reaches firing positions behind the gate, the defending 'Mechs at the throat fight with their rear armor exposed and no room to reposition, until they break contact and withdraw, which gives up the gate.

decisionPoints.name: Holding the Throat
decisionPoints.context: Your company has enough machines to wall the gate, or to wall it lighter and cover the high traverse, or to hold a middle posture - not all three. The frontal fight is the one you can see; the traverse is the one that kills you.

options.title: Wall the Gate
advantages: Maximum killing power at the narrowest point - every machine in the wall, the throat negates the enemy's weight
The frontal grind can be held as long as the armor lasts
disadvantages: Nothing covers the high traverse - a turned flank is total and unanswered
No reserve to exploit a stumble in the enemy's frontal echelon
options.consequence: The gate holds against any frontal weight; the entire engagement rides on whether the enemy finds the traverse, which you will not see coming.

costs.resource: the high traverse left unwatched - its discovery is the whole game
costs.risk: a flanking element behind the gate ends the hold in a single turn, with no warning and no answer

options.title: Watch the High Path
advantages: The traverse is screened and any climber is seen and contested early
Warning buys the gate force time to wheel or break before it is cut off
disadvantages: The gate wall is thinned by the detachment - the throat may be forced by weight first
The screen is small and a determined flanking element can brush it aside
options.consequence: Both threats are covered, neither at full strength; the engagement is decided by whether the gate holds the extra weight long enough for the screen to matter.

costs.resource: {ENEMY_OVERMATCH}-to-one at the throat made worse by the detached screen
costs.risk: a thinned wall forced frontally loses the gate before the traverse is ever turned

options.title: Mobile Backstop
advantages: A fast pair can race to whichever shoulder is turned - either threat gets an answer
The gate is still held, lighter, while the reserve stays uncommitted
disadvantages: Neither threat is met at full strength - the backstop is a compromise on both
The race to a turned flank can simply be lost to the {TRAVERSE_HOURS}-hour head start
options.consequence: Flexibility at the cost of decisiveness; the company answers the threat that develops and prays it develops slowly enough to reach.

costs.resource: fuel and coolant for a pair held at constant readiness across the defile
costs.risk: the backstop arrives at the turned shoulder a step late and fights uphill into an established flanking force

decisionPoints.name: The Hour to Break
decisionPoints.context: The gate must hold for {HOLD_DAYS} days, and then the company has to be somewhere other than the throat or the whole stand was a way of dying in place. How you leave the gate matters as much as how you hold it.

options.title: Hold to the Last Hour
advantages: Maximum time bought for the interior line - every hour at the gate is an hour the line digs
The enemy never gets a free advance through an abandoned throat
disadvantages: The longer you hold, the likelier the traverse is turned behind you
A late break runs the gauntlet of a closing flank
options.consequence: The line behind gets its full window; the company gambles that the traverse holds until the last machine is clear.

costs.resource: the company's own margin - the break is run with the flank already closing
costs.risk: an hour too long and the gate is shut behind you with the interior line still forming

options.title: Phased Thinning
advantages: The company peels back machine by machine on a timetable - an orderly, survivable withdrawal
No single catastrophic moment of disengagement under fire
disadvantages: The wall weakens visibly with each machine pulled - the enemy reads it and rushes
Time bought tapers off early as the throat's killing power drops
options.consequence: A clean withdrawal at the cost of the last day's delay; the enemy is through the gate sooner but the company is largely intact.

costs.resource: the final day of delay surrendered to keep the company whole
costs.risk: a thinning wall invites a rush that catches the rearmost machines while they are pulling back

options.title: Pre-Set Demolition Break
advantages: The throat is wired to drop the cut and deny the lane for weeks on a single trigger
A clean break behind a collapsed defile - the enemy must find another route entirely
disadvantages: The charges are a one-shot - a premature blow strands the forward machines on the wrong side
Engineering stores and time to rig, both scarce on a contested frontier
options.consequence: If the timing is right the lane is closed for weeks and the company is clear; if it is wrong, the company seals itself out with the enemy.

costs.resource: engineering stores and 3 days to rig the throat for demolition
costs.risk: a charge blown early strands the forward machines on the enemy's side of the collapse

entries.event: The advance guard reaches the throat and begins the frontal grind; only three or four machines engage abreast across {GATE_WIDTH_M} meters of passable width. Probes feel along both shoulders.
A fast light element detaches from the column and disappears toward the high ground - the hunt for the traverse has begun.
The frontal echelon commits its heavy weight to the throat, accepting attrition to fix the gate force in place.
If the traverse has been found, the flanking element is most of the way along it; a screen on the high path must be in contact by now to deny it.
Earliest a flanking element completes the {TRAVERSE_HOURS}-hour traverse and reaches firing positions behind the gate.
The interior line behind the defile reports the minimum needed to receive a withdrawal; before this the gate force has nowhere prepared to fall back to.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The high traverse must be screened or denied by T+20:00, or a flanking element reaches positions behind the gate at T+28:00 and cuts the holders off in a defile with no width to fight rearward - and the interior line cannot receive a withdrawal until T+34:00, so a flank turned between those hours destroys the company in place.

opforSketch.composition: A breakthrough echelon built to bull a defile: 'Mechs only, weight capped by the throat's width so only three or four engage abreast - heavy and assault 'Mechs (60-90 tons) leading the frontal grind at Veteran quality, plus a detached fast light element (20-40 tons, jump-capable preferred) hunting the high traverse. No vehicles; the broken country and the lane deny them. The frontal element accepts heavy attrition at the throat; the flanking element avoids contact and races the path.
opforSketch.behavior: He fights with two hands at once: pin the gate with weight while the light element finds and clears the traverse, then collapse the position from behind. The frontal grind is only meant to fix you in place, spent freely and not meant to win on its own. The real decision is the flank. He will not break off the gate while the traverse is uncleared, and he presses hardest in the hour the climbers are expected to arrive.

forks.name: OPERATION FORMED LINE
forks.trigger: The gate held the full window, the traverse was denied or mapped and screened, and the company broke clean.
forks.consequence: The interior line is set and the company falls back into it as a known quantity on prepared ground - GARRISON_DUTY on the line the gate bought time to build, the delaying stand converted into a deliberate defense.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN GATE
forks.trigger: The traverse was turned and a flanking force reached the rear before the interior line could receive a withdrawal.
forks.consequence: The company is cut off in the defile with the enemy front and rear and the line behind not yet formed. It fights out through broken country under pursuit - an EXTRACTION_RAID withdrawal that abandons the gate to save the command.

forks.name: OPERATION TRADED GROUND
forks.trigger: The gate held at heavy cost or broke late, with the interior line only partly formed.
forks.consequence: The breakthrough is through the range but behind the tempo it needed, and the company fights a stay-behind covering action through the high country - GUERRILLA_WARFARE trading ridge for ridge to buy the half-built line the days the gate could not.

storyElementSeed: At the throat a tech paints range marks on the rock at a hundred-meter step while the wall above watches the high ground, and someone asks how a machine would even get up there, and the answer is that one already has, somewhere, and is climbing now.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: This is a deliberate trade: a sacrifice at the gate to buy the main body's escape behind the range. Hold the throat the full {HOLD_DAYS} days the line needs. The company is the price of the interior defense, and that price is paid by holding, not by dying for its own sake.

is-marik.objectives.secondary: The traverse is a counterintelligence problem before it is a tactical one - find who in the high country knows the path and deny it at the source. A screen on the ridge treats the symptom; mapping the route first, and finding the seller, denies it permanently.

HOLD_DAYS.unit: days the gate must be held for the interior line to form

ENEMY_OVERMATCH.unit: to-one numerical overmatch the throat negates

TRAVERSE_HOURS.unit: hours a flanking element needs to clear the high path once found

resourceGates.lackingText: No depot access for demolition stores: charges are improvised from salvaged munitions with unreliable yield and a day longer to rig, or 20,000 C-bills for engineered cutting charges freighted to a contested frontier.

phases.name: POSTURE - THE GATE
phases.lead: The defile is the strongest ground on the march and the high traverse is the weakest, and they are the same hill. The work before the column arrives is to read both ends of it - measure the throat, range the rock, and get into the high country before the enemy buys the path that makes the gate a trap.

dataBlock.Throat: {GATE_WIDTH_M} m passable - only 3 to 4 machines abreast, which is how an outnumbered company holds a {ENEMY_OVERMATCH}-to-one fight
dataBlock.Hold required: {HOLD_DAYS} days for the interior line behind the range to form
dataBlock.The traverse: A concealed high path around the shoulder; {TRAVERSE_HOURS} hours to clear once found - and locals can sell it in an afternoon
dataBlock.Rearward: No width in the throat to fight or turn around; a flank reaching the rear can fire down the length of the wall

phases.protocol: Two nets, two words. SHOULDER means a contact on the high traverse - the screen reports it by line if it has one and the gate wall braces to be turned. HOLD FAST means the frontal grind alone, no climbers seen, and the wall fights as deep as it can. The high-path screen reports on a fixed interval whether or not it sees anything, because silence from the ridge is the one report that means the traverse is already lost.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Why the gate's strength is its danger: how a fixing attack at the throat is meant to be lost, and what the enemy's detached light element tells you about how close he is to the path - read the absence of pressure, not just its presence.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT - THE GRIND AND THE CLIMB
phases.lead: Two fights run at once and only one is visible. The throat grinds - durable, bloody, winnable - while somewhere on the shoulder a light element climbs a clock. The deadline is not the gate; it is the traverse, and the gate is held with one eye always behind it.

dataBlock.Frontal clock: Heavy weight commits to the throat from T+12:00; the wall holds as long as armor and ammunition last
dataBlock.Flank clock: Light element detaches T+5:00; the screen must be in contact by T+20:00; the flank arrives rearward by T+28:00
dataBlock.The inversion: A force behind the gate fires down the length of a wall that has no room to turn - the strongest position becomes the death-trap
dataBlock.Fallback: The interior line cannot receive a withdrawal until T+34:00

sidebarKernel.kernel: Fighting forward while watching backward: when to commit the backstop to the ridge instead of the throat, and why the order to break the gate has to be written before the flank is confirmed, not after.

phases.name: RESOLUTION - THE HOUR TO BREAK
phases.lead: The gate was never meant to be held forever - it was meant to be left at the right hour with the company intact and the lane denied behind it. How the throat is given up decides whether the days bought were worth the command that bought them.

dataBlock.Break window: Between the line being ready (T+34:00) and the flank closing (T+28:00) - a withdrawal run inside a window that can invert
dataBlock.Demolition option: The throat dropped closes the lane for weeks but the charges fire once; timing is the whole risk
dataBlock.Mapping the path: The traverse mapped and denied is worth more than the traverse merely watched - the bonus and the next campaign's open flank

sidebarKernel.kernel: What it takes to drop a defile and keep it dropped: where the cut has to be set to deny a lane for weeks rather than days, and why a charge blown one minute early strands the machines it was meant to save.

skeleton: a defender who pre-selected and pre-ranged the battlefield must spend its one husbanded reserve on exactly the right zone, because the assault arrives in honor-bound massed waves it can read but not outnumber, and committing the reserve to the wrong zone forfeits the only edge the chosen ground was supposed to buy
inspiration: a defender pre-selects and pre-ranges the battlefield and fights a massed honor assault zone by zone, and must spend its one husbanded reserve on exactly the right zone - because committing it wrong forfeits the only edge the chosen ground was meant to buy.
title: OPERATION CHOSEN GROUND
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. This invasion does not have to be fought wherever it could land. It can be fought on ground the defender chooses, because the {TARGET_FACTION} driving it is bound by its own honor code to accept a named battlefield and a declared force. So the ground was chosen. Weeks ago, surveyors walked a line of ridges overlooking the only approach worth using, measured and pre-ranged every fold of the terrain, marked out the kill-zones, and fortified the industrial town at the mouth of the corridor. This battle is a proxy fight, and its outcome decides a truce, the pace of the coming season, and whether the world is surrendered or held. {EMPLOYER} has committed to it on the agreed terms. Your command, {FORCE_SIZE}, holds one zone of this chosen ground: a stretch of ridge with {PRE_RANGED_SACKS} pre-ranged kill-zones and a single reserve of {RESERVE_LANCES} lance(s) held back behind it. The rest of the line holds the neighboring zones. The attacker comes in massed waves, {ASSAULT_WAVES} expected in your sector before his committed force is spent, over roughly {BID_HOURS} hours. And he comes predictably, because the Clan honor code binds him: one warrior against one target, escalating in weight wave by wave, with a reserve Star honestly held back from the declared force. {NPC:opfor-commander} fights by that code and expects you to do the same. Your entire advantage is up front and limited: the ground you chose, the fire you pre-ranged, and the one reserve you can commit only once. The question is not whether to hold. It is when to spend your advantage. Commit the reserve to spring a kill-zone and you can break one wave hard, but the next wave hits a zone with nothing behind it. Hold the reserve back for a breakthrough and your prepared ground does less than it could. Feed the reserve in a little at a time and it wears away with nothing to show for it. The honor code itself is also a tool you can use. Fight the one-on-one duels and the battle stays at a pace you can survive but never win. Break the code and concentrate your fire and you can shatter a wave, but then the attacker declares the terms void and commits everything he held back. The ground is yours and measured to the meter. The reserve is yours and you have it only once. Spend both on the right zone at the right moment, or you will hold a perfect position that decides nothing.

objectives.primary: Hold your zone of the chosen ground until the attacker's committed force is spent, keeping the line in your sector unbroken, so the prepared advantage pays off instead of being wasted.
objectives.secondary: Spend the reserve and the kill-zones to real effect: break at least one massed wave hard on the surveyed ground, rather than just enduring the assault.
objectives.bonus: Keep the duel code intact in your sector to the end, so the attacker never gets an honorable reason to commit his held-back reserve Star against the line.

complications.name: The Edge Spends Once
complications.text: Everything that favors you is front-loaded: the ground was chosen weeks ago, the fire was registered weeks ago, the reserve is a single force you commit a single time. Against an enemy you can read but cannot outnumber, every decision is about spending a fixed advantage at the right instant, and a fixed advantage spent at the wrong instant is simply gone.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The reserve may be committed as one decisive action; once engaged it cannot be recalled to another zone. Pre-ranged kill-sacks grant a one-time fire bonus the first time a wave enters them and revert to ordinary ground thereafter.

complications.name: Read But Not Outnumbered
complications.text: The honor code makes the attacker predictable: head-on, one-on-one, heavier wave by wave. That is the only reason a smaller force survives at all. But predictable is not weak. The waves keep coming heavier, and a defender who reads them perfectly still cannot stop the weight unless the chosen ground and the reserve do the work the numbers cannot.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Attacker waves arrive on a known schedule and fight one-on-one, so the defender always knows what comes next. Weight rises each wave, and reading the pattern gives you position but no relief from losses unless a kill-zone or the reserve is spent against it.

complications.name: The Honor Code Is a Lever
complications.text: The honor code is not just the enemy's rule. It is a tool the defender can keep or break. Hold to the one-on-one duels and the attacker keeps his reserve out of the fight and comes at a pace you can survive. Mass your fire to break a wave and he declares the terms void and brings in everything he was honor-bound to leave out. This choice only works in one direction.
complications.mechanicalEffect: While the defender fights by the code, the attacker's held-back reserve Star stays off the board. The first turn the defender masses fire on one target, the attacker is freed from the code and commits the reserve Star and concentrated fire for the rest of the battle. It is a permanent change in terms.

decisionPoints.name: The Reserve
decisionPoints.context: You have {RESERVE_LANCES} lance(s) of reserve and you spend it once. The chosen ground was built to be sprung with it; the breakthrough you fear is the reason to hold it. Both cannot be served, and the attacker is watching to learn which you chose.

options.title: Counterattack in the Kill-Zone
advantages: Springs a pre-ranged kill-zone with the reserve: one wave broken hard on ground you surveyed
A clean local win counts as honorable and rattles the attacker's timing
disadvantages: The reserve is spent, so the next wave hits a zone with nothing behind it
Commit early and a feint can draw the reserve before the real weight arrives
options.consequence: One wave is destroyed in the kill-zone. From that point the zone is held on the line units alone, and the attacker knows your reserve is gone.

costs.resource: the single reserve, {RESERVE_LANCES} lance(s), spent in one blow
costs.risk: a feint that draws the counterattack leaves the decisive wave with no reserve to oppose it

options.title: Hold for the Break
advantages: The reserve stays hidden until a wave actually breaks through, then seals the gap
Insurance against the worst case: no zone is lost outright while the reserve survives
disadvantages: The pre-ranged kill-zones go underused, so the prepared edge is given up, not spent
A reserve held too long is one that watched the zone bleed for nothing
options.consequence: The zone is traded down slowly and held. The surveyed kill-zones do less than they could, and the battle becomes plain attrition on ground meant to be decisive.

costs.resource: the pre-ranged kill-zones left underused, the front-loaded advantage left on the table
costs.risk: holding the reserve through every wave spends the chosen ground's edge without ever cashing it in

options.title: Piecemeal Feed
advantages: A lance per wave keeps continuous pressure - the reserve is never fully committed at once
Decision is deferred - each wave answered as it comes, no single gamble
disadvantages: Never decisive. The reserve wears away wave by wave with no payoff
The worst of both: kill-zones half-used and the reserve gone by the time the heavy waves arrive
options.consequence: Each wave is blunted and none is broken. By the time the heaviest wave arrives, the reserve is a memory and the kill-zones are half-used.

costs.resource: the reserve fed away lance by lance with no decisive moment
costs.risk: the heaviest wave arrives to find the reserve already worn away and the kill-zones already half-used

decisionPoints.name: The Convention
decisionPoints.context: The attacker fights by the one-on-one honor code and expects the same from you. Keeping it holds the battle at a pace you can sustain. Breaking it lets you actually destroy a wave, but releases everything he held back. This lever moves once, and only one way.

options.title: Honor the Duel
advantages: The attacker keeps to the code: one-on-one, a pace the zone can sustain, his reserve Star kept out of the fight
The chosen ground and pre-ranged fire do their work inside a fight you can endure
disadvantages: You cannot win decisively under the code, only endure, and a single lost duel still loses ground
The proxy is graded on terms that favor the patient attacker's weight over time
options.consequence: The battle runs at a survivable pace on your prepared ground. You trade the decisive blow for the certainty of never provoking the weight he is holding back.

costs.resource: the decisive blow given up: you can hold but not shatter a wave
costs.risk: endurance is your only tool, and {ASSAULT_WAVES} waves is a long time to never lose a duel

options.title: Break Honor, Mass Fire
advantages: Concentrated fire can actually destroy a wave - a wave broken, not merely blunted
A zone won outright instead of held on sufferance
disadvantages: The attacker declares the terms void and drops the code: his reserve Star and held-back weight commit at once
The whole battle's rules harden against you, in every zone, not just yours
options.consequence: You win the immediate exchange and lose the code that kept the attacker restrained. The next wave comes with everything he was holding back.

costs.resource: the code itself: the restraint that capped how much the attacker would commit
costs.risk: the held-back weight, committed the moment honor breaks, turns a winnable proxy into a straight attrition loss

options.title: Selective Break
advantages: Honor the duel until one decisive instant, then mass-fire a single wave - the killing blow without forfeiting the framework
If timed right, one wave is shattered and the convention survives the surprise
disadvantages: Timing is everything - a mistimed break gives the cost without the payoff
Even a clean break risks the attacker reading the convention as abandoned
options.consequence: Done at the right moment, one wave is destroyed and the duel resumes; done wrong, you pay the full price of breaking honor for a wave that was not decisive.

costs.resource: one irreversible decision banked for a single moment - used once or wasted
costs.risk: a break called a wave too early gives the attacker cause to commit his reserve for nothing gained

entries.event: The formal challenge is answered and the first wave enters the forward kill-zone: a light/medium Star, fighting one-on-one, testing the zone's ranging and resolve.
Second wave, heavier, on the same axis. The pre-ranged kill-zones have fired once, and the attacker has adjusted to them.
The attacker commits his main weight. The heavy waves begin, {ASSAULT_WAVES} expected in your sector before his force is spent.
Adjacent zones report their own pressure. A reserve committed to your zone now cannot be recalled to help them, nor theirs to help you.
If your zone is still held and the reserve still uncommitted, the attacker is close to spent. If a wave has broken through, the chosen ground begins to fall apart.
The attacker's committed force is spent or breaks through. Beyond this the proxy's terms are decided in your sector one way or the other.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Your zone must still be held at T+18:00, when the attacker is close to spent, with the reserve still uncommitted and the line unbroken. If a wave breaks through your sector, the chosen ground falls apart and the prepared advantage is lost for the whole line. The proxy is graded on the {BID_HOURS}-hour clock, and a zone lost early loses it for everyone.
