opforSketch.composition: A Clan assault Cluster fighting under a formal challenge: OmniMechs only, no vehicles, Veteran-to-Elite, attacking the zone in successive waves of rising weight. Light and medium Stars probe first, heavier Stars follow as the main force commits, and a reserve Star is held honestly out of the declared force. Early engagements are fought one warrior to one target. It breaks the code and masses fire only if the defender does so first, or if a wave is dishonored.
opforSketch.behavior: Honor-disciplined and predictable by design: massed head-on waves on the chosen ground, one-on-one targeting, rising tonnage on a readable schedule. It reads the defender's reserve commitment and punishes a spent reserve without mercy. If the duel code is broken against it, it declares the terms void and commits the held-back weight at once for the rest of the battle.

forks.name: OPERATION SPENT BID
forks.trigger: The zone held until the attacker was spent, a wave was broken hard on the chosen ground, and the honor code was kept intact.
forks.consequence: The attacker's force is spent on the ground you chose, and the line still holds the ridge. The defender counterattacks off the prepared positions while the attacker has nothing left to commit. It is a PLANETARY_ASSAULT counterstroke down the approach the kill-zones command.

forks.name: OPERATION BREACHED ZONE
forks.trigger: Your zone was broken through before the attacker was spent, and the chosen ground fell apart in your sector.
forks.consequence: The reserve from an adjacent zone mounts a relief into your collapsing sector to reseal the line before the breach spreads across the whole chosen ground. It is RELIEF_DUTY in the worst case, fighting on ground that is no longer prepared.

forks.name: OPERATION SPENT RESERVE
forks.trigger: The zone held, but the reserve was spent and the kill-zones used up, with heavy losses and the honor code strained.
forks.consequence: The ridge is still yours but the edge is gone: no reserve, no surveyed advantage, and the attacker still has weight to commit. The zone is now held on attrition alone against whatever the attacker has left. It is GARRISON_DUTY on ground that no longer favors the holder.

storyElementSeed: A gunner walks the forward kill-zone at first light, tapping the pre-ranged stakes with a boot and reciting the ranges aloud like a prayer. The ground was chosen and measured weeks ago. The only thing not yet decided is whether the reserve comes when the enemy reaches those stakes.

is-kurita.objectives.bonus: The duel is its own reward and its own trap. A warrior of the Dragon who fights the one-on-one code honors himself, but the order here is to save a reserve and treat that code as a tool, which sits ill. Keep the code because it caps the enemy's weight, not because it is owed.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: The kill-zones are an engineering problem solved weeks early: the ground was surveyed, ranged, and registered before a single machine arrived. Hold the zone by spending that preparation, not by matching the enemy's weight, which cannot be done and should not be tried.

ASSAULT_WAVES.unit: massed waves the bid force throws at your zone

RESERVE_LANCES.unit: lances of husbanded reserve, spent once

BID_HOURS.unit: hours the bid force runs before culminating

phases.name: POSTURE - THE GROUND CHOSEN
phases.lead: The battle was half-won and half-lost weeks before it started, when the ground was named and ranged. The work now is to know the chosen ground better than the men who surveyed it, every kill-zone stake and every fold the reserve can move through unseen, and to settle the one question the survey could not: when the edge gets spent.

dataBlock.Kill-zones: {PRE_RANGED_SACKS} pre-registered zones in your sector - a one-time fire advantage against the first wave that enters each
dataBlock.Reserve: {RESERVE_LANCES} lance(s), committed once and never recalled to another zone
dataBlock.Waves expected: {ASSAULT_WAVES} in your sector, rising weight, over roughly {BID_HOURS} hours until the attacker is spent
dataBlock.Honor code: binds the attacker to one-on-one duels with his reserve Star held out of the fight, until the defender breaks it

phases.protocol: The honor channel is open and monitored: the challenge is answered in form, the terms acknowledged, the ground confirmed. On the line, the codeword BREAK passed in clear is the order that the code is broken in this zone. Every machine masses fire from that call and does not stop, because a half-broken code is the worst of both. SPRING followed by a zone number means a kill-zone is triggered and its one-time advantage is being spent now.

sidebarKernel.kernel: What the formal Clan challenge actually commits both sides to, and why answering it in form is worth a reserve Star kept off the board: how the honor channel is a weapon the defender fires by keeping quiet.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT - THE WAVES
phases.lead: The waves come on a schedule you can read and a weight you cannot match, and the whole engagement comes down to two linked decisions: which zone gets the reserve, and whether the honor code holds. Both are spent once. Both are watched by an enemy who will punish the wrong call instantly.

dataBlock.Schedule: Probing waves to T+4:00, heavy waves from T+9:00, the attacker spent near T+18:00 to T+22:00
dataBlock.Reserve window: Commit before T+14:00 and the adjacent zones are out of reach; the kill-zone counterattack is a one-time spring
dataBlock.The lever: The code held keeps the attacker's reserve Star off the board; the first mass-fire call releases it for the rest of the battle
dataBlock.Breakthrough: A wave through your zone before the attacker is spent makes the chosen ground fall apart for the whole line

sidebarKernel.kernel: Spending a fixed edge against a predictable enemy: how to tell the feint wave that wants your reserve from the decisive wave that earns it, and why the code should be broken at most once, and only at the killing moment.

phases.name: RESOLUTION - THE BID GRADED
phases.lead: The proxy is decided when the attacker's force is spent, and the grade is read off the ground: held or breached, edge spent well or wasted, honor code kept or thrown away. What the zone has left when the attacker is spent decides whether the next move is a counterattack or a salvage job.

dataBlock.Attacker spent: The attacker's force runs out near T+22:00; a zone held to here cashes in the prepared advantage
dataBlock.Counterattack window: An attacker spent on your kill-zones is open to a counter down the approach they command - brief, and gone once he regroups
dataBlock.The reckoning: Reserve spent, kill-zones used, honor code intact or broken - the facts the proxy is graded on, and the terms the next mission inherits

sidebarKernel.kernel: Reading a spent Clan attack: the signs an attacker has used up his honor-bound weight and has nothing left to commit, and the narrow window in which a counterattack off the chosen ground turns a successful defense into a decided proxy.

title: OPERATION GLASS HEARTH
skeleton: a relief force must seize a city's only power-and-water station without cracking it, restart it under fire, and keep it at survival output through a counterattack whose entire aim is to force the holder to be the one who finally darkens the city - so the holder's own weapons are the objective's chief threat and the population sheltering inside the wire is the clock
inspiration: a force takes an enemy-held power or water plant and must keep it producing intact for the civilian population that depends on it, because the prize is only worth holding if it never goes dark.
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. One facility keeps this whole city alive, and most of the city does not realize it. A single walled compound in the industrial ring — a fusion power hall, a water-cracking line, and the switchyard that connects them to the grid — supplies every liter of water and every kilowatt of power that keeps {HOSTAGE_POP} thousand people in the old town and the sealed worker blocks alive: hospital power, the pumps that hold back the water table beneath the lower city, and the cracking line that makes the taps run. {TARGET_FACTION} captured the station eight months ago and has held it ever since — not because they care about the city, but because controlling it means controlling the city's survival. {EMPLOYER} is committing {FORCE_SIZE} to the industrial ring to take it back, and the order is the kind that worries experienced soldiers: the station must be captured INTACT and must keep running, because a city that loses its water will blame whoever was last seen holding the controls. The enemy garrison knows this too, and has prepared the one move that lets a force win even when it cannot hold ground — destroy the facility rather than lose it. {NPC:intel-source}, a station engineer who escaped through the spillway tunnel three weeks ago, has drawn the layout from memory: {SCUTTLE_CHARGES} demolition charges placed on the reactor shroud, the turbine bearings, and the cracking-line manifolds, detonated from a panel in the control hall or, if that is captured, from a hardened bunker beneath the switchyard. If the charges go off, the city has only {RESERVE_HOURS} hours of reservoir and battery reserve before the taps run dry, the lower-city pumps stop, and the water table floods up through the basements. The garrison is a reinforced company with combined-arms support; their mobile reserve is two hours away and will not come to retake the compound so much as to force you to destroy it. And the station cannot run on its own: {PLANT_CREW} enemy technicians are still inside at the controls — the only people on {WORLD} who know this plant's quirks — and your engineers cannot cold-start a cracking line they have never seen before the deadline the city's water supply sets. The compound is crowded with civilians who fled the fighting into the one place with power and clean water; they are sheltering right against the very machinery you have to fight to protect, and your heaviest weapons are aimed at a building you must hand back in working order. The job here is not the firefight. It is keeping the lights on while you hold it.

objectives.primary: Seize the central station and keep it producing at or above civilian-survival output through the counterattack — no damage to the reactor hall, cracking line, or switchyard exceeding 14 days' repair, and no grid-down interval longer than the city's reserve allows.
objectives.secondary: The city's reservoir-and-battery reserve never fully depletes — the taps do not run dry and the lower-city lift pumps never stop.
objectives.bonus: Take the garrison's demolition officer or the firing-panel keys intact, so the scuttle plan dies with the position instead of being carried out as the reserve arrives.

complications.name: The Pre-Rigged Core
complications.text: The garrison wired the station to die before they signed for it. {SCUTTLE_CHARGES} charges sit on the reactor shroud, the turbine bearings, and the cracking manifolds, fired from the control hall or a hardened backup cell under the switchyard. Until both firing points are in your hands, the plant is one button from cold.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The control hall and the switchyard backup cell are two separate objectives; until both are physically held by friendly units, at the end of any turn in which an enemy unit occupies either, roll 1d6 — on a 6 (5-6 once the reserve arrives) the charges fire and the primary objective fails by demolition.

complications.name: Fire Discipline Trap
complications.text: The fight is inside the machinery you must protect. A round that passes through a target, a missed shot, ammunition that catches fire in the turbine hall: the station does not care whose round cracked the manifold. The garrison fights from inside the most fragile rooms on purpose, daring you to bring the firepower that wins the room and loses the city.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any area-effect, missile, or autocannon fire resolved inside the reactor hall, cracking line, or switchyard hexes rolls on a fragility table; on a failed roll the relevant subsystem takes repair-days damage counting against the primary objective even if the shot was friendly. 'Mechs may fire only direct energy or aimed-shot weapons inside those hexes without penalty.

complications.name: The Population Inside the Wire
complications.text: Thousands sheltered in the compound for its power and water and have nowhere to go. They fill the yards, the pump galleries, the loading docks. Every firing lane through the compound is a lane through civilians, and a crowd that panics toward an exit can mask a counterattacking platoon or block your own reserve's move.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Civilian-occupied hexes are placed by the gamemaster after deployment; any area-effect or building-collapse damage in them triggers an immediate employer-standing penalty and ends bonus eligibility. Movement through crowded hexes costs double, for both sides.

complications.name: The Crew You Captured
complications.text: The {PLANT_CREW} technicians at the panels worked for the occupier yesterday. You need their hands to restart the cracking line on time; you cannot read their loyalty, and a single closed valve or false gauge reading at the wrong minute does more than a demolition charge.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the captured crew is used to restart the plant (see decision point), roll once at restart: on a failure the line stalls and the reserve clock advances 6 hours before the fault is found; cooperating crew under close engineering supervision converts the failure roll to a delay only. Without the crew, the restart deadline lengthens by one stage on the reaction timeline.

decisionPoints.name: Taking the Hall
decisionPoints.context: The control hall holds the master firing panel and the cold-start sequence both. You cannot have it both ways: the fastest way in is the most violent, the safest way in is the slowest, and the slowest way in gives the garrison every minute it needs to fire the charges or rig new ones.

options.title: Storm the Control Hall
advantages: Beats the scuttle timer — the firing panel is in your hands before the garrison can use it deliberately
Seizes the cold-start sequence intact, the fastest path to restarting the line
disadvantages: The assault goes in through the most fragile rooms in the station, under the fire-discipline penalty
A failed entry leaves your point element fixed inside the hall with the backup firing cell still live beneath the switchyard
options.consequence: If the storm succeeds, the plant is yours intact and the restart clock starts early; if it stalls, you are fighting a close-quarters battle in the one room you most need undamaged, with the charges one panic away.

costs.resource: breaching stores and a dedicated assault element committed to the hall and unavailable on the perimeter
costs.risk: The decisive fight happens inside the reactor hall's blast radius — your own success can crack what you came to save

options.title: Isolate and Squeeze
advantages: No battle damage to the core — the station is never fought through
Cutting power and water to the garrison's barracks and sealing the exits breaks their will without breaking the plant
disadvantages: The garrison has the hours it takes to seat new charges and arm the backup cell
Every hour spent squeezing is an hour off the city's reserve — the population pays for your patience in taps that slow and stop
options.consequence: The plant survives the method, but the reserve clock runs the whole time and the garrison may scuttle the moment their position is hopeless rather than surrender it — a clean approach that can still end cold.

costs.resource: the city's reserve hours spent as your siege fuel — {RESERVE_HOURS} hours is the whole budget
costs.risk: A cornered garrison bent on denial fires the charges on the way down, and squeezing buys them the time to mean it

options.title: Coopt the Crew
advantages: The plant's own technicians cold-start a line your engineers have never seen, hours faster than any outside team
Working the crew keeps the machinery operated by the hands that know it — the gentlest possible restart
disadvantages: You are trusting people who served the occupier this morning, under the Crew complication's sabotage risk
Holding and guarding the crew ties down an element that is then not clearing the backup firing cell
options.consequence: The fastest restart on offer if the crew is clean; if even one technician is loyal to the occupier, the first fault appears at the worst minute of the counterattack and the reserve clock jumps before anyone trusts the gauges again.

costs.resource: an engineering and security detail bound to the panels for the duration, watching hands instead of the wire
costs.risk: A single closed valve from a turned technician costs more than a charge, and you will not know which technician until it is too late

decisionPoints.name: When the Reserve Comes
decisionPoints.context: The garrison's mobile reserve does not arrive to win the station back. It arrives to make you wreck it. Where you choose to meet it decides whether the fight happens in the city blocks, on the wire, or never — at the price of the city's lights.

options.title: Forward Defense in the Blocks
advantages: The counterattack is fought a kilometer from the station, in the industrial blocks, where your heavy fire endangers nothing irreplaceable
Channeling the reserve into the ring's narrow streets blunts its weight before it reaches the wire
disadvantages: Pushing forward disperses your force and thins the perimeter the demolition team is built to exploit
An ambush or a wrong read leaves elements out of position when the real thrust slips past toward the compound
options.consequence: If you read the thrust right, the station never hears the fight; if you read it wrong, a demolition party is at the core while your guns are six blocks away.

costs.resource: perimeter strength spent forward — the wire thins while the blocks are held
costs.risk: Reading the feint wrong puts your firepower in the wrong street while the charges go in

options.title: Tight Perimeter on the Wire
advantages: The station is never out of your guns — nothing reaches the core without crossing your line
Concentrated defense means no element is caught alone against the reserve's weight
disadvantages: The fight happens AT the station, under the fire-discipline penalty, with the population in the compound behind you
A determined demolition rush can trade casualties to force you into the volume of fire that cracks the plant
options.consequence: Nothing reaches the core past your line — unless the enemy makes the line the killing ground and dares you to win it with the fires that finish the station yourself.

costs.resource: obstacle and revetment stores worked into the compound wire before the reserve arrives
costs.risk: The decisive exchange happens inside the plant's fragility radius with the sheltering population at your back

options.title: Keep-It-Running Triage
advantages: Dropping the line to minimum safe output frees the crew and your engineers to harden the core and shutter the most fragile galleries
A plant at minimum output and sealed is far harder to scuttle or crack in the exchange
disadvantages: Minimum output starts the city's reserve clock the moment you throttle down
A throttled plant restarting to full takes time you may not have if the reserve breaks through
options.consequence: You trade the city's margin for the plant's survivability — the machinery rides out the counterattack hardened and dim, and the taps slow while you fight, racing the reserve hours you spent buying safety.

costs.resource: the city's reserve hours spent again — output thrown away to buy structural odds
costs.risk: If the reserve breaks the wire anyway, you have a hardened plant and a city already counting down its last hours of water

entries.event: Compound seized or contested; the garrison's net goes hot and the city grid flickers as control changes hands. The occupier's mobile reserve is ordered to recall.
Cold-start window: the cracking line must be restarting by now to refill reserve faster than the city draws it down. Captured-crew restart begins here; an outside engineering team begins later.
The mobile reserve's lead elements reach the industrial ring's edge. Demolition party can be moving with them under cover of the assault.
Forward blocking position in the ring must be set, or the reserve reaches the compound wire with its weight unbroken.
Demolition team can be at the switchyard backup cell from this point; every 10 minutes of enemy possession of either firing point is a roll for the charges.

If the plant is not producing and the wire not held by now, the city's reserve crosses the point where the lower-city lift pumps begin to fail and the primary objective slips from a battle into a flood.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The station must be producing at survival output AND both firing points held by T+30:00 — if the line is still cold or either firing point is in enemy hands when the reserve arrives, the city's {RESERVE_HOURS}-hour buffer runs out, the taps and the lift pumps quit, and the primary objective fails by thirst rather than by battle.

opforSketch.composition: A reinforced garrison company holding the station — a light/medium 'Mech lance, two security infantry platoons, and a dedicated engineer demolition detail wired into the core — backed at T+12:00 by a recalled mobile reserve of fast medium 'Mechs (40-55 tons) with hover and wheeled support and a second demolition party. Regular-to-Veteran, equipped for occupation rather than open battle.
opforSketch.behavior: The garrison fights to deny, not to win. It only needs to keep one firing point live and force the holder to choose between losing the room and losing the city. The reserve counterattacks to retake the switchyard or to pin the defender's heavy weapons inside the plant. The demolition detail is the real mission: it goes after the firing points relentlessly and does not retreat with the rest of the force.

forks.name: OPERATION KEPT LIGHT
forks.trigger: Station intact and producing at survival output, both firing points held, and the demolition officer or firing keys taken.
forks.consequence: The grateful district turns out for the force that kept the water running, but a city with the lights back on is a city worth taking again — {EMPLOYER} contracts your command to hold the industrial ring and its grid through the unrest and the occupier's spoiling probes, a SECURITY_DUTY follow-on among a population now firmly yours.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY CITY
forks.trigger: The core scuttled or cracked, the line cold past the reserve deadline, or the lower-city pumps lost.
forks.consequence: The taps are dry and the water table is coming up through the lower city; the population that cheered the assault is now a crisis. Your command escorts emergency water-and-power convoys into a city turning on its liberators while engineers fight to bring the wrecked line back — a RELIEF_DUTY recovery under hostile observation, threat raised.

forks.name: OPERATION HALF MEASURE
forks.trigger: Station held but damaged, output below survival level, or the reserve extracted with the demolition officer and the firing keys.
forks.consequence: The plant runs at half and the city rations water by district; the demolition cell went to ground in the ring with the spare firing keys and the knowledge to finish what they started. Someone has to find and finish them before they walk back in — an OBJECTIVE_RAID follow-on into the industrial blocks the population still half-blames you for.

storyElementSeed: A line of people forms at the station's east gate at first light with empty cans and jugs, not to demand water but to ask whether the lights will hold tonight; the gate sergeant has no orders for this and lets an old woman fill one can from the test tap, and writes it in the log because the whole mission is in that one can.

is-davion.objectives.primary: The station stands and runs when this is over — intact, producing, the city lit. That is the order and the whole of it. The realm that takes a world owns its water; we do not free people into the dark.

HOSTAGE_POP.unit: thousand civilians the station supplies with power and water

RESERVE_HOURS.unit: hours of city reservoir-and-battery reserve if the plant drops

SCUTTLE_CHARGES.unit: demolition charges the garrison pre-rigged on the core

PLANT_CREW.unit: enemy plant technicians still at the controls

resourceGates.lackingText: With no established base on {WORLD}, you have no vetted engineering cadre to supervise the captured crew: the restart leans entirely on technicians you cannot watch closely, raising the Crew complication's sabotage roll by one band until a base and its specialists are stood up.

title: OPERATION DEEP ROOT
skeleton: an activated pre-planted stay-behind apparatus of unknown integrity must bleed an occupier's rear by waking buried cells one compartment at a time, where the activation signal is also the exposure, a cell cannot be verified clean until it is already committed, and the network is a wasting asset the counter-intelligence traces back thread by thread
inspiration: a force activates a stay-behind cell network planted before the occupation, lighting its compartments one at a time to bleed the occupier's rear - knowing every cell it wakes is a thread the enemy's counter-intelligence can pull back to the rest.
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The valley fell in a week and the war moved on, but the people who lost it left a resistance network behind. Before {TARGET_FACTION} came over the passes, a stay-behind organization was set up throughout the highland interior — {SECTOR_CELLS} cells operating under cover identities in the ridge villages and upland farms, plus a hidden cache holding {CACHE_MECHS} light 'Mechs stripped down and wrapped against the cold, along with weapons, fuel, and the coded signals that activate them. Your command is the activation authority, slipped in over the passes with the recognition codes and one hard task: damage the occupier's rear areas. The front is two jumps away and {TARGET_FACTION} needs every battalion forward; the only thing holding their line together is the supply route that climbs the main pass-road through this valley — a convoy every {CONVOY_DAYS} days carrying fuel, munitions, and replacement troops, guarded by a rear-area garrison that would rather be anywhere else. Cut that supply line badly enough and the occupier will have to pull a frontline unit back to hold the rear — which is the entire goal. The valley cannot be liberated outright, only made too expensive to hold on the cheap. But the network you hold the keys to is not your own. {NPC:intel-source}, the courier who brought you in, is honest about the problem: the network has sat for eight months under occupation, and there is no way to tell from the outside which cells are still trustworthy. A cell may be intact, may be dead, or may have been quietly captured and turned against you — and the only way to find out is to activate it, because the activation signal is the same transmission the occupier's counter-intelligence section is listening for. Every cell you activate gives their hunters a lead they can follow to the others. And the network is finite: the cache does not refill, a destroyed cell does not come back, and the occupier responds to every attack with a standing reprisal order — {REPRISAL_COUNT} hostages taken from the nearest village per attack, a toll the highland people are counting even if you are not. Use the network too fast and it is destroyed before it does enough damage; use it too slowly and the occupier secures the rear and the opportunity closes. You are not fighting a battle. You are carefully spending a buried asset during the one week it will ever be worth using.

objectives.primary: Bleed the occupier's rear over the campaign window hard enough to force a frontline unit back to the interior. That means steady attacks on the supply road without the network being rolled up before that point is reached.
objectives.secondary: Keep at least a third of the sector's cells asleep and intact at the window's end, an unused reserve for the decisive strike or the next uprising.
objectives.bonus: Find and take out the garrison's counter-intelligence officer, or break their effort to recruit informers in the ridge villages, blinding the hunt that traces the network.

complications.name: Unknown Integrity
complications.text: Eight months of occupation sit between the planting and the waking. A compartment may be clean, may be dead, may be a trap run back at you — and the file says nothing, because the people who would know are dead or arrested. You learn what a cell is only after you have committed it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: When a fresh cell is first activated, the gamemaster rolls its integrity secretly: clean, dead (no assets materialize, the action aborts), or turned (the strike walks into a prepared cordon). Intelligence work before activation can convert one die step toward clean but never fully clears a cell.

complications.name: Activation Is Exposure
complications.text: The coded wake-signal is the one transmission the counter-intelligence section is built to catch. Every cell you light radiates, however briefly, and direction-finding does not need to break the code to draw a line on the map.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each activation adds a cumulative point to the occupier's trace track; at thresholds the gamemaster places a cordon-and-sweep on the most recently active sector. Activating two cells from the same valley inside one cycle doubles the trace gain for the second.

complications.name: The Reprisal Ledger
complications.text: The occupier answers sabotage it cannot prevent with reprisal it can: {REPRISAL_COUNT} hostages from the nearest village per strike, by standing order. The highland people shelter the cells, and they are counting. There is a number of empty chairs past which a village stops hiding partisans and starts naming them.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each strike raises the local reprisal counter; past a threshold the sheltering population's cooperation drops a band — caches become harder to reach, warnings stop coming, and the informer-recruitment effort (bonus objective) gains traction. Strikes that draw the garrison away from villages, or that free reprisal hostages, lower the counter.

complications.name: The Finite Apparatus
complications.text: The cache holds what it holds: {CACHE_MECHS} 'Mechs, a fixed stock of fuel and munitions, and no resupply this side of the passes. A burned cell is gone, a spent magazine is not replaced, and a 'Mech lost is a 'Mech the rising does not get back. The network is a budget, not an income.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track expended cache stock across the campaign; cells activated and lost reduce the available force pool for later strikes and for the forks. There is no in-mission resupply — overspending early caps the force available when the recall threshold is finally in reach.

decisionPoints.name: Which Cells to Wake
decisionPoints.context: The trunk-road convoy is {CONVOY_DAYS} days out and you have to hit it with something. A fresh compartment is at full strength but unknown integrity; a cell you have run before is proven clean but patterned; running it cold with your own infiltrators exposes no part of the net but carries no local knowledge. The choice is which risk you would rather own.

options.title: Wake a Fresh Compartment
advantages: Full strength — the cell's whole cache and roster come up untouched
A compartment the hunters have never seen leaves no pattern for them to match against past strikes
disadvantages: Unknown integrity: the cell may be dead, or turned and waiting
Each fresh activation is a new transmission and a new line on the counter-intelligence map
options.consequence: If the cell is clean, you hit the convoy at full weight with no trail to your other compartments; if it is turned, your strike element walks into a cordon prepared specifically for the wake-signal it answered.

costs.resource: one compartment spent from a finite net and one point onto the trace track
costs.risk: You cannot verify the cell until you have already sent your people into it

options.title: Re-Use a Proven Cell
advantages: Known clean — no integrity roll, the people and cache are trusted
Established dead-drops and routes mean a faster, smoother strike with the population already aligned
disadvantages: The hunters already hold this cell's signature from its last action and have been refining the trace
Leaning on one compartment concentrates the reprisal on its sheltering villages until they break
options.consequence: A clean, fast strike against a convoy you know how to hit — at the cost of feeding the one pattern the counter-intelligence section has had the most time to solve, and the one village ledger filling fastest.

costs.resource: the reprisal counter on this cell's villages, climbing toward the band where they stop hiding it
costs.risk: Re-using a patterned cell hands the hunters their best chance to close the trace

options.title: Run It Cold, Yourself
advantages: No part of the buried net is exposed — no wake-signal, no trace point, no cell committed
Your own command keeps full control of the action with no unknown-integrity gamble
disadvantages: No local guides, no pre-positioned cache, no village screen — your force is the signature, on ground you do not know
An off-world unit moving in the interior without cover is exactly what the garrison's patrols are watching for
options.consequence: The net stays dark and intact, and you take the convoy on your own terms or not at all — but a strike that goes wrong is your whole committed force caught in the open, not a deniable cell, and the rising has shown its hand without lighting a single lamp.

costs.resource: your own force committed forward without the net's screen or its caches
costs.risk: Caught in the open without local cover, your command is the one that gets cordoned

decisionPoints.name: The Trace Comes
decisionPoints.context: A cell has been lit, a convoy burns, and the counter-intelligence section has drawn its line — a cordon is forming on the valley where the wake-signal originated. The cell inside it is yours to save, spend, or fight for, and each answer teaches the hunters something different.

options.title: Go Quiet
advantages: The compartment shuts down, scatters into its cover identities, and the cordon closes on an empty valley
Protects the rest of the net — a cold cell pulls no thread toward the others
disadvantages: The cell is out of the fight for the rest of the window — its tempo and its cache are frozen behind the cordon
A sweep through a 'quiet' valley still falls on the villages, and the reprisal ledger does not pause for your discipline
options.consequence: The net survives intact and dark, the hunters learn nothing, and you have one fewer cell bleeding the rear at the exact moment you most need the tempo — patience paid in lost pressure.

costs.resource: one compartment's strikes for the rest of the window, frozen behind the cordon
costs.risk: Going quiet under a sweep still bills the villages, and a frozen cell may not come back live before the window shuts

options.title: Feed the Trace
advantages: A controlled cell run as bait pulls the hunters onto a false line, away from the compartments that matter
Burning one cell on your terms protects several and buys the rest of the net a clean cycle
disadvantages: You are spending your own people deliberately — the bait cell is meant to be caught
If the counter-intelligence section reads the feed as a feed, the misdirection inverts and confirms the very links you meant to hide
options.consequence: The hunters chase a trail you built and the strong compartments stay dark — unless they see the hand behind it, in which case you have handed them a confirmed thread and spent a cell to do it.

costs.resource: one cell deliberately burned and the people in it written off to protect the net
costs.risk: A trace they recognize as bait inverts — the sacrifice confirms the network instead of hiding it

options.title: Fight the Cordon
advantages: The cache 'Mechs break the sweep and pull the cell out intact with its people and stores
A bloodied rear-security force is one more reason the occupier must recall weight from the front
disadvantages: Open battle converts deniable guerrilla into the stand-up fight the occupier's heavier rear force is built to win
Committing the cache 'Mechs to a rescue spends the apparatus's irreplaceable heavy element on one cell
options.consequence: The cell comes out and the garrison bleeds — but the rising has fought a pitched action it cannot afford to repeat, the cache is lighter for it, and the next cordon comes in heavier knowing what you will spend to save your own.

costs.resource: the cache's heavy 'Mech element committed and attrited in a stand-up fight
costs.risk: Winning the cordon openly tells the occupier the rear is worth a line battalion sooner than you wanted them to decide

entries.event: First compartment activated; the wake-signal goes out and the first strike hits the trunk-road tail. The counter-intelligence trace track opens.
The garrison issues the standing reprisal order against the nearest village; the highland ledger starts filling. Direction-finding crews deploy to the valley the signal came from.
First cordon-and-sweep forms on the most recently active sector. The next trunk convoy is due — strike it or let the tail run.
Informer-recruitment effort takes hold in any village past its reprisal threshold; warnings to the cells slow and the trace accelerates.
The occupier weighs the rear against the front: if the bleed has met the threshold, a line unit is ordered back; if not, the rear garrison is reinforced and the window begins to close.
End of the activation window. Whatever cells are still lit and traced are rolled up in a coordinated sweep; whatever stayed dark survives to the next rising.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The rear must be bled past the recall threshold before the trace track fills — if the counter-intelligence section rolls up the linked compartments before the occupier is forced to recall a line unit (by roughly T+14d, sooner if reprisals turn the villages), the network unravels into a list of arrests and the rising fails without forcing a single battalion off the front.

opforSketch.composition: A rear-area occupation garrison: two security infantry companies with wheeled and light-hover support, a quick-reaction lance of medium 'Mechs, a counter-intelligence section with direction-finding crews and a growing file of recruited informers, and the authority to reprisal at will. Regular quality, occupation-equipped, spread thin across the interior and oriented forward by standing order.
opforSketch.behavior: It faces forward by default, because the front needs everything, and it answers each strike with a cordon-and-sweep, reprisals, and informer recruitment, rather than standing patrols it cannot afford. It traces the network patiently through activation signals and village informers. It will not pull weight off the front until the rear is clearly bleeding faster than the garrison can stop it, and that recall is exactly the win the uprising is built to force.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG WINTER
forks.trigger: Recall threshold met, a line unit pulled back to the interior, and a third of the sector's cells still dark.
forks.consequence: The recalled battalion grinds up the trunk pass-road toward a rear it cannot find, and the partisan command wants it pinned and humiliated where the front can see — your surviving cells and your intact reserve fix and demonstrate against the recalled unit, a DIVERSIONARY_RAID follow-on that turns the occupier's own correction into a second wound.

forks.name: OPERATION DEEP CACHE
forks.trigger: The tail was bled but the net is exposed and the villages turning, or the threshold met only after most cells were burned.
forks.consequence: The rising survives degraded: the surviving cells must break contact and relocate to the deep-cache over the passes before the cordon tightens, abandoning the burned compartments and the villages that can no longer hide them. The campaign continues from worse ground and a lighter cache — a GUERRILLA_WARFARE pivot under a population that has counted too many empty chairs.

forks.name: OPERATION COLD COURIER
forks.trigger: The net unraveled — compartments rolled up before the threshold, the trace closed, the rising broken.
forks.consequence: What is left is a list of names the counter-intelligence section is working through and a cell-master who knows too much to be caught. Your command runs an EXTRACTION_RAID recovery to pull {NPC:intel-source} and the surviving cadre off {WORLD} over the passes ahead of the sweep, before the apparatus becomes a confession.

storyElementSeed: A boy from a ridge village leaves a wedge of cheese on a flat stone above the trunk road three mornings running — the old recognition sign that a cell is still clean and still watching — and on the fourth morning the stone is bare, and the cadre argues in the cache about whether the silence means the cell is dead, taken, or simply that the boy's family finally counted the cost and stopped.

merc.objectives.primary: The contract pays on the recall — force a line unit back off the front and the bonus clears; the apparatus is the employer's asset on loan, and a net you burn out is a net you do not get paid to have spent. Bleed the rear, keep the cell-master breathing, and bring the keys home.

SECTOR_CELLS.unit: dormant cells in your compartment of the stay-behind network

CACHE_MECHS.unit: light 'Mechs buried in the highland cache

REPRISAL_COUNT.unit: hostages shot per strike under the occupier's standing reprisal order

CONVOY_DAYS.unit: days between rear supply convoys on the trunk pass-road

resourceGates.lackingText: Breaking a cordon with the cache 'Mechs means fielding the buried heavy element — without depot access to the deep-cache over the passes, the wrapped 'Mechs cannot be reactivated and armed in time, and this option is unavailable until the cache is reached.

title: OPERATION FIRST KEEL
inspiration: A high-value world held in depth cannot be taken in one battle; it is reduced in phases - orbit and DropPort, then the coastal beachhead, then the interior line, then the capital - and each phase can fail and force a different next move.
skeleton: first wave must take a contested coastal DropPort intact under the fixed descent clock of the heavy ships already committed to their burn overhead, where cratering the field denies it to everyone and the demolition firing point is the whole battle
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. Taking this world starts the way taking any defended world starts: by seizing the one piece of ground the heavy ships can land on. {EMPLOYER}'s invasion plan commits {FORCE_SIZE} to the surface in waves, and the first wave is yours — a lead element dropped to capture the coastal DropPort intact before the assault transports behind you reach the bottom of their descent corridor. There is no second landing field within reach. The DropPort sits on a headland above a tidal estuary; it is the only paved landing surface on the continent rated to berth an assault-class DropShip, and {TARGET_FACTION} has used the warning you gave them to wire it for demolition, planning to deny it to everyone rather than lose it. {NPC:intel-source} reports {FIELD_CHARGES} demolition charges under the landing surface and the fuel farm, fired from a hardened control bunker at the landward edge of the field. The field is defended by {DEFENDER_MECHS} 'Mechs plus a fixed gun line and a hover reaction force under {NPC:opfor-commander}. That report is 6 days old, so treat the numbers as a rough guide, not an exact count. The problem is the headland and the orbit above it at the same time. The orbital approach is a single descent corridor. The assault transports can wait {ORBIT_PASSES} passes, no more, before fuel and the planetary defense guns force them to either commit to landing or burn fuel for another full orbit, which loses the whole timetable. On the ground, the headland is ringed on three sides by the tidal estuary. At low tide it is a firm flat a light 'Mech can cross; at high tide it is nine meters of cold sea. So the field has only two approaches: one over land across a seawall causeway the defender has had years to range, and one at sea level across the tidal flat, passable only when the tide is out. The demolition control bunker is the whole battle. Capture it, cut its firing line, or hold the field long enough that {NPC:opfor-commander} cannot fire the charges in sequence, and the heavy wave lands on a working port. Fail, and {DESCENT_WINDOW_MIN} minutes after the transports commit, they are landing into a cratered field — or aborting to a bare beach with the schedule already a full phase behind. The civilians here are the port's own workers — dock crews, fuel handlers, crane operators — ordered to evacuate but not all gone, because a working port is the only paycheck on the headland. They are not the enemy. They are standing on top of the charges.

objectives.primary: Seize the DropPort intact - the landing surface, the control bunker, and the fuel farm undamaged enough to berth and service the heavy wave - and hold it through the descent window.
objectives.secondary: Take or cut the demolition control bunker before the field charges can be fired in sequence. The landing surface must be certified safe for the assault transports.
objectives.bonus: Capture the fuel farm and the field cranes intact and working, so the beachhead opens supplied rather than starved.

complications.name: The Committed Wave
complications.text: The assault transports overhead are already in the descent corridor and cannot loiter indefinitely. They can hold for {ORBIT_PASSES} passes; every pass beyond that runs them under the planetary defence guns with their bays full of the second wave. The clock above you is not yours to stop.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each pass held past the second exposes a transport to battery fire: roll 1d6 per extra pass, on 1-2 a transport takes a hit and lands a unit's worth of the follow-on late by two turns or with a damaged 'Mech.

complications.name: The Tide on the Reach
complications.text: The sea-level approach across the flat is firm only at low water. Twice a cycle the reach drains for a window long enough to cross; outside it the flat is nine meters of sea. A force caught on the flat by the turning tide does not withdraw - it drowns.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The tidal-flat approach is open only during the low-water window; any unit still on the flat when the tide turns is removed from the engagement, recovered or not at the gamemaster's call.

complications.name: Charges Under the Field
complications.text: The hardstand and fuel farm are wired from the control bunker. The defender's intent is plain: a field he cannot hold is a field nobody uses. Reading the bunker's readiness is the difference between a captured port and a smoking crater.
complications.mechanicalEffect: From T+12:00 the control bunker can fire the full charge string. A fired string voids the bonus, craters the hardstand, and forces the heavy wave to abort to the bare beach. Cutting or seizing the bunker before T+12:00 removes the threat.

complications.name: The Labour Did Not All Leave
complications.text: Crane crews and fuel handlers remain on the field, some because they were not told in time and some because the port is their living. A firefight on the hardstand is a firefight among them, and a destroyed labour force cannot work the cranes the beachhead needs.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Civilian casualties on the hardstand or fuel farm impose an employer-standing penalty and convert any advancing fork to its COMPROMISED reading; collateral to the cranes themselves voids the bonus regardless of capture.

decisionPoints.name: Taking the Port Intact
decisionPoints.context: The control bunker fires the charges, and that bunker is what the battle is for. The pads are the fastest path to it and the most exposed. The seawall causeway is orderly and slow. The tidal flat is a blind flank the tide can close. The descent clock is already running when the first 'Mech is on the ground.

options.title: Combat-Drop the Pads
advantages: Shortest path to the control bunker, denying the defender the time to fire the charges in sequence
Lands the force exactly where the heavy wave needs it held
disadvantages: Drops into the pre-ranged field gun belt and the pad anti-air
A scattered combat drop fights the gun belt in small pieces for the first turns
options.consequence: You reach the control bunker first but bleed on the open hardstand under fixed fire, and an off-target drop fights its way in alone.

costs.resource: drop cohesion: a contested pad drop scatters the element across the field
costs.risk: the gun belt and pad AA range the pads - the first two turns are fought inside their cone whether you like it or not

options.title: Land Short, Assault the Seawall
advantages: Organized landing off the field, clear of the pad anti-air
The seawall causeway funnels your force - and the defender's counterattack with it
disadvantages: The causeway is ranged and slow
Every minute on the causeway is a minute {NPC:opfor-commander} spends arming the string in order
options.consequence: You arrive in order but late, racing the firing sequence to the bunker across ground the defender has measured for years.

costs.resource: time: the causeway approach concedes the turns the defender spends arming charges
costs.risk: a defender who finishes the firing sequence before you cross craters the field as you arrive

options.title: Cross the Tidal Flat at Low Water
advantages: Avoids both the pad AA and the causeway guns
Arrives on the control bunker's blind seaward flank
disadvantages: Tide-gated and weight-capped: light and medium 'Mechs only on the firm flat
A mistimed crossing strands the flanking force when the sea comes back in
options.consequence: You turn the bunker from the flank it does not watch, betting the tide table against the firing clock.

costs.resource: tide window: the flank only opens at low water and closes hard
costs.risk: caught by the turning tide, the flanking element is lost to the sea with the bunker still uncut

decisionPoints.name: Committing the Heavy Wave
decisionPoints.context: The field is contested and the transports have reached their commit point in the corridor. The call is yours and it cannot be unmade: weight ashore now, one more pass to be sure, or wave them off the field entirely.

options.title: Commit Now, Land Hot
advantages: Keeps the timetable - the reduction opens on schedule
Weight ashore immediately turns the fight for the headland
disadvantages: If the string fires as they land, the follow-on lands into craters and fire
Bets the wave on your having silenced the control bunker
options.consequence: The schedule holds and the gamble is total - a clean port or a catastrophe under a settling transport.

costs.resource: margin: the descent-window reserve is spent committing early
costs.risk: a fired string under a landing assault transport is the wave lost before it is ashore

options.title: Hold One More Pass
advantages: The wave lands onto a port you have certified safe
Buys the assault team the minutes to confirm the charges are dead
disadvantages: Costs a pass against the planetary guns
Burns the descent-window margin you cannot get back
options.consequence: A clean landing bought with one more orbit under fire and a tighter clock for everything after.

costs.resource: an orbital pass held under the planetary defence guns
costs.risk: a transport hit on the held pass lands the follow-on short a 'Mech and a phase behind

options.title: Divert to the Austere Beach
advantages: Takes the field charges out of the equation entirely
The wave lands safe on the strand below the headland
disadvantages: No cranes, no fuel farm - the beachhead opens starved
The DropPort stands uncaptured behind the lodgment as a problem for later
options.consequence: You trade the port for certainty and inherit a supply problem into the beachhead phase, the captured-field bonus gone.

costs.resource: the beachhead opens without port cranes or fuel - resupply runs off the strand
costs.risk: an uncaptured DropPort at your back can be reinforced and used against the lodgment

entries.event: First wave makes planetfall at the DropPort perimeter; site alarm sounds and the defender's demolition crews move to the field charges.
The fixed gun belt and pad AA go weapons-free; the hover reaction section moves to the causeway approach. The control bunker begins arming the string in sequence.
The control bunker can fire the full charge string from this point. If it is not taken or cut, the hardstand is one command from a crater.
The assault transports reach their commit point in the descent corridor; they must be waved down onto a certified field or held for another pass under the planetary guns.
If the field is not declared safe, the committed wave lands into a hot or cratered field or aborts to the austere beach - the reduction opens a phase behind schedule.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The demolition control bunker must be taken or cut by T+12:00 and the field declared safe by T+20:00, or the heavy wave commits into a cratered or contested port and the beachhead phase opens late, starved, and against a defender who kept his footing.

opforSketch.composition: One reinforced DropPort-defence company of {DEFENDER_MECHS} medium-to-heavy 'Mechs (40-70 tons) at Regular-to-Veteran quality, dug into the headland behind a fixed gun belt and pad anti-air, supported by a hover and wheeled reaction section of 4-6 vehicles (Saracen/Pegasus behaviour) and an engineer demolition party tending the field charges. Aerospace limited to a pair of interceptors held back for the heavy wave's descent.
opforSketch.behavior: Deny the field intact to no one: hold the hardstand while the odds allow, and if the line bends past saving, {NPC:opfor-commander} fires the charge string and cedes a crater rather than a port. The reaction section breaks contact at 40 percent force damage; the demolition party does not break - it exists to push the firing handle.

forks.name: OPERATION FULL BERTH
forks.trigger: DropPort taken intact with the fuel farm and cranes captured and working, the control bunker in hand before the string could fire.
forks.consequence: The heavy wave berths and services on a captured field; the beachhead opens fully supplied. Your command holds the lodgment from a port that resupplies it - the next phase begins with fuel and cranes the defender meant to deny you.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND WAVE DOWN
forks.trigger: DropPort secured.
forks.consequence: The heavy wave lands and the line force is ashore behind you; the defender falls back to counterattack the new lodgment. Your command holds the beachhead while the reserve forms inland - the reduction moves to the coast.

forks.name: OPERATION RELIEF SHORE
forks.trigger: The field cratered or the landing contested past saving - the heavy wave diverts to the austere beach.
forks.consequence: The first wave is ashore and isolated on the headland with no port and a starved supply line; a second wave must fight in along the coast to relieve it before the defender finishes it - a relief under the tide, the reduction's opening gambit recovered the hard way.

storyElementSeed: A loadmaster walks the drop bay one last time before the burn, counting breaching charges against the manifest, because the field below is wired to swallow the whole wave and the only thing that opens it is getting down before the man at the firing panel decides the day is lost.

is-kurita.objectives.primary: The field is the doorway to the Coordinator's new ground, and it will be taken whole. An officer who lands the wave onto a crater has failed the Dragon twice: once at the field, and once at every phase that field was meant to supply. Take the control bunker. Hold the hardstand. The cranes will turn for us by nightfall.

merc.objectives.primary: The contract pays the lead-element bonus on a CERTIFIED field. The auditor will not sign off on a crater, and Section 7 docks the whole assault premium if the heavy wave aborts to the beach. Cut the control bunker before you do anything else. The bonus is in the fuel farm intact, and so is the next phase's fuel.

DESCENT_WINDOW_MIN.unit: minutes the committed heavy wave can be held before its descent corridor closes

FIELD_CHARGES.unit: demolition charges wired under the DropPort hardstand and fuel farm

ORBIT_PASSES.unit: orbital passes before the assault transports must commit or burn for another

resourceGates.lackingText: No organic assault DropShip on the descent: the held pass runs on {EMPLOYER}'s contracted lift, and the charter's commit clause forfeits the hold-margin - the wave commits on the corridor's schedule, not yours, at 30,000-class penalty pricing if you wave it off.

phases.name: DESCENT - THE CORRIDOR
phases.lead: The phase begins in vacuum, in a descent corridor with room for only one timetable. The lead element commits to an approach to the headland before the first gun opens up, knowing the heavy wave behind it cannot wait around.

dataBlock.Descent corridor: single approach lane; transports hold {ORBIT_PASSES} passes before the planetary guns force a commit
dataBlock.Field charges: {FIELD_CHARGES} under the hardstand and fuel farm, fired from the landward control bunker
dataBlock.Approaches: seawall causeway (ranged, all-tonnage) and the tidal flat (low-water only, light/medium)
dataBlock.Descent window: {DESCENT_WINDOW_MIN} minutes from commit to the corridor closing

routes.name: KEEL - THE PADS
routes.desc: Combat drop directly onto the hardstand toward the control bunker
routes.tradeoff: Fastest to the bunker, but lands inside the pre-ranged gun belt and pad anti-air

routes.name: WALL - THE SEAWALL CAUSEWAY
routes.desc: Land short and assault up the one land approach
routes.tradeoff: Orderly and off the anti-air, but slow and ranged - it buys the defender his firing sequence

routes.name: FLAT - THE TIDAL REACH
routes.desc: Cross the drained flat at low water to the bunker's seaward flank
routes.tradeoff: Turns the blind flank but is tide-gated and capped to medium 'Mechs - the sea closes it on a clock

phases.protocol: The descent net matters here more than anything: the lead element passes FIELD STATE on the assault frequency at each marker - RED (charges live), AMBER (bunker contested), GREEN (charges cut, hardstand safe). The heavy wave commits on GREEN and only on GREEN. A wave commander who hears nothing holds his pass, because silence on this net means the field is still wired.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Why a committed descent corridor cannot simply wave off - the burn arithmetic, what a held pass costs in fuel and exposure to the planetary guns, and why the man on the ground owns the clock the man in orbit cannot stop.

phases.name: THE FIELD - THE CONTROL BUNKER
phases.lead: The battle is the control bunker and the seconds around it. Everything on the hardstand is arranged to reach the firing point before {NPC:opfor-commander} can use it - and to do it without wrecking the cranes the next phase needs.

dataBlock.Firing window: charges can fire from T+12:00; the bunker taken or cut before then removes the threat
dataBlock.Forbidden damage: cranes, fuel farm, the loaded berths - a hit here voids the supplied-beachhead bonus
dataBlock.Heavy-wave commit: T+20:00 at the corridor commit point; GREEN required to wave down
dataBlock.Civilian presence: crane and fuel crews still on the field - the firefight is among them

sidebarKernel.kernel: Cutting a demolition control bunker versus storming it: where the firing line is cut for a safe field, why a hardened bunker fights back, and what a captured fuel farm is worth measured against the crater it would otherwise be.

phases.name: THE WAVE DOWN - CERTIFY OR DIVERT
phases.lead: With the control bunker resolved one way or the other, the call goes up the corridor. The wave lands onto a working port, holds for one more pass, or diverts to the beach - and the beachhead it opens is the port you left it, working or starved.

dataBlock.Certification: FIELD STATE GREEN and the hardstand clear before the wave commits
dataBlock.Hold cost: each extra pass risks a transport to the planetary guns on a 1-2
dataBlock.Divert cost: austere beach landing - no cranes, no fuel, the DropPort left uncaptured at your back
dataBlock.Hand-off: captured cranes and fuel farm open the beachhead supplied; a crater or a divert opens it starved

sidebarKernel.kernel: The commit decision no one can take back - reading whether the field is safe enough to land the people who will hold it, and why diverting to the beach trades a hard fight now for a harder phase next.

title: OPERATION SALT BERM
inspiration: A high-value world held in depth cannot be taken in one battle; it is reduced in phases - orbit and DropPort, then the coastal beachhead, then the interior line, then the capital - and each phase can fail and force a different next move.
skeleton: lodgment force must hold a shallow coastal beachhead against a mobile reserve's timed counterattacks, giving no ground it cannot retake, until the still-landing line weight ashore flips the perimeter from defence to breakout
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The DropPort is taken and the first wave is ashore, which means the hard part begins. {EMPLOYER}'s line force is landing behind you onto a shallow crescent of coast - a beachhead {LODGMENT_DEPTH_KM} kilometers deep on a good hour, the sea at its back, follow-on DropShips still settling onto the strand through the surf - and {TARGET_FACTION}'s mobile reserve is forming inland to throw it into the water before it can deepen. Your command holds the lodgment. The terrain problem is the coast itself: a strand backed by dunes and a coastal flat that gives way, inland, to a low ridge line and a tidal estuary that cuts the crescent on its left. There is no depth to trade - every hundred meters given up is a hundred meters of strand the still-landing line cannot use, and a beachhead that gives ground gives it onto its own ships. {NPC:intel-source} reads the reserve as a defending battalion's mobile element that will commit in timed waves rather than all at once: {RESERVE_COUNTERATTACKS} counterattacks expected before enough of the line is ashore, each a fresh slice driven at the seam between the strand and the ridge. It is led by {NPC:opfor-commander}, who has fought this coast before and knows where the estuary can be forded at low water. That read is 4 days old, so treat it as solid but not certain. Your deadline is the landing itself: {LANDING_SHIPS} follow-on DropShips are still putting the line force down, and you must hold for {ASHORE_HOURS} hours before the lodgment has enough weight ashore to stop giving ground and start advancing. Until then your force is a cork in a bottle the enemy is trying to shake loose. Keep the landing strand open and out of enemy fire, keep the reserve from breaking through at either the ridge or the estuary, and do not let any counterattack reach the beach where the unarmed transports are sitting. The civilians here are a fishing settlement on the estuary, whose boats are the only craft that know the fordable channels — they will move people or cargo for whoever controls the water, and they are watching to see who that will be.

objectives.primary: Hold the beachhead perimeter and keep the landing strand open and clear of direct fire until the line force is ashore - the lodgment intact, the still-landing DropShips unthreatened.
objectives.secondary: Deny the mobile reserve the ridge line and the estuary ford; no counterattack reaches the strand or the unarmed transports on it.
objectives.bonus: Hold with enough depth that the lodgment transitions to breakout on schedule rather than merely surviving - the next phase opens with momentum, not relief.

complications.name: No Ground to Trade
complications.text: A beachhead with the sea at its back cannot give ground to buy time the way a defence inland can. Every meter yielded is a meter of strand the line needs to land on, and a perimeter pressed back far enough puts direct fire on the transports themselves. Trading space for time is not an option here.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any perimeter sector pushed back to within direct-fire range of the strand halts all landing for as long as it is contested; a delayed landing extends the hold deadline by the turns lost.

complications.name: Timed Waves
complications.text: {NPC:opfor-commander} does not commit the reserve all at once. He feeds it in {RESERVE_COUNTERATTACKS} timed counterattacks, each a fresh slice aimed at the same seam, learning your dispositions between waves and pressing hardest while the lodgment is shallow.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Counterattacks arrive on a schedule, not en masse; each wave that gains ground or a kill shifts the next wave's axis toward the proven weak point, and the defender gains a free repositioning move if the same sector is held in the same posture across two waves.

complications.name: The Estuary Ford
complications.text: The estuary that anchors the lodgment's left is fordable at low water on channels only the fishing settlement knows. At the wrong tide it is a wall; at the right one it is a back door onto the strand. The reserve has a guide who has used it before.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During the low-water window the estuary becomes a crossable flanking axis for light and medium units; a perimeter that anchors on the estuary without watching the ford concedes a free entry behind the line during that window.

complications.name: The Strand Still Lands
complications.text: The follow-on DropShips are unarmed once down and crowd the strand as they unload. They cannot disperse and they cannot fight; protecting them costs depth the perimeter would rather spend on the ridge. The lodgment defends its own reinforcement.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Up to two strand hexes per turn are occupied by landing/unloading transports that block movement and fields of fire and must not be fired across; a transport lost on the strand removes that increment of the follow-on line force from the campaign.

decisionPoints.name: Shaping the Lodgment
decisionPoints.context: The crescent is shallow, the ships are still landing, and the reserve is forming inland. Where you set the perimeter decides what the counterattacks hit and what the follow-on stacks up behind. Hug the strand, reach for the ridge, or let the estuary do the work on one flank - each reads differently when the first wave comes.

options.title: Hug the Strand - a Tight Perimeter
advantages: Every unit mutually supports; the reserve must cross open ground to reach you
Nothing is overextended - the line is short and strong
disadvantages: No depth: the still-landing ships stack up under fire with nowhere to disperse
The reserve's indirect fire ranges the whole crescent at once
options.consequence: You hold the line easily but the lodgment cannot grow, and the follow-on lands into a crowded, ranged box that bleeds the breakout's momentum.

costs.resource: depth: the shallow box leaves the line landing under fire with no room to deploy
costs.risk: a beachhead that cannot deepen survives the phase and starts the next one already behind

options.title: Push to the Coastal Ridge - Buy Depth
advantages: Depth to land the follow-on in order and observation over the reserve's forming-up ground
Room enough that the lodgment can become a breakout, not just a hold
disadvantages: Thins the line to take and hold the ridge
Opens a flank along the shore the reserve can turn
options.consequence: The lodgment gains the room it needs to transition, but a counterattack into the thinned flank can roll the perimeter up against its own beach.

costs.resource: force spread thin across the ridge line to hold the depth you bought
costs.risk: a turned coastal flank unzips the beachhead from the side the sea cannot protect

options.title: Anchor on the Estuary - Let Terrain Cordon
advantages: Economizes force - the estuary is a flank that mostly defends itself
Concentrates strength on the open landward side where the reserve must come
disadvantages: Cedes the far estuary bank as an axis you have chosen not to contest
A low-water ford turns the anchor into an open door behind the line
options.consequence: You hold a smaller, cheaper perimeter, betting the tide and the channels that the estuary stays a wall - and handing the defender one axis if his guide finds the ford.

costs.resource: the far estuary bank ceded as an uncontested axis for the phase
costs.risk: the settlement's channels in enemy hands make the anchor the weakest point, not the strongest

entries.event: The first reserve counterattack forms inland and crosses its line of departure; the lodgment is shallow, the follow-on DropShips still landing on the strand.
Lead reserve lances strike the seam between strand and ridge - the perimeter is tested before it has depth, the estuary's low-water window opening.
Second counterattack wave; {NPC:opfor-commander} throws it at the sector that gave most in the first, and the estuary ford is crossable now if it is unwatched.
Enough line weight is ashore that the lodgment can hold without giving ground; the perimeter stops being a cork and starts being a fist.
The lodgment can transition from defence to breakout - if it held the strand open and kept the ridge and ford out of the reserve's hands.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The perimeter must keep its landing strand open and unranged until T+30:00, when enough of the line is ashore to stop giving ground; lose the strand before then and the follow-on cannot land, the lodgment is pinned against the sea, and the beachhead fails by drowning rather than by battle.

opforSketch.composition: A defending battalion's mobile reserve committed against the lodgment in timed slices: 1-2 'Mech lances (45-75 tons) at Regular-to-Veteran quality leading each wave, with a hover and tracked armour element (Manticore/SRM-carrier behaviour) for weight and a mechanized infantry element to retake ground the 'Mechs clear. Each counterattack is a fresh portion of the reserve, never the whole.
opforSketch.behavior: Timed, repeated counterattacks aimed at the seam between the landing beach and the high ground: presses hard while the lodgment is shallow, learns the perimeter between waves, and grows cautious as line weight comes ashore. A given counterattack breaks off at 35 percent to reset for the next; {NPC:opfor-commander} spends the reserve to bleed the beachhead before it can deepen, not to die on it.

forks.name: OPERATION FULL STRAND
forks.trigger: Lodgment held with depth, the line ashore early and intact, the ridge and estuary held throughout.
forks.consequence: The breakout drives inland ahead of schedule and reaches the interior line before the defender has finished wiring it - the next phase opens against incomplete demolition. Your command leads the drive to the passes with the defender on the back foot.

forks.name: OPERATION INLAND
forks.trigger: Beachhead held and the line force ashore; the reserve spent and falling back to the interior line.
forks.consequence: The lodgment becomes a breakout; the reduction drives off the coast toward the fortified pass network the defender has prepared in the interior. Your command moves to force the line.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND SHORE
forks.trigger: The strand lost or the lodgment overrun before the line is ashore - the perimeter pinned against the sea.
forks.consequence: The surviving lodgment is cut off on the crescent with the reserve closing and the tide against it; a relief force must fight in along the coast to extract or reinforce it before it is finished - a relief under the tide, the beachhead recovered rather than won.

storyElementSeed: A crew chief on the strand watches the next DropShip settle through the surf-spray and paints a lane marker by hand in the wet sand, because the tide is coming up and the line still landing has nowhere to go but the few meters he can keep dry and clear.

merc.objectives.primary: The contract pays on a held strand and a landed line - Section 4 measures the lodgment by the tonnage put ashore, not the ground gained. Lose a transport on the beach and the loss comes out of the salvage pool; keep the strand clear and the breakout bonus is depth, banked for the phase that needs it.

is-kurita.objectives.secondary: The reserve will come in disciplined waves because the officer leading it has honour enough to spend his force carefully. Meet it with more. The ridge and the ford are the Dragon's now; a sector that yields them invites the next wave through a door of its own making.

LODGMENT_DEPTH_KM.unit: kilometers of beachhead depth the lodgment can hold

RESERVE_COUNTERATTACKS.unit: timed counterattacks by the mobile reserve before the line is ashore

LANDING_SHIPS.unit: follow-on DropShips still putting the line force ashore

ASHORE_HOURS.unit: hours of holding until enough line weight is ashore to break out

resourceGates.appliesTo: Push to the Coastal Ridge - Buy Depth
resourceGates.lackingText: No established forward base ashore: holding the ridge runs on what the strand can hand-carry up, and the depth you buy is rationed by porter lift - the ridge holds at half the staying power until the beachhead can stand up a supply point.

phases.name: POSTURE - THE STRAND
phases.lead: The hold begins the moment the ramp drops. Before the first counterattack the lodgment learns its own ground - where the ridge gives observation, where the estuary can be forded, how much strand the tide leaves to land on - because the reserve is already forming inland and the ships are already coming down.

dataBlock.Lodgment depth: {LODGMENT_DEPTH_KM} km on a good hour, the sea at the back, no ground to trade
dataBlock.Landing: {LANDING_SHIPS} follow-on DropShips still putting the line ashore; the strand crowds as they unload
dataBlock.Estuary ford: crossable at low water on channels the fishing settlement knows; a wall otherwise
dataBlock.Hold clock: {ASHORE_HOURS} hours until the line weight ashore flips the perimeter to breakout

phases.protocol: Landing control runs the strand by lane and tide: each transport is talked onto a marked lane, and the codeword SLACK on the lodgment net means the low-water window is open and the estuary ford is live - every sector watching the water stands to until SLACK FULL passes and the tide closes it. No fire crosses a marked landing lane; a transport on the strand is louder than any order.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Why a beachhead is a logistics fight wearing a tactical costume - what tonnage has to be ashore before a lodgment can stop defending and start attacking, and why the strand the line lands on is worth more than the ridge that overlooks it.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT - THE COUNTERATTACK
phases.lead: The reserve comes in timed waves at the seam between strand and ridge, learning between each. The perimeter's job is to give no ground it cannot retake and to keep every wave off the beach where the unarmed ships sit.

dataBlock.Wave schedule: {RESERVE_COUNTERATTACKS} counterattacks before the line is ashore, each a fresh slice of the reserve
dataBlock.Axis drift: each wave that gains ground shifts the next toward the proven weak sector
dataBlock.Ford window: low-water crossings open the estuary flank mid-phase - watch it or lose it
dataBlock.No-trade line: any sector pushed to direct-fire range of the strand halts the landing

sidebarKernel.kernel: Holding a line you cannot shorten - why a beachhead fights every wave forward instead of trading space for time, and how to read which counterattack is the main effort and which is shaping the next one.

phases.name: RESOLUTION - THE BREAKOUT
phases.lead: Past the hold deadline the weight ashore tips the balance and the perimeter inverts from cork to fist. What the lodgment held with depth it now breaks out from; what it held by its fingernails it merely survives.

dataBlock.Tip point: T+30:00 - enough line ashore to stop giving ground
dataBlock.Breakout: T+45:00 - the lodgment can transition to the attack inland
dataBlock.Depth dividend: a beachhead held with depth breaks out on schedule; a shallow one starts the next phase behind
dataBlock.Settlement: the fishing settlement's channels and goodwill go to whoever holds the water at the end

sidebarKernel.kernel: Reading the landing curve - how to tell when enough of the line is ashore to switch from holding the strand to driving off it, and why ending the phase with depth is worth more than ending it with a longer casualty list on the enemy's side.

title: OPERATION STONE GATE
inspiration: A high-value world held in depth cannot be taken in one battle; it is reduced in phases - orbit and DropPort, then the coastal beachhead, then the interior line, then the capital - and each phase can fail and force a different next move.
skeleton: breakthrough force must choose which of several mountain passes to force when the defender has wired some to collapse and bluffed others, so the real problem is reading which seam is a trap before committing weight that cannot be recalled, and taking the pass still usable
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} interior, {YEAR}. The beachhead is broken out and the line force is driving inland, and the whole reduction now waits on a wall of rock. The interior of the continent is closed off by a mountain range with only a handful of vehicle-capable passes through it, and {TARGET_FACTION} has fallen back onto that range to make the attacker pay for every meter of altitude. Your command leads the breakthrough. The terrain problem is the passes themselves: {PASS_COUNT} throats through the range, each a switchback climb between rock walls where a heavy 'Mech can be fought from above by a lighter one in cover, and each one a place a few charges can turn a road into a landslide in {COLLAPSE_SECONDS} seconds. {NPC:intel-source} reports a defending force of {DEFENDER_MECHS} 'Mechs holding the range from the high ground. He says {NPC:opfor-commander} has wired {WIRED_PASSES} of the passes to collapse and dressed up the rest to look prepared, with sandbagged emplacements that have no charges behind them and demolition cable strung to nothing. But he cannot say which are which, because the defender did the work at night under his own jamming. That report is 5 days old and rated shaky, so trust none of it too far. That is the entire problem. The weight you commit to a pass cannot be recalled once it is inside. A column caught in a pass when the charges fire is buried, and a pass you bring down to spite the defender is a pass the heavy wave behind you cannot use to reach the capital. The defender would rather lose a road than hand it over usable, which means taking a pass and keeping it usable are opposing goals, raced against a man holding the firing handles.
