The rock walls also blind your sensors: they scatter your scans, leaving you unable to detect anything under 300 meters inside the passes. A force in a pass is half-blind, and the emplacements above it are not. The civilian environment is the high villages - herders and miners who live in the passes, who know exactly which throats the soldiers worked at night and which they only pretended to, and who will trade that knowledge for a guarantee their village is not the one that comes down.

objectives.primary: Force a vehicle-capable pass through the interior range and hold it open and usable for the heavy wave - the breakthrough achieved through a throat the assault can drive, not a buried one.
objectives.secondary: Identify and avoid or neutralize the wired passes before committing the main body; bring no column down inside a collapsing throat.
objectives.bonus: Capture the defender's demolition triggers or charge stocks intact, denying him the ability to wire the next line and proving which passes were real.

complications.name: Wired or Bluffed
complications.text: {WIRED_PASSES} of the {PASS_COUNT} passes will come down on a column; the rest only look like they will. The defender built the bluffs to be convincing and ran the real work in the dark, so the prepared throat and the trap look identical from the approach. Reading wrong costs a column.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each pass carries a hidden flag, wired or bluffed; committing the main body into a wired pass past the point of no recall buries that force, while a bluffed pass can be forced through its emplacements at the normal cost of prepared positions.

complications.name: The Point of No Recall
complications.text: A switchback throat is a place you cannot reverse out of quickly. Once the lead units are deep enough in a pass, a collapse traps them whether the charges were meant for that column or simply fired in panic. Depth in a throat is commitment, and commitment is irreversible.
complications.mechanicalEffect: From T+12:00 any unit that has advanced past a pass's midpoint cannot withdraw before a collapse resolves; a pass fired while units are past the midpoint removes them from the engagement.

complications.name: Fought From Above
complications.text: The emplacements sit on the high ground over each throat, in cover a climbing 'Mech cannot easily answer. A force in the pass is half-blind in the rock-bounce while the guns above it are not. The mountain favours the defender who chose it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Units in a pass have their detection range halved (sensors are blind under 300m in the rock) and take a to-hit penalty firing uphill at dug-in defenders, who fire down with prepared ranges and partial cover.

complications.name: The High Villages Know
complications.text: Herders and miners live in the passes and watched the defender work them at night. They know which throats are wired and which were theatre, and they will tell - but only the village that believes telling will not be the one buried for it. Their knowledge is the best intelligence available and the hardest to earn.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Securing a high village's cooperation before commitment reveals one pass's true flag; a village whose throat is then forced or whose safety is disregarded withdraws all such cooperation for the remainder of the engagement.

decisionPoints.name: Choosing the Seam
decisionPoints.context: {NPC:intel-source} counts {PASS_COUNT} passes and {WIRED_PASSES} wired, but cannot say which. The defender prepared some to bring down and bluffed others to look prepared. The weight you commit cannot be recalled once it is in a throat, and a pass comes down in {COLLAPSE_SECONDS} seconds. You read the seam, or the mountain reads you.

options.title: Force the Pass That Looks Open
advantages: If the read is right, you drive through a throat the defender chose not to wreck and keep it usable
Lighter prepared defence - the open-looking pass shows fewer emplacements
disadvantages: 'Looks open' is exactly what a bluff is built to look like - or what a wired pass looks like with the trigger held
If it is the trap, the column is inside when it comes down
options.consequence: A clean breakthrough if you read true; a buried column if the open road was the one the defender most wanted you to take.

costs.resource: the gamble itself: the open-looking pass is the cheapest one to bluff and the most tempting to wire
costs.risk: a column committed into the wrong open throat is lost whole, and the breakthrough with it

options.title: Force the Pass That Looks Wired
advantages: The defender may have spent his real charges elsewhere and bluffed this one
A prepared throat with no charges behind it can be reduced like any emplaced line
disadvantages: If it is genuinely wired, you assault a kill-throat and lose the pass to collapse anyway
The heaviest prepared fire is here whether the charges are real or not
options.consequence: You eat the prepared fire to call the bluff, and win the pass usable only if there were no charges behind the emplacements.

costs.resource: casualties: assaulting the most prepared throat to prove it hollow
costs.risk: real charges behind real positions is the worst of both - the cost of the assault and the loss of the road

options.title: Split - Probe Two, Commit to One
advantages: Forces the defender to reveal a wired pass by firing it on the probe, or to hold and let the probe through
Commits the main body only once a seam is proven real
disadvantages: A probe heavy enough to draw the trigger is heavy enough to be lost to it
Splitting concedes the defender time to ready a second pass behind the first
options.consequence: You buy certainty with the probing element and the clock, learning which throat is safe before the weight that matters goes in.

costs.resource: the probing element risked to draw a trigger, and the hours the split costs
costs.risk: a defender who holds his charges lets the probe through clean and re-wires the throat behind it for the main body

entries.event: The breakthrough column reaches the pass approaches; the emplacements above the throats open with pre-ranged fire and the defender's demolition element stands to at the triggers.
Lead units commit to a throat; the high villages' cooperation, if earned, has named a pass by now - if not, the read is blind.
The point of no recall - lead units past a pass's midpoint can no longer withdraw before a collapse resolves.
If no usable pass is in hand, {NPC:opfor-commander} begins bringing down the throats the attacker is NOT in, sealing the line behind a single chosen seam.
The interior line is either broken through a usable pass or sealed by collapse, forcing the attack into the broken country off the roads the slow way.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: A usable pass must be in hand by T+20:00, or the defender collapses the alternates and the attack is funneled to a single ruined throat or forced into the trackless high country - the line holds not by combat but by geology, and the capital phase waits on a breakthrough that has not come.

opforSketch.composition: A reinforced 'Mech force holding the pass network - {DEFENDER_MECHS} machines (50-85 tons, a heavy-weighted line) at Veteran quality, fighting from prepared positions on the high ground with pre-ranged fire down each throat, backed by an engineer demolition element holding the collapse triggers. No vehicles - the grades and broken rock above the passes are no place for armour, and the defence is built on 'Mechs that climb and shoot from cover the attacker cannot reach.
opforSketch.behavior: Hold the passes by making them not worth the price, and where a pass cannot be held, bring it down on the column inside it. The line fights to 50 percent before yielding a throat; the demolition element answers only to {NPC:opfor-commander}, who would rather lose a road than hand it over usable and times his collapses to seal the line, not merely to kill.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN GATE
forks.trigger: A pass forced and held intact and usable, the defender's charges spent or captured and the wired throats identified.
forks.consequence: The heavy wave drives through a working pass onto the capital's approaches with momentum the defender cannot reset, his demolition stocks in your hands. Your command leads the final assault still in tempo.

forks.name: OPERATION THROUGH THE LINE
forks.trigger: The line broken and a pass open to the interior, at the ordinary cost of forcing prepared ground.
forks.consequence: The breakthrough reaches the capital's approaches and the final assault begins; the defender falls back on his last fortified ground. Your command drives on the capital.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN COUNTRY
forks.trigger: The passes collapsed, the breakthrough stalled, a column lost in a buried throat.
forks.consequence: The attack cannot force the line on the defender's timetable and goes off the roads into the trackless high country; your command wages interdiction and ambush in the broken interior to bleed the line's supply until it can be turned - the reduction stalled in the mountains but not ended.

storyElementSeed: A scout pilot holds at the mouth of a pass that reads empty, watching the rock above the road for the seams a charge leaves, and waits for the order to go in or pull back, knowing the difference is whether someone fifty kilometers away guessed right about which throat was the bluff.

clan.situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} interior, {YEAR}. The garrison force is broken and flees into the high ground, where it has wired the passes to deny what it cannot hold: a coward's defence, charges in the rock instead of honour in the cockpit. You will force a pass and take it whole, because to bring the mountain down on a road is the act of a beaten dog who has already lost. {NPC:opfor-commander} has prepared {WIRED_PASSES} of {PASS_COUNT} passes to collapse and dressed the others up to deceive. Read the deception, force the real pass, and let the enemy answer for fighting with stone instead of steel.

is-kurita.objectives.primary: Force a pass and keep it open for the Dragon's weight behind you. A throat brought down is a failure even in victory - the officer who buries a road to win it has only done the enemy's demolition for him. Read the seam. Take it whole.

PASS_COUNT.unit: vehicle-capable passes through the interior range

WIRED_PASSES.unit: passes the defender has wired to collapse

COLLAPSE_SECONDS.unit: seconds from trigger to a pass coming down

DEFENDER_MECHS.unit: BattleMechs holding the line from the high ground

phases.name: APPROACH - READING THE LINE
phases.lead: Before a single 'Mech enters a throat the breakthrough reads the wall of rock in front of it. The work is intelligence under fire: which pass is real, which is theatre, and what the high villages will say before the column commits to ground it cannot reverse out of.

dataBlock.Passes: {PASS_COUNT} throats, {WIRED_PASSES} wired - the defender ran the work at night under jamming
dataBlock.Collapse: a wired throat comes down in {COLLAPSE_SECONDS} seconds once triggered
dataBlock.Sensor floor: the rock scatters your scans, blinding you under 300m in the passes; emplacements above see clearly
dataBlock.Village knowledge: the high villages know which passes are real - earned, not taken

routes.name: GATE - THE OPEN THROAT
routes.desc: Force the pass that reads undefended and unwired
routes.tradeoff: Lightest prepared fire if true - but the most tempting throat to wire, and a column inside it when it goes is lost

routes.name: TEETH - THE PREPARED THROAT
routes.desc: Assault the most obviously wired-looking pass on the bet that it is a bluff
routes.tradeoff: Heaviest prepared fire whether bluff or not; usable only if no charges back the emplacements

routes.name: FORK - PROBE AND COMMIT
routes.desc: Push light elements into two throats to draw a trigger before the main body moves
routes.tradeoff: Buys certainty with the probe and the clock; a held charge lets the probe through and re-wires behind it

phases.protocol: The breakthrough runs a throat-state net the same way the descent ran a field-state net: each probing element calls SEAM RED (collapse triggered or imminent), SEAM AMBER (prepared, charges unconfirmed), or SEAM GREEN (forced, usable, charges spent or absent). The main body commits only on GREEN. A village that names a pass is logged by the colour it gives, never by the name of the village - the high country remembers who is recorded talking to soldiers.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Reading a bluff in rock - the signatures a real demolition job leaves that a fake one cannot fake, why the defender ran the work at night, and what a herder who lives in a throat can tell you that no sensor will.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT - THE SEAM
phases.lead: The column commits to a throat and the choice becomes irreversible at the midpoint. The fight is uphill, half-blind, against guns in cover - and the clock is the defender's hand on a firing handle somewhere above.

dataBlock.No-recall point: T+12:00 - past a throat's midpoint there is no withdrawing before a collapse resolves
dataBlock.Uphill fight: detection halved, a to-hit penalty firing up at emplaced defenders in partial cover
dataBlock.Alternate seal: T+20:00 - the defender begins collapsing the throats you are NOT in
dataBlock.Demolition triggers: held by the engineer element, answering only to {NPC:opfor-commander}

sidebarKernel.kernel: What it takes to keep a forced pass usable - clearing emplacements without touching the rock that holds the road up, finding and cutting charge cable under fire, and why a captured trigger stock is worth more than the pass it would have buried.

phases.name: RESOLUTION - THROUGH OR BURIED
phases.lead: The line resolves one of two ways: a throat forced and held open for the weight behind, or the passes down and the attack thrown into the trackless high country. The mountain keeps whatever it takes.

dataBlock.Through: a usable pass in hand by T+20:00 opens the road to the capital's approaches
dataBlock.Sealed: alternates collapsed funnel the attack to a ruined throat or off the roads entirely
dataBlock.Captured stock: the defender's charges and triggers taken deny him the next line and prove the bluffs
dataBlock.Hand-off: a clean gate opens the capital phase in tempo; a stall sends the force to ground in the interior

sidebarKernel.kernel: The breakthrough that buries itself - why a pass brought down in spite is a defeat dressed as a victory, and how to tell when a stalled line should be forced again versus worked around through the broken country.

title: OPERATION COLD CROWN
inspiration: A high-value world held in depth cannot be taken in one battle; it is reduced in phases - orbit and DropPort, then the coastal beachhead, then the interior line, then the capital - and each phase can fail and force a different next move.
skeleton: decapitation assault must take a fortified capital from a defender with nothing left to trade, where the fast route through the inhabited core risks the very prize and the seat of power is either a last stand to storm or a shell the principal already fled
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The defensive line is broken and there is one objective left to take: the capital, designed from the ground up to be the last place on this world to fall. {EMPLOYER}'s campaign to take the planet ends here or not at all. {TARGET_FACTION}'s surviving force has fallen back into the city core around the government quarter - the seat of power, the planetary command, and {NPC:opfor-commander} with whatever he pulled out of the line - and they have nothing left to trade, which makes them the most dangerous defenders of the whole campaign. Your command leads the assault into the core. The terrain problem is the city itself: {CORE_BLOCKS} fortified blocks between the assault line and the government quarter, a dense urban grid of hard cover and ranged avenues where a defender in prepared positions can make every floor a fighting position and every intersection a killing ground. {CIVILIAN_THOUSANDS} thousand civilians are still in the core, sheltering or trapped, which caps the methods available - the fast route through the inhabited blocks is also the route that buries the people you came to govern, and a capital reduced to rubble is a capital not worth the campaign that took it. {NPC:intel-source} reports {DEMO_RING} prepared demolition rings in the core: the bridges over the river that splits the city, the quarter's own approaches, and the quays. They are rigged to drop behind the defender as he falls back, both to slow you and to cover an escape. That report is 3 days old and rated solid but not certain. The question intelligence cannot answer is the one that matters: whether {NPC:opfor-commander} and the planetary leader mean to make their last stand in the government quarter, or whether the quarter is already a shell and the leader is running for the broken country under the cover of the collapsing core. The cornered defender can hold the quarter for perhaps {HOLDOUT_HOURS} hours before the rings are his only remaining move. Storm a shell and you have spent the assault on a symbol; cordon a last stand and you give him the time to bury it. The civilian environment is the population that will live under whoever wins - watching whether the force that takes the capital is one that can be lived with, or one that took the city by taking it apart.

objectives.primary: Take the government quarter and end organized resistance in the capital - the seat of power seized and the planetary command broken, the reduction completed.
objectives.secondary: Take or kill {NPC:opfor-commander} and the planetary leader, or seal every route out so neither can escape into the broken country to rally a holdout.
objectives.bonus: Take the quarter intact enough to govern from - the demolition rings denied, the core left a capital rather than a ruin, the population given a city to be ruled rather than a grave.

complications.name: Nothing Left to Trade
complications.text: A defender with no fallback and no terms is the worst kind. {NPC:opfor-commander}'s force will not break at the usual thresholds - there is nowhere to break to - and will fight from prepared position to prepared position until destroyed or until the rings are the only move left. Expect no surrender that buys you time.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The core defenders ignore standard morale break points and fight to destruction from successive prepared positions; a defender reduced below 25 percent in a block triggers the local demolition ring rather than withdrawing.

complications.name: The Inhabited Core
complications.text: {CIVILIAN_THOUSANDS} thousand civilians remain in the blocks between your line and the quarter. The fast route is the inhabited route, and every method that clears a block faster clears the people in it too. The capital you are trying to win is full of the reason it is worth winning.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Area-effect fire, building demolition, and saturation methods in occupied blocks void the bonus and impose escalating employer-standing and population penalties; the population's cooperation - guides, shelter, intelligence - is available only to a force that takes the core by precision rather than by rubble.

complications.name: The Rings
complications.text: {DEMO_RING} demolition rings are wired across the core - the river bridges, the quarter's approaches, the quays. The defender drops them behind himself to slow you and beneath himself to cover a run. A bridge gone is a route home for your own assault element gone too.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The defender may trigger a demolition ring at any block he yields, collapsing that approach for both sides; a ring dropped behind an advanced friendly element isolates it, and the quarter's own rings fired together both seal the seat of power and open the leader's extraction window.

complications.name: Stand or Shell
complications.text: No analysis can tell you whether the quarter holds the leader or an honour guard left to die for an empty chair. The defender wants you to believe it is a last stand if it is a shell, and a shell if it is a last stand. Being wrong spends the assault on the wrong problem.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The quarter's true state - leader present or already escaping - is set hidden at the start. A force that storms it wrong (assaults a shell or cordons a stand) loses the time either to a wasted assault or to the rings firing, shifting the resolution toward the COMPROMISED fork.

decisionPoints.name: Into the Core
decisionPoints.context: {CORE_BLOCKS} fortified blocks, {CIVILIAN_THOUSANDS} thousand people in them, and {DEMO_RING} rings wired to drop the approaches. How you cross the core decides the cost in blocks, in time, and in the population you mean to govern when it is over.

options.title: Drive the Main Avenues - Speed
advantages: Fastest route to the quarter before the defender can extract the leader or fire the core rings
Armour can be brought to bear on the broad approaches
disadvantages: The avenues are the defender's pre-ranged killing ground
The demolition rings are wired to drop on the avenues first
options.consequence: You reach the quarter fast if the avenues hold, straight into the prepared defence and the falling bridges - and the inhabited blocks along the way pay for the speed.

costs.resource: the avenues are the ranged ground and the wired ground at once
costs.risk: a ring dropped on an avenue mid-drive buries the assault's own spearhead

options.title: Work the Side Blocks - Method
advantages: Avoids the pre-ranged avenues and the obvious ring triggers
Takes the core in order, block by block, with less collateral
disadvantages: Slow - every floor a position, every block a fight
Gives the defender time to extract the leader and fire the rings at leisure
options.consequence: Lower immediate cost and a city left more intact, but the seat of power may be empty by the time you reach it.

costs.resource: time: a block-by-block reduction is hours the defender spends extracting
costs.risk: method buys the city and may lose the leader - an intact, empty quarter taken too late

options.title: Seize the Quarter's Approaches First - Guile
advantages: Take the bridges and chokepoints the rings are wired to before the defender can drop them
Holding the approaches denies him both the collapse and the clean extraction
disadvantages: Those approaches are where the defender's strength and his hair-triggered rings are concentrated
A small force racing ahead to the chokepoints is exposed and alone
options.consequence: A decisive lock on the quarter if it works - the defender cannot collapse the core behind himself or run - and a force shattered on the prepared chokepoints if the rings fire first.

costs.resource: engineering and risk: racing the demolition rings to the chokepoints with a forward element
costs.risk: a hair-triggered ring on a held bridge buries your own approach force and the lock with it

decisionPoints.name: The Seat of Power
decisionPoints.context: The assault reaches the government quarter and the unanswerable question demands an answer. Intelligence still cannot say whether the leader is behind the walls or already gone, and being wrong either way costs the campaign its point.

options.title: Storm It - Assume a Last Stand
advantages: If the leader is there, a decisive storm ends the war at its root
Denies a genuine last-stand defender the time to fire the quarter's rings
disadvantages: If it is a shell, you spend the assault force storming an empty fortress
A stormed quarter is the most likely to be wrecked in the taking
options.consequence: Decapitation if the leader is there; a costly assault on a symbol while the leader runs if he is not.

costs.resource: the assault force committed to the storm whether the chair is full or empty
costs.risk: an empty quarter stormed is the assault spent for a flag while the war's object slips the cordon you did not set

options.title: Cordon and Search - Assume a Shell
advantages: If the leader already fled, the cordon catches the extraction; if he is there, it holds him
Methodical clearance spares the quarter and the people in it
disadvantages: A cordon gives a genuine last-stand defender time to fire the quarter's rings under your encirclement
Slower - the search is hours the defender may not give you
options.consequence: You trade the storm's speed for certainty, at the risk of the rings going off around the cordon and burying the prize.

costs.resource: time: a cordon is the hours a last-ditch defender uses to arm and fire the core rings
costs.risk: the rings fired under a cordon bury the quarter and your encircling force around it

options.title: Cut the Extraction Routes First
advantages: Whether last stand or flight, the leader cannot leave
The quarter resolves itself once it can be neither relieved nor fled
disadvantages: Cedes the quarter and the symbol for the duration
The defender holds the seat of power on every screen while you hold the roads
options.consequence: You win the war's actual object - the leader - and lose the optics of the seat until last, the capital's flag flying over a fortress that can no longer matter.

costs.resource: the seat of power left flying the defender's flag while you hold the exits
costs.risk: a population that sees the old flag still over the quarter wavers on which side has actually won

entries.event: The assault enters the capital core; the defender opens from prepared blocks and drops the first demolition ring to shape the fight.
The defender begins the timed collapse of approaches behind his fallback line, trading blocks for the quarter and channeling the assault.
The core rings on the government quarter's own approaches are armed; from here the quarter can be sealed or buried on {NPC:opfor-commander}'s command.
The cornered defender's hold reaches its limit - {HOLDOUT_HOURS} hours in, {NPC:opfor-commander} either makes his stand final or fires the rings and runs.
The leader's escape window closes; after this he is taken in the quarter or already gone to the broken country.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The government quarter's approaches must be locked by T+40:00, or {NPC:opfor-commander} fires the core rings and uses the collapse to extract the leader - the capital falls as a ruin with the war's object gone, and a clean victory becomes a COMPROMISED one chasing a man into the hills.

opforSketch.composition: A cornered defence fighting from a fortified capital core: 1-2 'Mech lances (mixed 40-80 tons, whatever survived the line) at Regular-to-Veteran quality fighting from hard cover, stiffened by dug-in tracked armour and turret emplacements in the government quarter (Demolisher/Po behaviour) and a mechanized infantry garrison contesting every block. Aerospace spent. {DEMO_RING} prepared demolition rings wired through the core - bridges, quays, the quarter's approaches.
opforSketch.behavior: A last-ditch, nothing-to-trade defence: trades the city block by block, collapses approaches behind itself, and will bury the government quarter rather than surrender it intact. No standard break threshold - the defence fights from prepared position to prepared position until destroyed, or until {NPC:opfor-commander} triggers the core rings and tries to extract the leader in the confusion.

forks.name: OPERATION COLD CROWN
forks.trigger: The quarter taken intact and the leader captured or killed in it, the demolition rings denied and the capital largely standing.
forks.consequence: The world is reduced and yours to hold. Your command transitions from the assault to consolidating the taken capital and governing a sullen, intact population - the reduction complete, the campaign won where it was meant to be won.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY THRONE
forks.trigger: The capital taken but the leader extracted ahead of the cordon, or the quarter buried by its own rings and the core left in ruins.
forks.consequence: The seat of power is yours and hollow - the leader is loose in the broken country rallying a holdout resistance, and the capital you hold is a wreck that proves nothing. Your command must run the leader down before the reduction unravels from the hills.

forks.name: OPERATION LAST RELIEF
forks.trigger: The assault stalled in the core, the lead force cut off among the blocks with its approaches collapsed behind it.
forks.consequence: The assault force is pinned in the burning capital with its routes home dropped behind it and the cornered defender closing; a relief column must fight in through the core to break it out before it is finished - the reduction's last gamble, recovered street by street.

storyElementSeed: A rifleman in a stairwell three blocks from the government quarter shares a ration tin with a family that would not leave, listens to the bridges going down one at a time across the river, and counts them, because each one is a road home that will not be there when the order comes to fall back.

is-kurita.objectives.bonus: Take the seat whole. A capital broken to win it is a victory that shames the hand that took it - the Coordinator is given cities to rule, not rubble to mourn. The officer who storms the quarter into ruin has handed the enemy his last demolition for free.

merc.objectives.primary: The contract's completion clause pays on the government quarter taken and organized resistance ended - Section 12 holds the final tranche against the leader's capture or confirmed death, and the demolition of the core voids the intact-capital bonus entirely. Read which fight pays before you commit to the avenues.

phases.name: INGRESS - THE CORE
phases.lead: The assault enters a city built to be the last thing to fall, full of the people it was built to shelter. The first work is reading the core - which avenues are ranged, which bridges are rings, where the defender means to make you fight - before committing armour to streets that can drop out from under it.

dataBlock.Population: {CIVILIAN_THOUSANDS} thousand civilians in the core - the methods cap is the people

routes.name: AVENUE - THE MAIN APPROACHES
routes.desc: Drive the broad avenues straight for the quarter
routes.tradeoff: Fastest and armour-capable; the pre-ranged killing ground and where the rings drop first

routes.name: WARREN - THE SIDE BLOCKS
routes.desc: Grind through the residential blocks off the main axes
routes.tradeoff: Less collateral and off the obvious triggers; slow enough to let the leader extract

routes.name: LOCK - THE QUARTER APPROACHES
routes.desc: Race a forward element to seize the wired bridges and chokepoints first
routes.tradeoff: Locks the quarter if it works; the forward element dies on the chokepoints if the rings fire first

phases.protocol: The assault runs the core on a strict fire-discipline net: codeword GLASS HOUSE means an occupied block - precision methods only, no area fire, no demolition, the population is in the building. RING DOWN reports a fired demolition ring and the approach it closed, so no element advances onto a route that is no longer there. A held bridge is reported and guarded by name; a bridge is a road home, and the net counts them aloud as they survive or fall.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Reading whether a fortified quarter holds a man or a symbol - the signatures of a genuine last stand versus a covering honour guard, and why the defender spends as much effort selling you the wrong answer as defending the right one.

phases.name: GROUND - THE QUARTER
phases.lead: The fight closes on the government quarter and the central question forces itself: stand or shell, storm or cordon or cut the roads. Every choice spends a resource the campaign needs - time, the assault force, or the prize itself.

dataBlock.Quarter state: leader present or already escaping - set hidden, learned only by committing
dataBlock.Ring window: core rings armed from T+20:00, fired on {NPC:opfor-commander}'s command
dataBlock.Extraction: the leader's window closes at T+50:00 - taken in the quarter or gone to the hills
dataBlock.No-break defender: the core fights to destruction; a block reduced below 25 percent fires its ring

sidebarKernel.kernel: The decapitation gamble - why cutting the roads out can matter more than holding the throne room, and how to weigh taking the seat of power against taking the man who sits in it when you cannot do both in time.

phases.name: RESOLUTION - THE CROWN
phases.lead: The capital falls one of three ways: taken whole with the leader in hand, taken hollow with him loose in the hills, or stalled with the assault pinned among the burning blocks. The population watches which it was.

dataBlock.Whole: quarter intact, leader taken, rings denied - a capital to govern from
dataBlock.Hollow: the seat taken but the leader extracted or the core buried - a wreck that proves nothing
dataBlock.Stalled: the assault cut off in the core, approaches dropped behind it, waiting on relief
dataBlock.The watchers: the population reads whether the city was taken or taken apart, and remembers

sidebarKernel.kernel: The cost of a city fight that is not on any contract ledger - what the aid stations and the population carry out of a capital taken block by block, and why the way the last phase is won decides whether the world is held or merely occupied.
